* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of Allah mighty and majestic with this perfect attribute, namely the judgment of truth, and that He does nothing in vain or idly, but everything He decrees is truth.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the denunciation of idol-worshippers, since they worshipped with Allah one who is nothing in relation to Allah mighty and majestic, by His saying ﴿those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that these idols do not benefit their worshippers at all, by His saying ﴿do not judge anything﴾, and "shay'" (anything) is indefinite in a negative context, so it encompasses everything.

If someone says: among the people who invoke a god besides Allah are those whom, when they call upon these idols, the idols answer them; when they call upon them to remove harm, the harm is removed from them; and among people are those who, when they oppose these idols, are afflicted with a trial. So what is the answer?

The answer is to say: what occurs, occurs from Allah mighty and majestic, not from these idols, as a trial and a test. And it is said regarding it: it happened at that time, not by it. That is, this judgment came from Allah mighty and majestic at the time of invoking these idols, not by the invocation of these idols.

If someone says: why do you turn away from the apparent cause to another cause that is not known?

We say: we turned to that because of the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything﴾, and by His saying: ﴿If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you; and on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association. And none can inform you like one who is all-aware﴾ [Fatir 14], and by His saying: ﴿And who is more astray than one who invokes other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication? (5) And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5-6].

Otherwise, the common person may go to the owner of a grave and say: "O my master, O friend of Allah, O my lord, rescue me from this calamity, rescue me from this distress." Then he goes home and finds the matter has been relieved. In any case, he will attribute this relief to the apparent cause he performed, namely invoking this grave, until the distress was lifted from him.

We say: this is a trial, and we know with certainty that he, that is the owner of the grave, is not the one who removed the harm; rather, it was Allah mighty and majestic who removed it, but the removal occurred at the invocation of the owner of the grave, not by his invocation.

Pay attention to this, for the people of graves constantly raise this doubt against us. They say: "I invoked so-and-so, and he responded to me, and the distress was lifted." And one of us came from Makkah to Madinah a long time ago. When we approached Madinah, they began to invoke, and to invoke the Messenger. I said, "Fear Allah, O people," and at that time the person was still young and not yet grown: "Fear Allah, invoke Allah." They said: "No, this is our master, one of the people whose belly was split open and whose intestines hung out, and the earth became too narrow for him. They said: go to the Prophet of Allah." So he went, and when he approached Madinah he invoked Allah, and the intestines went back in and the belly closed.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, he invoked the Prophet. When he approached Madinah, he invoked the Prophet, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, rescue me," the belly was split and the intestines hanging out, so the intestines went back into the belly and the belly closed.

First, as to this story: whoever says it is true. Then, supposing it has become true, did this happen by the invocation of the Messenger? Never; this did not happen. The Messenger does not possess this at all. During his life, Allah may show them a sign of the Messenger's, and such a thing happens, as happened to the eye of Abu Qatada, which was injured and hung out until it lay on his cheek; the Prophet, peace be upon him, put it back in its place and it healed immediately [narrated by Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad (1549) and in al-Mafarid (61), al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (19/8) (12), and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (1043, 1184), from the hadith of Qatada ibn al-Nu'man]. This is a sign of Allah, but it occurred during his life; after his death, no.

The point is that Allah the Exalted may make healing follow the invocation of the owner of a grave as a trial and a test, so a person believes by the senses and disbelieves the Shari'a. He believes by the senses, building this matter on the apparent thing, and disbelieves the Shari'a.

If someone says: are there parallels to this? We say: yes. Allah may test a person by facilitating the means of disobedience, as a trial to know who fears Him in the unseen, as He tested the Children of Israel with the fish. Allah forbade them to hunt fish on the Sabbath and tested them: on the Sabbath the fish would come upon the water in abundance, and on other days they did not come. A long time passed, and they said: "We must catch these fish, but the Sabbath is forbidden to us. What shall we do?" He said: there is a stratagem—and the Jews are people of stratagems: place a net on Friday, the fish will enter on Saturday, and take the fish on Sunday, and say to Allah: "We did not hunt on the Sabbath." So what were they treated with? ﴿And you certainly knew those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath, so We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾ [al-Baqarah 65]. Allah the Exalted turned them into something resembling a human but not a human, as they did something resembling lawfulness but not lawful—a recompense in kind.

This nation: Allah forbade hunting while in the state of ihram, and Allah tested them. The game began to come in abundance: flying game could be reached by the spear, and creeping game by the hand. ﴿O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach, that Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94]. So the flying game came to be reached by a person with his spear, though flying game is ordinarily reached only with an arrow, and creeping game by the hand. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, avoided this: they did not catch with the hand, nor hunt with the spear.

So beware, O Muslim, lest you be deceived when the means of disobedience are made easy for you. Allah may test you. Perhaps Allah tests a person with a position in which he could steal from the public treasury, either by outright theft, taking dirhams, or indirect theft, such as arriving late to work or leaving early. For whoever does that is a thief. If we suppose he is late by a sixth, or leaves early by a sixth, how much has he stolen from his salary? He has stolen a sixth, because if he is late by a sixth he deserves only five-sixths of the salary, and the rest he takes without right. He is content, because no one is above him—he is the manager, for example—or he is content because his manager is also late, and it is known that when a manager is late and those under him are late, he says nothing to them, for if he said something to them he would expose himself.

So beware of being deceived when Allah makes the means of disobedience easy for you; for Allah knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. Do not be deceived by this matter.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a sharp rebuke of the foolishness of those people who worship besides Allah—from where do they take this? In that they turned away from worshipping the One who judges with truth to worshipping one who judges nothing, and this is the utmost foolishness.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names: al-Samī' (the Hearing) and al-Baṣīr (the Seeing).

And the affirmation of what they indicate of attributes, and the affirmation of what they indicate of effect or of ruling.

This is because faith in Allah's names is not complete except by believing in three matters, if they are transitive: first, affirming the name; second, affirming the attribute it indicates; third, affirming the effect or ruling it indicates. This is if it is transitive.

But if it is intransitive, faith in it is complete only by two matters: affirming the name, and affirming the attribute it indicates.

Is al-Samī' intransitive or transitive?

* Students: Intransitive.

* Other students: Transitive.

* Shaykh: How intransitive, transitive? Then we move to the third category: neither intransitive nor transitive.

Is it intransitive or transitive?

* Students: Transitive.

* Shaykh: Transitive. ﴿Allah has certainly heard the saying of﴾ and ﴿Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾ [al-Mujadila 1]: transitive. So you must believe in al-Samī' as a name of Allah.

And has anyone denied the names? Yes: among the Mu'attila who claim to belong to the Islamic community are those who deny Allah's names.

And you must believe in the attribute it indicates, which is hearing. Allah is not Hearing without hearing; rather, He is Hearing with hearing.

Has anyone affirmed the name without the attribute? Yes: the Mu'tazila. Their principle is to affirm the names and deny the attributes indicated by these names.

They say: Allah is Hearing without hearing, Seeing without sight. Glory be to Allah! How is He Seeing without sight? He says: Yes, Seeing without sight, because if you affirm sight, then sight is an attribute added to the essence, or not? The attribute is other than the qualified. If you say it is eternal, you affirm a plurality of eternals, and become more disbelieving than the Christians. How many did the Christians affirm? Three gods. You now want to affirm fifty gods or more, according to the number of names for which you affirm an attribute, and this is disbelief. If we declare the Christian disbeliever for three and say: he is a disbeliever, we say: you are a disbeliever, a disbeliever, a disbeliever; multiply three by... until you reach the names. You are more disbelieving than the Christians if you affirm an eternal attribute.

If I assert that it is created (ḥādith), then it follows that created events subsist in Allah. But created events cannot subsist except in something created, so you would be establishing that Allah is created and that He is originated.

What about when this statement is phrased in words more eloquent and more forceful than mine? Would the ignorant not be deceived by it? Undoubtedly they would be deceived by it.

But we say: Allah, exalted is He, is All-Hearing (samī') with a hearing (sam'), and it is not conceivable that a derived name (mushtaqq) exists without that from which it is derived, never. For it is not correct to say of the deaf that he is "All-Hearing," nor of the blind that he is "All-Seeing." It is impossible for a derived name in all the languages of the world to exist without its root from which it is derived preceding it.

As for your statement that the attribute is other than the one described, we say: Allah, exalted is He, has never ceased and will never cease to be with His attributes, and there is absolutely no existing essence without an attribute. Whoever claims that there exists an essence without an attribute has claimed the impossible. Nothing that exists is without an attribute. Even if the only attributes it has were the attribute of existence, of self-subsistence, and the like, still everything described has an attribute. However, the one described by his attributes is not something separate from him. Therefore we do not say, "The attributes of Allah are Allah," nor do we say, "They are other than Allah." Rather we say, "Allah with His attributes." Because if you say, "The attributes are Allah," the meaning becomes that He has no attribute. And if you say, "They are other than Him," you have separated the attribute from the one described, and this is impossible.

So, belief in a name requires that you believe in what it contains of an attribute. Its containing of the attribute may be by inclusion (taḍammun), and it may be by necessary implication (iltizām). So do we believe in the attribute that the name indicates by inclusion only, or by inclusion and necessary implication? Do you not know what the meaning is? By inclusion and by necessary implication.

For example: "the Creator" (al-Khāliq) is a name that indicates the attribute of creating by inclusion. Its indication of knowledge is by necessary implication, because there is no creating except with knowledge. Its indication of power is also by necessary implication, because there is no creating except with power.

So you believe in what the name indicates of an attribute, whether that is by inclusion or by necessary implication.

The third condition: if the name is transitive (muta'addiyan), the third matter is the effect or the judgment (ḥukm). For example, "the All-Hearing" is one possessing hearing which hears. You must believe in a hearing that extends to others, so that He hears every speech. "The All-Seeing" is likewise transitive. We believe in "the All-Seeing" as a name, in "sight" as an attribute, and that He sees, as a judgment or an effect.

But if the name is intransitive (lāzim), then one believes in two matters: the first is the name, and the second is the attribute.

Is "the Living" (al-Ḥayy) intransitive or transitive?
* Student: Intransitive.
* Shaykh: How? Is not Allah giving life (yuḥyī)?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: "Yuḥyī" is not from "al-Ḥayy"; it is from "al-Muḥyī." "Al-Ḥayy" is an intransitive description, or "life" is an intransitive attribute that does not extend to anyone other than Allah.

So "al-Ḥayy" is therefore one of the intransitive names. You believe in "al-Ḥayy" as one of Allah's names, and you believe in the attribute indicated by "al-Ḥayy," which is life.

... Because there is no creating except with power. Good. So you believe in what the name indicates of an attribute, whether by inclusion or by necessary implication.

The third matter: if the name is transitive, the effect or the judgment. For example, the All-Hearing, who possesses hearing that hears, you must believe in a hearing that extends to others, so that He hears every speech. The All-Seeing, likewise transitive: we believe in "the All-Seeing" as a name, in "sight" as an attribute, and that He sees as a judgment or an effect.

But if the name is intransitive, one believes in two matters: the first, the name, and the second, the attribute. Is "al-Ḥayy" intransitive or transitive?
* Students: Intransitive.
* Shaykh: How? Is it not Allah who gives life?
* Students: Yuḥyī.
* Shaykh: "Yuḥyī" is not from "al-Ḥayy"; it is from "al-Muḥyī." "Al-Ḥayy" is an intransitive description, or "life" is an intransitive attribute that does not extend to anyone other than Allah. So "al-Ḥayy" is one of the intransitive names. You believe in "al-Ḥayy" as one of Allah's names, and you believe in the attribute indicated by "al-Ḥayy," which is life.

Thus, if we hold to this, we oppose all the people of ta'ṭīl (the denial of Allah's names and attributes). We oppose those who do not name Allah with any name nor describe Him with any attribute, and these are the extreme Jahmiyyah (followers of Jahm ibn Ṣafwān). We oppose those who believe that Allah has names but has no attributes, like the Mu'tazilah. And we oppose those who say: He has names and attributes, but they have no judgment, they do not extend, because if they extended to others, it would necessitate the subsistence of created events in Him. For what is heard is created, or is it eternal? It is created. So when hearing is connected to a created thing, the hearing becomes created in the same way as the thing heard, and so created events would subsist in Him. Therefore say: He is All-Hearing, He has hearing, but He does not hear by it, lest created events subsist in Him. So when we come to these three conditions: (1) belief in the name; (2) what it includes of an attribute; (3) the effect or judgment, our belief in the names is sound.

As for "the All-Hearing" and "the All-Seeing," we have already explained their meanings, and we mentioned that "the All-Hearing" indicates hearing, and that the hearing of Allah, exalted is He, is of two kinds: hearing in the sense of responding, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is All-Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrāhīm 39]. Does hearing come in the sense of responding in the Arabic language?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The evidence?
* Student: He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And if they had heard, they would not have responded to you﴾ [Fāṭir 14].
* Shaykh: ﴿And if they had heard, they would not have responded to you.﴾ But is there any evidence in that?
* Student: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾.
Yes, ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfāl 21], meaning: they do not respond. And from it is the saying of the one praying, and you, every day, pray at least seventeen rak'ahs and say: "Allah hears whoever praises Him" (sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah). What does it mean? It means "He responds." It does not mean merely hearing the one who praises, because that would not benefit anything. Rather its meaning is "He responded." This is hearing in the sense of responding.

The second kind: hearing in the sense of perceiving what is heard (idrāk al-masmū'). This divides into three categories. The first is what is meant as a threat (tahdīd). The second is what is meant as support (ta'yīd). The third is what is meant to show the comprehensiveness of Allah's hearing, that is, the hearing of encompassing knowledge (samā' al-iḥāṭah).

An example of the first, which is meant as a threat: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation? Yes, and Our messengers with them are recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80]. This is for a threat; that is why He said: ﴿Yes, and Our messengers with them are recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80].

An example of hearing meant as support is His saying to Mūsā and Hārūn: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 46].

An example of what is meant to show encompassing hearing is His saying: ﴿Allah has already heard the statement of she who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾ [al-Mujādilah 1]. So hearing is first divided into two: hearing of response and hearing of perception. Perception is three categories, or if you wish, say: three kinds, so that the categories do not overlap: hearing that entails a threat, hearing that entails support, and hearing that shows encompassment. All of this is established for Allah, mighty and majestic.

If a questioner says: What determines that this hearing is for support, or for threat, or for encompassment?

We say: the context of the speech and the indications of the circumstances. Therefore it can be said of Allah's saying to Mūsā and Hārūn: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 46], that this hearing is for support and for threat, support of whom?
* Students: Mūsā.
* Shaykh: And a threat to Pharaoh. But what prevents saying that it is a threat to Pharaoh is that Pharaoh was not hearing these words from Allah. So how is one threatened who does not hear the threat? Therefore the scholars said: the hearing in this verse is for support. I have not seen them say that it is for threat, nor for the threat to Pharaoh. The reason is that Pharaoh now is not hearing what Allah, mighty and majestic, says. So how is one threatened who does not hear the threat?!

As for "the All-Seeing" (al-Baṣīr), it means the one possessing piercing sight, from whose gaze nothing is absent, mighty and majestic. Whatever movement or whatever action, Allah, exalted is He, sees it. Good. If He sees everything, what is our position regarding His saying (ﷺ): "Three whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify" — and He said, "nor look at them," so He negated looking at them?

We say: the affirmed look is not the negated look. The negated is the look of mercy, and the affirmed is the look of encompassment. Allah, exalted is He, looks at everything with a look of encompassment; even those upon whom is wrath are seen before Allah, mighty and majestic, but with a look of encompassment. As for what is negated, it is the look of mercy: "He will not look at them." By this the evidences harmonize, and it becomes clear that there is no contradiction between them. There is "al-Baṣīr" in the sense of knowledge, but what comes to mind from it is sight, as has already been explained.

* Student: What happens to the worshippers of graves of trial and testing? If we tell them that Allah, mighty and majestic, says such and such, they are not convinced. The believer in the Qur'an who accepts it is convinced by the verses, but these are not convinced by the Qur'an.
* Shaykh: May Allah bless you. Most of the people of graves are Muslims; that is, they see themselves as being upon Islam and believe in the Qur'an.
* Student: Is there a stronger proof, O Shaykh, (...)? The auditory (sam'iyyah) proof is a theoretical argument for debating them. Is there not another proof?
* Shaykh: It is possible, by way of challenge, that a person challenges them with something that would anger their gods, which he does, and nothing happens. This may be part of the challenge.
* Student: Regarding "the All-Hearing": is it an attribute of essence or an attribute of action?
* Shaykh: "The All-Hearing" is an attribute of essence. But what makes the thing heard exist is an attribute of action. As for hearing, Allah has never ceased and will never cease to be All-Hearing; it is not connected to His will. If you want to know the difference: if it were possible for Allah to be free of this attribute, it would be an attribute of action; if it is not possible, it is an attribute of essence. And it is known that it is impossible for Allah, mighty and majestic, to be free of the attribute of hearing so that He would be deaf, for Allah is exalted above that. But what occurs is the thing heard.
* Student: Is the look of mercy the same as the mercy of Allah, mighty and majestic? I mean, what is meant by ...?
* Shaykh: What is meant is that Allah looks at him with a look by which He shows him mercy. It is not the same as mercy itself. This is why you now distinguish between looking at your child who pleases you and looking at your child who angers you. When you look at the child who pleases you, you look at him with a cool look, while he feels that your eye has been delighted by him. "Delighted" (qarrat) comes from "qarr," which is coolness, and therefore "Allah cool your eye" (aqarra Allāhu 'aynak) means He made it cool. What is the meaning of "qarrahā"? He calmed it so that it does not move. Good. The child with whom you are angry: when you look at him, how is your eye? Hot and red, with sparks coming from it, almost blinding the child. Is that not so?
* Student: May Allah be good to you. In His saying: ﴿And those who call upon other than Him﴾ [Ghāfir 20], the author applied it to (...), and it has also passed us that the polytheists, the author always applies it to the people of Makkah, perhaps because the surah was revealed in Makkah, so perhaps the author applied it to this. What do you say about this?
* Shaykh: No, this is not correct. What matters is the generality of the wording, not the specific cause (sabab). He has a view, and a stronger view than this is His saying after this verse: ﴿Have they not traveled in the land and seen?﴾ [Ghāfir 21]. But we say: what matters is the generality of the wording, and the cause does not specify the general, and if a ruling is mentioned that relates to some individuals of the general, that does not require restricting it either, as is the established principle.
* Student: The expression, for example, if we say: "This deed is closer to the look of Allah's mercy"?
* Shaykh: It is not correct to say "closer to the look of Allah's mercy." Mercy is not looked at. Say "closer to the mercy of Allah."
* Student: Interpreting "those called upon" as idols excludes the rabbis and monks and others. Is there not a deficiency in this?
* Shaykh: What do you say about this question? Yes, there is no doubt that worship of rabbis and monks in the sense that the Messenger (ﷺ) explained is not like the worship of idols, because the worship of idols is worship of approach and submission, while the worship of rabbis and monks is worship of following. And there is no doubt that it is worship, as came in the hadith: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary; and they were not commanded except to worship one God﴾ [al-Tawbah 31]. So if the worship of rabbis and monks is like the worship of the Messiah son of Mary, it follows that they worship them with the worship of approach. But the Messenger (ﷺ) said to 'Adī ibn Ḥātim: "Do they not make lawful what Allah has made unlawful, and you make it lawful, and make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and you make it unlawful?" He said: Yes. He said: "That is their worship." This is worship of following, while most of the worship of the polytheists is worship of approach and exaltation.

[Footnote: Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (218) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Kubrā (20350) with their chains from 'Adī ibn Ḥātim (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a golden cross around my neck. He said: "O 'Adī, throw this idol away from your neck." So I threw it away, and I came to him while he was reciting Sūrat Barā'ah. He recited this verse: ﴿They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 31] until he finished it. I said: We do not worship them. He said: "Do they not forbid what Allah has permitted and you forbid it, and permit what Allah has forbidden and you permit it?" I said: Yes. He said: "That is their worship."]

* Student: Does His saying: ﴿Indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ not include the hearing of encompassment (...)?
* Shaykh: The hearing here is hearing of encompassment, but what is intended by it is victory and support, because mere encompassment, even Pharaoh is heard by Allah, mighty and majestic.
* Student: What are the best books (...) on the names and attributes?
* Shaykh: By Allah, the books are many and differ in method. For example, for mere affirmation, establishing the creed, the best is al-'Aqīdah al-Wāsiṭiyyah, because it is all built on verses and hadiths. For the aspect of debate and argument, the best I have seen is al-Ṣawā'iq al-Mursalah by Ibn al-Qayyim, and its abridgment. This is among the best for the student of knowledge in debate. Al-Ṣawā'iq al-Mursalah 'alā al-Jahmiyyah wa al-Mu'aṭṭilah (The Dispatched Thunderbolts Against the Jahmiyyah and the Denialists), and its abridgment is also beneficial, because he, may Allah have mercy on him, mentions the principal issues in which there is disagreement, then debates these people or argues with the more correct view. It is not a mere discussion; he argues with them until the truth becomes clear.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By Allah, I have forgotten the one it belongs to.
* Student: al-Mawṣilī.
* Shaykh: Al-Mawṣilī, what is his name?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Just al-Mawṣilī? In any case, the abridgment is known by this name: Mukhtaṣar al-Ṣawā'iq al-Mursalah.
* Student: Is it permissible to classify shirk, for example the verse: ﴿They took their rabbis and monks as lords﴾? Meaning this is the shirk of obedience and the shirk of following?
* Shaykh: Yes, it is the shirk of following and the shirk of obedience, but that is shirk of worship. This is why among the best definitions of ṭāghūt is what Ibn al-Qayyim said: whatever a servant transgresses his limit with, of a deity worshipped, or a leader followed, or an authority obeyed. The worshipped are idols, the followed are scholars, and the obeyed are rulers. This is the best that is said in defining ṭāghūt. But this is considering the transgressor. As for considering the worshipped, the followed, or the obeyed, these are not ṭawāghīt in terms of their own essences, because the scholar may not be pleased with this matter, and the ruler likewise, and the worshipped likewise. But in terms of the actor, they are ṭawāghīt, because he has transgressed concerning them; they are the place of his transgression, and they are not themselves transgressing. So 'Īsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, is worshipped. Do we say he is a ṭāghūt? No, but he is the place of transgression of those who worshipped him. Pay attention to this point, because some people raised an objection to Ibn al-Qayyim's words and said: How does he say this? So is 'Īsā a ṭāghūt because he is worshipped? It is said: his intention, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the place of transgression is in the worshipped, the followed, and the obeyed.
* Student: What is the difference between a transitive verb and an intransitive verb?
* Shaykh: The intransitive is what does not govern a direct object, and the transitive is what governs a direct object. Does "sami'a" (to hear) govern a direct object or not? Living? Great (ʿaẓuma)? Can you make "ʿaẓuma" act on something? "ʿAẓuma" is itself; but "ʿaẓẓama" (to magnify) is correctly transitive, while "ʿaẓuma" is undoubtedly intransitive. "Jalla"? Intransitive. So "al-ʿAẓīm" (the Mighty) is one of Allah's intransitive names, "al-ʿAlī" (the Most High) is one of Allah's intransitive names, and "al-Ajall" or "al-Jalīl" (the Majestic) is one of Allah's intransitive names.
* Student: (...) ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. How (...) our master Jesus and other righteous people?
* Shaykh: Do you memorize the Qur'an?
* Student: I have not memorized it.

The Shaykh: Good. "Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be its certain entrants. Had these been gods, they would not have entered it, and all will abide therein forever. For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear. Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it" [al-Anbiya 98–101] [al-Anbiya: ]. And 'Isa is among those for whom the best reward has preceded, do you understand? For this reason the disbelievers cited 'Isa as an example, and when the verse "Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell" was revealed, they said: "Then 'Isa is in the Fire as well, by way of dispute." So Allah the Exalted revealed: "Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it." It is like His saying: "Are our gods better, or he?" Allah the Exalted said: "They did not cite it to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people" [al-Zukhruf 58]. And the most hated of men to Allah is the most quarrelsome adversary.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah. (21) That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, severe in punishment. (22) And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority (23) to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, but they said, "A sorcerer, a liar." (24) So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women. But the scheming of the disbelievers is nothing but in error."﴾ [Ghafir 21–25].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them?﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾. This construction occurs frequently in the Qur'an: the interrogative particle is followed by a conjunction and then the clause. The grammarians (al-mu'ribun) differed over how to analyse this structure (i'rab, grammatical analysis).

Some of them said: the underlying sense is *wa-alam yasiru* ("and have they not travelled"), so the wa is conjunctive to what precedes, and the hamza (interrogative) enters upon its clause, the clause being introduced by it. This view requires no supposed omission, but it faces the objection that the hamza precedes the conjunction. They answered this by saying that placing the hamza first is permissible in such cases.

The second view of the grammarians is that the hamza enters upon something omitted (muqaddar), and the conjunction is conjunctive to that omitted element. In that case we need to specify what is omitted, and only the context can specify it. So the omitted element is supplied according to what the context requires. For example, one may say: *a-fa-raṭū wa-lam yasiru fi al-ard* ("have they then been negligent and not travelled in the land?"), or *aghfalū wa-lam yasiru fi al-ard* ("have they been heedless and not travelled in the land?"), or anything that conveys this meaning.

As for His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾: is the intended meaning the travelling of the hearts, through reflection, contemplation and pondering, or the travelling of feet, until a person comes to know, with his own eyes, what happened to the earlier nations? Both are intended. Whoever cannot travel with his feet should travel with his heart. But what is the way of travelling with the heart? The way of travelling with the heart is to read the history of the earlier nations. Then, by what is this history established? It is established by only two means. The first is the Qur'an. The second is the authentic Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah, glorified and exalted, said concerning those who came before: ﴿And those after them, none knows them except Allah﴾. Since none knows them except Allah, the source for receiving information about them is from Allah or from His Messenger ﷺ.

As for what the Children of Israel narrated about earlier peoples, this divides into three categories:

The first category: what our Sharia has testified to, or what the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to. This is accepted, not because it is a report from the Children of Israel, but because the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to its truth.

The second: what the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to be false. This is rejected, and it is not permissible to relate it except when a person intends to explain its falsehood and invalidity.

The third category: what revelation has neither confirmed as true nor declared false, that is, what neither the Qur'an nor the Sunnah confirms or denies. Concerning this the Prophet ﷺ said: "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3461) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] so it becomes speech that is permissible to transmit, but it has no benefit, so one should not occupy oneself with it instead of what is more important. By this we learn how to travel with our hearts through the reports of those who came before. Thus the primary, certain source for receiving reports about those who came before is the Book and the Sunnah. As for what has come down in reports from the Children of Israel, you now know that it falls into three categories.

His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾: some grammarians said that *fi* here means *ala* ("upon"), because it is impossible to travel *in the interior* of the earth, on the basis that *fi* denotes enclosure, and the container encloses the contained, as when you say: "The water is in the vessel," where the vessel encloses the water and the water is inside it.

However, someone may say that this is not definite, because the intended meaning is *fi al-ard*, meaning *in the regions (manakib) of the earth*, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you, so walk in its regions﴾ [al-Mulk 15]. The enclosure here would then be the enclosure of the atmosphere: that is, in the atmosphere of the earth, and the atmosphere is the container for the one who travels within it.

﴿So that they might see what was the end of those who came before them﴾ [Ghafir 21]. As for ﴿fa-yanzuru﴾ ("so that they might see"): the *fa* here is said to be conjunctive. On this view, the travelling is negated and the seeing is also negated, and the sense on this view is: "Or have they not travelled in the land, so that they have not seen what was the end of those who were before you?"

It is also said that the *fa* is causal, meaning: "Because of their travelling, they see how it was." The two meanings are interrelated, because if they do not travel they do not see, and if they travel they see.

As for His words ﴿so that they might see how it was﴾: is the seeing here the seeing of the heart and insight, or the seeing of the eye and sight?

This follows from what came before concerning travelling. If the travelling is of the heart, then the seeing is of the heart and insight. If it is of the feet, then the seeing is of the eye and sight. We have already said that travelling is suitable for both, so the seeing is also suitable for both.

﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾: ﴿how﴾ (*kayfa*) is an interrogative noun in the accusative position, as the predicate of *kana* (was) placed before it, and ﴿the end (*aqibatu*)﴾ is its subject (ism).

﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾ means: their outcome (ma'al). What was their outcome? The mention of the outcome will come later, but Allah mentioned their state before mentioning their outcome. He said: ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾. ﴿Greater (ashadd)﴾ comes from *shiddah*, which means firmness and magnitude.

﴿And from them (minhum)﴾: concerning this word there are two readings. (In one reading it is ﴿from you (minkum)﴾.) Thus there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person to the second person. It is known that direct address has a stronger effect on the soul than speaking in the third person. Are you not of that opinion? That is, if you address a person directly, it strikes his soul more forcefully than if you speak in the third person. For this reason Allah's words ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ came in the third person, although the one who frowned and turned away was the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and He did not say "you frowned and turned away," because direct address is more forceful than the third person.

As for his words "(and in one reading ﴿minkum﴾)": know that the terminology of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "in a reading" (*fi qira'a*), it is one of the canonical readings (sab'iyya). When he says "and it was read" (*wa-quri'a*), it is an irregular reading (shadhdha), not one of the canonical seven.

(And in one reading ﴿minkum﴾) ﴿strength and traces upon the earth﴾: from buildings (masani') and palaces (qusur). They were strong in their bodies, and they had more traces upon the earth than those who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The evidence for this is clear in the dwellings of Thamud, for everyone who has seen them understands how strong those people were. Likewise are the remains of 'Ad in al-Ahqaf, which have been discovered, and concerning them Allah said: ﴿Iram, of the lofty pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands﴾ [al-Fajr 7–8]. Their strength was immense, to the point that 'Ad said, "Who is stronger than us?" So what became of them? Allah said: ﴿Allah seized them﴾, that is, destroyed them, ﴿for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah﴾.

These mighty people, who had traces that dazzle the mind, Allah seized for their sins, that is, destroyed them because of their sins. Their sins consisted of two things: denial and turning away. They denied the report and turned away from the command. They denied the news and opposed the commands. They fell into what they were forbidden, and abandoned what they were commanded, and they denied what they were obliged to affirm.

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾: the *bi* here is causal (sababiyya). ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾: ﴿ma﴾ is negative (nafiyya), ﴿min﴾ is attached to ﴿waqin﴾, and ﴿waqin﴾ is the subject of *kana*, to which the superfluous ﴿min﴾ was attached for emphasis. The original form of *waq* is *waqi*, and the *ya* was dropped for lightness. The meaning: they had no one who could protect them from the punishment of Allah. Even the son of Noah, peace be upon him, was not protected from the punishment of Allah by his closeness to Noah, nor by being included in the general promise, because Allah, exalted, had stated that He would save him and his family, meaning Noah's family. When Allah sent the flood upon them, his son called to him to board the ship with him, but he refused and said: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾ [Hud 43], and he drowned. Noah said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family﴾ [Hud 45], and Allah had promised him that He would save him and his family. Allah said: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, his conduct is unrighteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ [Hud 46]. So the closeness of this son to his father did not protect him from anyone, even though he was one of the resolute messengers, and he perished among those who perished, as Allah said here: ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾.

In this verse there are many benefits. Among them: encouragement to travel in the land, from His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾, on the basis that the interrogative here is for rebuke and reproach.

Among its benefits: travelling in the land of those who deny, and observing what punishment Allah brought upon them, is permissible when it is done for the sake of taking lessons, that is, lessons from their destruction, not admiring their strength. On this basis we know that those who now go to the dwellings of Thamud to look at their strength and admire their craftsmanship are gravely mistaken, because they have not travelled in the land in the manner Allah commanded, but in the manner the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not enter upon these punished people except while weeping, lest what befell them befall you. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38) from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. The wording is: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest there befall you what befell them. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."]] So who goes now to the dwellings of Thamud and stands looking at their remains while weeping?! No one, except one whom Allah guides and to whom the truth has become clear. Otherwise they go sightseeing. What is astonishing is that some of our ignorant people consider these to be honoured monuments, and it is said: "Glory be to Allah! The honoured monuments, O ignorant ones, are the Book and the Sunnah, the traces of revelation. As for the traces of those who denied the messengers, they are not honoured. Moreover, are these the traces of your fathers and grandfathers? They are the traces of a people who perished, and after them came people, then more generations." But this is ignorance and blind imitation, which makes people cling to material traces and neglect the spiritual traces.

Among the benefits of these noble verses: the end of those who came before them was an evil end, from His words ﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾ up to His words ﴿so Allah seized them﴾.

Also among their benefits: those who came before them were stronger than them in bodies, in craftsmanship and in traces, yet this strength did not prevent Allah from seizing them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strength of Allah, glorified and exalted, is above every strength. He said: ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾, and yet Allah, exalted, seized them. This is because when Allah wills something, He says to it "Be," and it is. He has no need to bring anyone to help Him, nor to manufacture bombs or cannons. No! "Be," and it is. Look at 'Ad, who boasted of their strength, and Allah destroyed them through the gentlest of things. He subjected the wind against them, not for them, and the wind is among the gentlest of things, yet it destroyed them: ﴿It destroys everything by the command of its Lord, and by morning none could be seen except their dwellings﴾ [al-Ahqaf 25], until they were like the hollow trunks of palm trees. It is said that the wind would lift one of them until he was in the heights of the sky, then cast him down to the earth, and he would land bent over like the hollow trunk of a palm. When you see the trunks of palms, you find that the palm has bent. Those who were mighty and strong, who stood on their feet, became ﴿as if they were hollow palm trunks﴾ [al-Haqqah 7], and in another verse ﴿as if they were uprooted palm trunks﴾ [al-Qamar 20].

Pharaoh said, as Allah reports: ﴿O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51]. With what did Allah destroy him? Allah destroyed him by causing him to leave Egypt, of which he boasted, while he had chosen to leave. He departed as though he were a victor, as though he were winning in battle. Then Allah destroyed him by the very thing he boasted of, water, to make clear that strength belongs to Allah, glorified and exalted, and that Allah is stronger than those people.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Allah intends evil for a people, nothing can avert it. This is shown by His words ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾. Allah has clearly stated this in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people misfortune, there is no repelling it﴾ [al-Ra'd 11]. Nothing protects against what Allah wills: neither palaces, nor defences, nor aircraft, nor anything else. ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾.

Among the benefits of this noble verse, and the one that follows it: the establishment of causes, and that no wrongdoer bears the crime except upon himself. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿That is because﴾ to the end. We have already explained this issue earlier, namely the question of causes, their influence, and the differences among people concerning them. We clarified that the most just and most correct view is that causes have a direct influence, but not an inherent influence in themselves; rather, it is through the powers that Allah has placed within them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He does not punish anyone without sin. This is shown by His words ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾ [Ghafir 22].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 21–22 (part 2 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no nation has passed away without its messengers having come to it. This is shown by His words: ﴿their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾. Every nation was sent a warner, and a messenger came to it to warn it and make things clear to it. These nations acknowledged this. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in Surah al-Mulk: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" (8) They say, "Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'" (9)﴾ [al-Mulk 8, 9]. Then they said: ﴿Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk 10]. Allah also said: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 24]. This is part of the completeness of Allah's mercy and wisdom, that He sent messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers, and for the benefit of creation. Consider: if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not been sent to us by Allah, would we know how to perform wudu'? Would we know how to pray? We would not. But by the mercy of Allah, He sent us a messenger who taught us how to perform wudu' and how to pray. Then, as a result of this wudu' and prayer, sins are forgiven. When a person performs wudu', his sins leave his body with the last drop of water. When he prays, the five daily prayers expiate what comes between them. If a person performs wudu' at home, does it perfectly, and goes out to the mosque with nothing driving him out but the prayer, he does not take a single step without Allah raising him a degree by it and removing a sin from him. Count your steps from your house to the mosque in a day and a night, five times. They are many. All of this is from the bounty of Allah, may He be glorified. Had Allah not guided us with the guidance of direction, and we ask Allah, exalted, to complete it with the guidance of success, we would have been destroyed and would not have known how to worship Allah. So this is from the mercy of Allah, that He sent messengers to the nations to make things clear to them. If you say that we have not yet reached this verse, you are believed, and we will take it up tomorrow, God willing.

* A student: Is a person rewarded for his steps when he comes to the mosque and when he returns from it?

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. As for coming to the mosque, you have heard what... As for returning, there is the story of the man with the donkey who lived far from the mosque. "It was said to him: 'Why do you not buy a donkey to ride?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I seek reward for my walking to the mosque and my returning from it.' He said: 'You will have what you sought reward for.'"[[Abu Dawud (557) and Ibn Majah (783), whose wording this is, narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man from the Ansar, whose house was the farthest house in Madinah, never missed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I felt sorry for him and said: "O so-and-so, if only you would buy a donkey to protect you from the heat, lift you from the dust, and protect you from the creatures of the earth." He said: "By Allah, I do not want my house to be beside the house of Muhammad ﷺ." So I carried him in my heart until I came to the house of the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He called the man and questioned him, and he mentioned the same thing and said he hoped for reward for his footsteps. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You will have what you sought reward for."]] So when a person seeks reward for this, he will have what he sought.

But, my brothers, I tell you: we often miss out on ihtisab (seeking reward with sincerity for an act). Is that not so? We often miss it. We pray, wanting only to fulfil the prayer that is incumbent on us, but we do not feel that we are seeking its reward, and that we will find the reward of this prayer, or the reward of this wudu', or the reward of these steps. We often miss this. Ihtisab has an effect, both in terms of reward and in terms of encouraging a person to act, because when a person knows that if he does a deed he will be recompensed, he increases in deeds. But if he acts only because it is an obligation on him that he must discharge, he becomes like one who pays off a debt on his own behalf, and the creditor takes it from him. For this reason I urge myself and you to this matter, the matter of ihtisab. What is the meaning of ihtisab? It means that he intends by his deed the reward and recompense. Allah said: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ [al-Fath 29]. Listen to the ihtisab: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure﴾ [al-Fath 29]. Seek the reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We ask Allah to remind us of this and help us to it.

* A student: The lesson for a person who enters the places of the people who were destroyed: is it every people who were destroyed, or the disbelievers who were not struck by punishment?

* The Shaykh: No, what is meant is those who were destroyed.

* A student: I said that whoever goes to Madain Salih is in great danger. But if someone says: "I am not affected by the Quran, but I am affected by seeing the remains of these earlier peoples, so as to take the lesson and admonition?"

* The Shaykh: This person went in order to take a lesson, and a person who goes to take a lesson will undoubtedly be affected. But many people now go to take lessons from what they have of strength, not from Allah's seizing of them.

* A student: A person goes to someone to call him to the religion, and he sees that this person commits many sins, has many transgressions, so he recalls the words of Allah: ﴿Thus you used to be before, then Allah bestowed His favour upon you, so verify﴾ [al-Nisa' 94]. The person recalls the matter of what had passed before his commitment, so he does not dare... (...) i.e., he does not proceed to wala' and bara' (loyalty and disavowal)... (...).

* The Shaykh: I did not understand. Give me the issue without preliminaries and conclusions. Say: "Is it permissible for me to go to so-and-so?" That is, you say: "Is it permissible for me to go to a sinful man...?"

* The student: That is, my chest becomes tight at going to him and seeing the sins, and he, of course, does not accept from me the first time, so my chest tightens, and Satan enters into this matter with his whispering.

* The Shaykh: And the question now is: will you go to him or not?

* The student: That is the question.

* The Shaykh: Alright, go. As long as you want to go to call him, then go to him. If your chest tightens, be patient. Even the one who calls people in the market and the mosque has his chest tighten when he sees them as they are. Be patient as long as you want to call him. But if you go wanting to honour him, then it is not permissible.

* A student: The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: "A person, when he is placed in (...), wretched or happy, it was not written for me, so why (...)?"

* The Shaykh: Correct. This is an argument, and the Companions used it against the Messenger ﷺ when he said to them: "There is none of you but that his place in Paradise and his place in the Fire have been written for him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds? Why should we work (...)?" He said: "Work, for each is made easy for what he was created for."[[al-Bukhari (4949), whose wording this is, and Muslim (2647/6), with their chains, narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was at a funeral, and he took something and began to scratch the ground with it. He said: "There is none of you but that his place in the Fire has been written, and his place in Paradise." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely on what is written and leave off deeds?" He said: "Work, for each is made easy for what he was created for. As for the one who is among the people of happiness, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the one who is among the people of wretchedness, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah (5) and believes in the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 5, 6], to the end of the verse.]] We say: you are written as being in Paradise or in the Fire because of your deed, so act with the deeds of the people of Paradise so that you may be among them.

* A student: The towns of the people of Lot, like the towns of Thamud and 'Ad, is it impermissible to go to such places?

* The Shaykh: The scholars say: there is no difference. Everything to which you go so that their traces and strength become clear to you, and you are amazed by this strength, is impermissible.

* The student: And the verse, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: The verse is a narration: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [al-Saffat 137, 138]. This is a report about something that occurred, just as the Messenger said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (7320) and Muslim (2669), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Does that mean the Messenger opens the way for us? It is a report about a matter that has occurred or will occur, just as he reported that a woman would travel from San'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment (22). And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority (23) to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun, but they said, "A magician, a liar"﴾ [Ghafir 22–24].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾ ﴿That﴾ refers to Allah's seizing them for their sins. So these sins were that ﴿their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾ The author said: (with manifest miracles).

﴿Their messengers﴾ is the plural of rasul (messenger). Every nation had a messenger, as Allah said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah"﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. The messengers came to them with clear proofs. The author said: (with miracles), but the correct expression is "with signs" (ayat), because Allah expresses them thus: ﴿Our signs are clear proofs﴾ [Yunus 15]. What is meant by the signs is that which human beings can believe in on its like. They are of two kinds: sensory and non-sensory, and innate and moral. All of them are clear, manifest, evident signs. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah did not send a prophet except that He gave him signs such that people believed on their like."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording of Muslim is: "Among the prophets there was none but that he was given signs such that people believed on their like, but what I was given is a revelation that Allah revealed to me, so I hope I will be the most numerous of them in following on the Day of Resurrection."]]

The wisdom behind these signs is that people cannot accept the call of someone who lived among them and whom they know, who comes and says: "I am a prophet" or "I am a messenger." "Then by what proof?" There must be signs that testify to his truthfulness.

As I told you: signs are of two kinds: non-sensory signs, which is what the revelation brought by these messengers contains, and sensory signs, which is what appears of extraordinary events that break habit. For this reason the definition of a sign has been given as: it is a matter that breaks habit, which Allah, glorified and exalted, manifests at the hand of a messenger to confirm him. This is what a sign is.

The scholars said that sensory signs are suited to the time in which the messenger was sent. They cited as evidence that Moses, peace be upon him, was given magical-seeming signs, that is, resembling magic, but stronger than it, overcoming it. He cast his staff, made of wood, onto the ground, and it became a serpent moving swiftly. He put his hand into his pocket, and it came out white, shining, without defect, that is, without leprosy. This is because in his time magic had reached a lofty, high stage, so he brought signs that overcame that magic. This appeared when he gathered with the magicians on the day they had agreed upon. They cast their ropes and staffs until it appeared to him, from their magic, that they were moving, and Moses felt fear within himself. Allah said: ﴿Do not fear﴾ [Ta-Ha 68], and commanded him to cast the staff. He cast it, and behold, it was a serpent that swallowed what they had fabricated.

Then Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, was sent in a time when medicine had advanced enormously and greatly. He brought something that the physicians could not do: he healed the blind and the leper by Allah's permission, and he brought the dead to life by Allah's permission. Indeed he brought the dead out of their graves by Allah's permission. He would stand over the occupant of a grave, address him, and say: "Come out," and he would come out. This was greater than the medicine they had.

As for Muhammad ﷺ, he was sent at a time when eloquence had reached its peak, and people boasted about who was most eloquent. Poets and orators came to the markets of the Jahiliyyah, such as 'Ukaz and others, competing in their poetry and oratory. Then this Quran came, overcoming all of it, and it defeated them, and they were unable to produce anything like it, even though they were the leaders of eloquence.

The point is that every prophet must have a sign on the like of which human beings can believe, because Allah, glorified and exalted, is Wise and Merciful. He is Wise and does not send a person who says to people, "I am a messenger," without evidence. He is Merciful in that He strengthened these messengers with signs in one respect, and showed mercy to creation by placing signs with the messengers so that the messengers' proof would be accepted by them.

﴿Their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved﴾: the fa' (then) is conjunctive, and it indicates that these people hastened to disbelief, and that they did not reflect or consider. The reason is that fa' indicates sequence and immediacy. ﴿But they disbelieved﴾ means: in the messengers and in the clear proofs they brought.

﴿So Allah seized them﴾ means: He destroyed them. ﴿Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment﴾: Allah, glorified and exalted, destroyed them all, except those who believed.

Then He explained that this seizing is severe, by His words: ﴿Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment.﴾ He is strong from eternity and forever. No weakness preceded His strength, and no weakness will afflict it. As for human beings, they are weak at first and at the end, and the ultimate of their strength is also nothing. Even if a person reaches his full strength and the peak of his power, he is still nothing. But the Lord, mighty and majestic, is strong from eternity and forever.

﴿Severe in punishment﴾ is an instance of an attribute being attributed to what it describes. The meaning is: His punishment is severe. Shadid (severe) means the mighty, strong one whose effects appear on those who are punished.

* There are benefits in this verse:
* Among them: explaining the cause of the destruction of nations, and that it was due to their sins, by His words: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾
* Among its benefits: that no nation passed without a warner having come to it.
* Among its benefits: that the messengers, peace be upon them, were sent with clear, manifest signs.
* Among its benefits: establishing the proof against creation by sending messengers first, then supporting them with clear signs that leave no room for doubt or denial.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that those to whom these were sent did not give thanks for the blessing, but hastened to disbelief and denial.
* Among its benefits: that if a sensible person reflected on what the messengers brought, it would not lead him to disbelief. But most of those who deny the messengers hasten to denial. Allah said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming causes, and that Allah linked effects to their causes. This indicates the completeness of Allah's wisdom, and that He, mighty and majestic, does nothing in vain, nor merely by will, unlike those among the Jabriyyah (determinists) and others who say that Allah does whatever He wills merely by will, not for wisdom. They denied Allah's wisdom and said: wisdom entails deficiency. This is one of the strangest of understandings. Wisdom entails deficiency? They said: yes, because wisdom is a purpose, and if He acts for such-and-such, then He needs this purpose. It is said to them: woe to you and to your understanding. Wisdom is the ultimate end of judgment; that is, wisdom is the greatest indication of distance from foolishness and play.
As for your saying that wisdom is a purpose, and that if you say Allah did such-and-such for such-and-such, it follows that Allah needs it: it is said that the wisdom for which Allah legislates the laws does not return to Himself except in terms of perfection alone. As for benefit, who benefits from it? Creation. As for Allah, mighty and majestic, His wisdom returns to Him with nothing except the manifestation of the perfection of His attributes, mighty and majestic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that al-Qawiyy (the Strong) is one of Allah's names. Is it of the intransitive or transitive names? It is intransitive. Qadir (Capable) is from transitive verbs, but al-Qawiyy is from intransitive ones. Accordingly, it must be affirmed, along with the attribute it indicates, which is strength.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah is severe in punishment, but toward those who disobey Him.

Among its benefits is a warning against opposing Allah, for He is Mighty and severe in punishment. So woe to whoever opposes the command of his Lord. He will face severe punishment from One whose might is never touched by weakness: ﴿Indeed, He is Mighty, severe in punishment﴾.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah. (21) That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, severe in punishment. (22) And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority (23) to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, but they said, "A sorcerer, a liar." (24) So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women. But the scheming of the disbelievers is nothing but in error."﴾ [Ghafir 21–25].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them?﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾. This construction occurs frequently in the Qur'an: the interrogative particle is followed by a conjunction and then the clause. The grammarians (al-mu'ribun) differed over how to analyse this structure (i'rab, grammatical analysis).

Some of them said: the underlying sense is *wa-alam yasiru* ("and have they not travelled"), so the wa is conjunctive to what precedes, and the hamza (interrogative) enters upon its clause, the clause being introduced by it. This view requires no supposed omission, but it faces the objection that the hamza precedes the conjunction. They answered this by saying that placing the hamza first is permissible in such cases.

The second view of the grammarians is that the hamza enters upon something omitted (muqaddar), and the conjunction is conjunctive to that omitted element. In that case we need to specify what is omitted, and only the context can specify it. So the omitted element is supplied according to what the context requires. For example, one may say: *a-fa-raṭū wa-lam yasiru fi al-ard* ("have they then been negligent and not travelled in the land?"), or *aghfalū wa-lam yasiru fi al-ard* ("have they been heedless and not travelled in the land?"), or anything that conveys this meaning.

As for His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾: is the intended meaning the travelling of the hearts, through reflection, contemplation and pondering, or the travelling of feet, until a person comes to know, with his own eyes, what happened to the earlier nations? Both are intended. Whoever cannot travel with his feet should travel with his heart. But what is the way of travelling with the heart? The way of travelling with the heart is to read the history of the earlier nations. Then, by what is this history established? It is established by only two means. The first is the Qur'an. The second is the authentic Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah, glorified and exalted, said concerning those who came before: ﴿And those after them, none knows them except Allah﴾. Since none knows them except Allah, the source for receiving information about them is from Allah or from His Messenger ﷺ.

As for what the Children of Israel narrated about earlier peoples, this divides into three categories:

The first category: what our Sharia has testified to, or what the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to. This is accepted, not because it is a report from the Children of Israel, but because the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to its truth.

The second: what the Qur'an and Sunnah have testified to be false. This is rejected, and it is not permissible to relate it except when a person intends to explain its falsehood and invalidity.

The third category: what revelation has neither confirmed as true nor declared false, that is, what neither the Qur'an nor the Sunnah confirms or denies. Concerning this the Prophet ﷺ said: "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3461) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] so it becomes speech that is permissible to transmit, but it has no benefit, so one should not occupy oneself with it instead of what is more important. By this we learn how to travel with our hearts through the reports of those who came before. Thus the primary, certain source for receiving reports about those who came before is the Book and the Sunnah. As for what has come down in reports from the Children of Israel, you now know that it falls into three categories.

His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾: some grammarians said that *fi* here means *ala* ("upon"), because it is impossible to travel *in the interior* of the earth, on the basis that *fi* denotes enclosure, and the container encloses the contained, as when you say: "The water is in the vessel," where the vessel encloses the water and the water is inside it.

However, someone may say that this is not definite, because the intended meaning is *fi al-ard*, meaning *in the regions (manakib) of the earth*, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you, so walk in its regions﴾ [al-Mulk 15]. The enclosure here would then be the enclosure of the atmosphere: that is, in the atmosphere of the earth, and the atmosphere is the container for the one who travels within it.

﴿So that they might see what was the end of those who came before them﴾ [Ghafir 21]. As for ﴿fa-yanzuru﴾ ("so that they might see"): the *fa* here is said to be conjunctive. On this view, the travelling is negated and the seeing is also negated, and the sense on this view is: "Or have they not travelled in the land, so that they have not seen what was the end of those who were before you?"

It is also said that the *fa* is causal, meaning: "Because of their travelling, they see how it was." The two meanings are interrelated, because if they do not travel they do not see, and if they travel they see.

As for His words ﴿so that they might see how it was﴾: is the seeing here the seeing of the heart and insight, or the seeing of the eye and sight?

This follows from what came before concerning travelling. If the travelling is of the heart, then the seeing is of the heart and insight. If it is of the feet, then the seeing is of the eye and sight. We have already said that travelling is suitable for both, so the seeing is also suitable for both.

﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾: ﴿how﴾ (*kayfa*) is an interrogative noun in the accusative position, as the predicate of *kana* (was) placed before it, and ﴿the end (*aqibatu*)﴾ is its subject (ism).

﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾ means: their outcome (ma'al). What was their outcome? The mention of the outcome will come later, but Allah mentioned their state before mentioning their outcome. He said: ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾. ﴿Greater (ashadd)﴾ comes from *shiddah*, which means firmness and magnitude.

﴿And from them (minhum)﴾: concerning this word there are two readings. (In one reading it is ﴿from you (minkum)﴾.) Thus there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person to the second person. It is known that direct address has a stronger effect on the soul than speaking in the third person. Are you not of that opinion? That is, if you address a person directly, it strikes his soul more forcefully than if you speak in the third person. For this reason Allah's words ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ came in the third person, although the one who frowned and turned away was the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and He did not say "you frowned and turned away," because direct address is more forceful than the third person.

As for his words "(and in one reading ﴿minkum﴾)": know that the terminology of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "in a reading" (*fi qira'a*), it is one of the canonical readings (sab'iyya). When he says "and it was read" (*wa-quri'a*), it is an irregular reading (shadhdha), not one of the canonical seven.

(And in one reading ﴿minkum﴾) ﴿strength and traces upon the earth﴾: from buildings (masani') and palaces (qusur). They were strong in their bodies, and they had more traces upon the earth than those who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The evidence for this is clear in the dwellings of Thamud, for everyone who has seen them understands how strong those people were. Likewise are the remains of 'Ad in al-Ahqaf, which have been discovered, and concerning them Allah said: ﴿Iram, of the lofty pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands﴾ [al-Fajr 7–8]. Their strength was immense, to the point that 'Ad said, "Who is stronger than us?" So what became of them? Allah said: ﴿Allah seized them﴾, that is, destroyed them, ﴿for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah﴾.

These mighty people, who had traces that dazzle the mind, Allah seized for their sins, that is, destroyed them because of their sins. Their sins consisted of two things: denial and turning away. They denied the report and turned away from the command. They denied the news and opposed the commands. They fell into what they were forbidden, and abandoned what they were commanded, and they denied what they were obliged to affirm.

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾: the *bi* here is causal (sababiyya). ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾: ﴿ma﴾ is negative (nafiyya), ﴿min﴾ is attached to ﴿waqin﴾, and ﴿waqin﴾ is the subject of *kana*, to which the superfluous ﴿min﴾ was attached for emphasis. The original form of *waq* is *waqi*, and the *ya* was dropped for lightness. The meaning: they had no one who could protect them from the punishment of Allah. Even the son of Noah, peace be upon him, was not protected from the punishment of Allah by his closeness to Noah, nor by being included in the general promise, because Allah, exalted, had stated that He would save him and his family, meaning Noah's family. When Allah sent the flood upon them, his son called to him to board the ship with him, but he refused and said: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾ [Hud 43], and he drowned. Noah said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family﴾ [Hud 45], and Allah had promised him that He would save him and his family. Allah said: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, his conduct is unrighteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ [Hud 46]. So the closeness of this son to his father did not protect him from anyone, even though he was one of the resolute messengers, and he perished among those who perished, as Allah said here: ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾.

In this verse there are many benefits. Among them: encouragement to travel in the land, from His words ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾, on the basis that the interrogative here is for rebuke and reproach.

Among its benefits: travelling in the land of those who deny, and observing what punishment Allah brought upon them, is permissible when it is done for the sake of taking lessons, that is, lessons from their destruction, not admiring their strength. On this basis we know that those who now go to the dwellings of Thamud to look at their strength and admire their craftsmanship are gravely mistaken, because they have not travelled in the land in the manner Allah commanded, but in the manner the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not enter upon these punished people except while weeping, lest what befell them befall you. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38) from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. The wording is: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest there befall you what befell them. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."]] So who goes now to the dwellings of Thamud and stands looking at their remains while weeping?! No one, except one whom Allah guides and to whom the truth has become clear. Otherwise they go sightseeing. What is astonishing is that some of our ignorant people consider these to be honoured monuments, and it is said: "Glory be to Allah! The honoured monuments, O ignorant ones, are the Book and the Sunnah, the traces of revelation. As for the traces of those who denied the messengers, they are not honoured. Moreover, are these the traces of your fathers and grandfathers? They are the traces of a people who perished, and after them came people, then more generations." But this is ignorance and blind imitation, which makes people cling to material traces and neglect the spiritual traces.

Among the benefits of these noble verses: the end of those who came before them was an evil end, from His words ﴿how was the end of those who came before them﴾ up to His words ﴿so Allah seized them﴾.

Also among their benefits: those who came before them were stronger than them in bodies, in craftsmanship and in traces, yet this strength did not prevent Allah from seizing them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strength of Allah, glorified and exalted, is above every strength. He said: ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾, and yet Allah, exalted, seized them.
