This is because when Allah wills something, He says to it "Be," and it is. He has no need to bring anyone to help Him, nor to manufacture bombs or cannons. No! "Be," and it is. Look at 'Ad, who boasted of their strength, and Allah destroyed them through the gentlest of things. He subjected the wind against them, not for them, and the wind is among the gentlest of things, yet it destroyed them: ﴿It destroys everything by the command of its Lord, and by morning none could be seen except their dwellings﴾ [al-Ahqaf 25], until they were like the hollow trunks of palm trees. It is said that the wind would lift one of them until he was in the heights of the sky, then cast him down to the earth, and he would land bent over like the hollow trunk of a palm. When you see the trunks of palms, you find that the palm has bent. Those who were mighty and strong, who stood on their feet, became ﴿as if they were hollow palm trunks﴾ [al-Haqqah 7], and in another verse ﴿as if they were uprooted palm trunks﴾ [al-Qamar 20].

Pharaoh said, as Allah reports: ﴿O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51]. With what did Allah destroy him? Allah destroyed him by causing him to leave Egypt, of which he boasted, while he had chosen to leave. He departed as though he were a victor, as though he were winning in battle. Then Allah destroyed him by the very thing he boasted of, water, to make clear that strength belongs to Allah, glorified and exalted, and that Allah is stronger than those people.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Allah intends evil for a people, nothing can avert it. This is shown by His words ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾. Allah has clearly stated this in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people misfortune, there is no repelling it﴾ [al-Ra'd 11]. Nothing protects against what Allah wills: neither palaces, nor defences, nor aircraft, nor anything else. ﴿And they had no protector from Allah﴾.

Among the benefits of this noble verse, and the one that follows it: the establishment of causes, and that no wrongdoer bears the crime except upon himself. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿That is because﴾ to the end. We have already explained this issue earlier, namely the question of causes, their influence, and the differences among people concerning them. We clarified that the most just and most correct view is that causes have a direct influence, but not an inherent influence in themselves; rather, it is through the powers that Allah has placed within them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He does not punish anyone without sin. This is shown by His words ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾ [Ghafir 22].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 21–22 (part 2 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no nation has passed away without its messengers having come to it. This is shown by His words: ﴿their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾. Every nation was sent a warner, and a messenger came to it to warn it and make things clear to it. These nations acknowledged this. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in Surah al-Mulk: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" (8) They say, "Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'" (9)﴾ [al-Mulk 8, 9]. Then they said: ﴿Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk 10]. Allah also said: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 24]. This is part of the completeness of Allah's mercy and wisdom, that He sent messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers, and for the benefit of creation. Consider: if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not been sent to us by Allah, would we know how to perform wudu'? Would we know how to pray? We would not. But by the mercy of Allah, He sent us a messenger who taught us how to perform wudu' and how to pray. Then, as a result of this wudu' and prayer, sins are forgiven. When a person performs wudu', his sins leave his body with the last drop of water. When he prays, the five daily prayers expiate what comes between them. If a person performs wudu' at home, does it perfectly, and goes out to the mosque with nothing driving him out but the prayer, he does not take a single step without Allah raising him a degree by it and removing a sin from him. Count your steps from your house to the mosque in a day and a night, five times. They are many. All of this is from the bounty of Allah, may He be glorified. Had Allah not guided us with the guidance of direction, and we ask Allah, exalted, to complete it with the guidance of success, we would have been destroyed and would not have known how to worship Allah. So this is from the mercy of Allah, that He sent messengers to the nations to make things clear to them. If you say that we have not yet reached this verse, you are believed, and we will take it up tomorrow, God willing.

* A student: Is a person rewarded for his steps when he comes to the mosque and when he returns from it?

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. As for coming to the mosque, you have heard what... As for returning, there is the story of the man with the donkey who lived far from the mosque. "It was said to him: 'Why do you not buy a donkey to ride?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I seek reward for my walking to the mosque and my returning from it.' He said: 'You will have what you sought reward for.'"[[Abu Dawud (557) and Ibn Majah (783), whose wording this is, narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man from the Ansar, whose house was the farthest house in Madinah, never missed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I felt sorry for him and said: "O so-and-so, if only you would buy a donkey to protect you from the heat, lift you from the dust, and protect you from the creatures of the earth." He said: "By Allah, I do not want my house to be beside the house of Muhammad ﷺ." So I carried him in my heart until I came to the house of the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He called the man and questioned him, and he mentioned the same thing and said he hoped for reward for his footsteps. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You will have what you sought reward for."]] So when a person seeks reward for this, he will have what he sought.

But, my brothers, I tell you: we often miss out on ihtisab (seeking reward with sincerity for an act). Is that not so? We often miss it. We pray, wanting only to fulfil the prayer that is incumbent on us, but we do not feel that we are seeking its reward, and that we will find the reward of this prayer, or the reward of this wudu', or the reward of these steps. We often miss this. Ihtisab has an effect, both in terms of reward and in terms of encouraging a person to act, because when a person knows that if he does a deed he will be recompensed, he increases in deeds. But if he acts only because it is an obligation on him that he must discharge, he becomes like one who pays off a debt on his own behalf, and the creditor takes it from him. For this reason I urge myself and you to this matter, the matter of ihtisab. What is the meaning of ihtisab? It means that he intends by his deed the reward and recompense. Allah said: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ [al-Fath 29]. Listen to the ihtisab: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure﴾ [al-Fath 29]. Seek the reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We ask Allah to remind us of this and help us to it.

* A student: The lesson for a person who enters the places of the people who were destroyed: is it every people who were destroyed, or the disbelievers who were not struck by punishment?

* The Shaykh: No, what is meant is those who were destroyed.

* A student: I said that whoever goes to Madain Salih is in great danger. But if someone says: "I am not affected by the Quran, but I am affected by seeing the remains of these earlier peoples, so as to take the lesson and admonition?"

* The Shaykh: This person went in order to take a lesson, and a person who goes to take a lesson will undoubtedly be affected. But many people now go to take lessons from what they have of strength, not from Allah's seizing of them.

* A student: A person goes to someone to call him to the religion, and he sees that this person commits many sins, has many transgressions, so he recalls the words of Allah: ﴿Thus you used to be before, then Allah bestowed His favour upon you, so verify﴾ [al-Nisa' 94]. The person recalls the matter of what had passed before his commitment, so he does not dare... (...) i.e., he does not proceed to wala' and bara' (loyalty and disavowal)... (...).

* The Shaykh: I did not understand. Give me the issue without preliminaries and conclusions. Say: "Is it permissible for me to go to so-and-so?" That is, you say: "Is it permissible for me to go to a sinful man...?"

* The student: That is, my chest becomes tight at going to him and seeing the sins, and he, of course, does not accept from me the first time, so my chest tightens, and Satan enters into this matter with his whispering.

* The Shaykh: And the question now is: will you go to him or not?

* The student: That is the question.

* The Shaykh: Alright, go. As long as you want to go to call him, then go to him. If your chest tightens, be patient. Even the one who calls people in the market and the mosque has his chest tighten when he sees them as they are. Be patient as long as you want to call him. But if you go wanting to honour him, then it is not permissible.

* A student: The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: "A person, when he is placed in (...), wretched or happy, it was not written for me, so why (...)?"

* The Shaykh: Correct. This is an argument, and the Companions used it against the Messenger ﷺ when he said to them: "There is none of you but that his place in Paradise and his place in the Fire have been written for him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds? Why should we work (...)?" He said: "Work, for each is made easy for what he was created for."[[al-Bukhari (4949), whose wording this is, and Muslim (2647/6), with their chains, narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was at a funeral, and he took something and began to scratch the ground with it. He said: "There is none of you but that his place in the Fire has been written, and his place in Paradise." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely on what is written and leave off deeds?" He said: "Work, for each is made easy for what he was created for. As for the one who is among the people of happiness, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the one who is among the people of wretchedness, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah (5) and believes in the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 5, 6], to the end of the verse.]] We say: you are written as being in Paradise or in the Fire because of your deed, so act with the deeds of the people of Paradise so that you may be among them.

* A student: The towns of the people of Lot, like the towns of Thamud and 'Ad, is it impermissible to go to such places?

* The Shaykh: The scholars say: there is no difference. Everything to which you go so that their traces and strength become clear to you, and you are amazed by this strength, is impermissible.

* The student: And the verse, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: The verse is a narration: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [al-Saffat 137, 138]. This is a report about something that occurred, just as the Messenger said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (7320) and Muslim (2669), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Does that mean the Messenger opens the way for us? It is a report about a matter that has occurred or will occur, just as he reported that a woman would travel from San'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment (22). And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority (23) to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun, but they said, "A magician, a liar"﴾ [Ghafir 22–24].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾ ﴿That﴾ refers to Allah's seizing them for their sins. So these sins were that ﴿their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾ The author said: (with manifest miracles).

﴿Their messengers﴾ is the plural of rasul (messenger). Every nation had a messenger, as Allah said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah"﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. The messengers came to them with clear proofs. The author said: (with miracles), but the correct expression is "with signs" (ayat), because Allah expresses them thus: ﴿Our signs are clear proofs﴾ [Yunus 15]. What is meant by the signs is that which human beings can believe in on its like. They are of two kinds: sensory and non-sensory, and innate and moral. All of them are clear, manifest, evident signs. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah did not send a prophet except that He gave him signs such that people believed on their like."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording of Muslim is: "Among the prophets there was none but that he was given signs such that people believed on their like, but what I was given is a revelation that Allah revealed to me, so I hope I will be the most numerous of them in following on the Day of Resurrection."]]

The wisdom behind these signs is that people cannot accept the call of someone who lived among them and whom they know, who comes and says: "I am a prophet" or "I am a messenger." "Then by what proof?" There must be signs that testify to his truthfulness.

As I told you: signs are of two kinds: non-sensory signs, which is what the revelation brought by these messengers contains, and sensory signs, which is what appears of extraordinary events that break habit. For this reason the definition of a sign has been given as: it is a matter that breaks habit, which Allah, glorified and exalted, manifests at the hand of a messenger to confirm him. This is what a sign is.

The scholars said that sensory signs are suited to the time in which the messenger was sent. They cited as evidence that Moses, peace be upon him, was given magical-seeming signs, that is, resembling magic, but stronger than it, overcoming it. He cast his staff, made of wood, onto the ground, and it became a serpent moving swiftly. He put his hand into his pocket, and it came out white, shining, without defect, that is, without leprosy. This is because in his time magic had reached a lofty, high stage, so he brought signs that overcame that magic. This appeared when he gathered with the magicians on the day they had agreed upon. They cast their ropes and staffs until it appeared to him, from their magic, that they were moving, and Moses felt fear within himself. Allah said: ﴿Do not fear﴾ [Ta-Ha 68], and commanded him to cast the staff. He cast it, and behold, it was a serpent that swallowed what they had fabricated.

Then Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, was sent in a time when medicine had advanced enormously and greatly. He brought something that the physicians could not do: he healed the blind and the leper by Allah's permission, and he brought the dead to life by Allah's permission. Indeed he brought the dead out of their graves by Allah's permission. He would stand over the occupant of a grave, address him, and say: "Come out," and he would come out. This was greater than the medicine they had.

As for Muhammad ﷺ, he was sent at a time when eloquence had reached its peak, and people boasted about who was most eloquent. Poets and orators came to the markets of the Jahiliyyah, such as 'Ukaz and others, competing in their poetry and oratory. Then this Quran came, overcoming all of it, and it defeated them, and they were unable to produce anything like it, even though they were the leaders of eloquence.

The point is that every prophet must have a sign on the like of which human beings can believe, because Allah, glorified and exalted, is Wise and Merciful. He is Wise and does not send a person who says to people, "I am a messenger," without evidence. He is Merciful in that He strengthened these messengers with signs in one respect, and showed mercy to creation by placing signs with the messengers so that the messengers' proof would be accepted by them.

﴿Their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved﴾: the fa' (then) is conjunctive, and it indicates that these people hastened to disbelief, and that they did not reflect or consider. The reason is that fa' indicates sequence and immediacy. ﴿But they disbelieved﴾ means: in the messengers and in the clear proofs they brought.

﴿So Allah seized them﴾ means: He destroyed them. ﴿Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment﴾: Allah, glorified and exalted, destroyed them all, except those who believed.

Then He explained that this seizing is severe, by His words: ﴿Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment.﴾ He is strong from eternity and forever. No weakness preceded His strength, and no weakness will afflict it. As for human beings, they are weak at first and at the end, and the ultimate of their strength is also nothing. Even if a person reaches his full strength and the peak of his power, he is still nothing. But the Lord, mighty and majestic, is strong from eternity and forever.

﴿Severe in punishment﴾ is an instance of an attribute being attributed to what it describes. The meaning is: His punishment is severe. Shadid (severe) means the mighty, strong one whose effects appear on those who are punished.

* There are benefits in this verse:
* Among them: explaining the cause of the destruction of nations, and that it was due to their sins, by His words: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.﴾
* Among its benefits: that no nation passed without a warner having come to it.
* Among its benefits: that the messengers, peace be upon them, were sent with clear, manifest signs.
* Among its benefits: establishing the proof against creation by sending messengers first, then supporting them with clear signs that leave no room for doubt or denial.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that those to whom these were sent did not give thanks for the blessing, but hastened to disbelief and denial.
* Among its benefits: that if a sensible person reflected on what the messengers brought, it would not lead him to disbelief. But most of those who deny the messengers hasten to denial. Allah said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming causes, and that Allah linked effects to their causes. This indicates the completeness of Allah's wisdom, and that He, mighty and majestic, does nothing in vain, nor merely by will, unlike those among the Jabriyyah (determinists) and others who say that Allah does whatever He wills merely by will, not for wisdom. They denied Allah's wisdom and said: wisdom entails deficiency. This is one of the strangest of understandings. Wisdom entails deficiency? They said: yes, because wisdom is a purpose, and if He acts for such-and-such, then He needs this purpose. It is said to them: woe to you and to your understanding. Wisdom is the ultimate end of judgment; that is, wisdom is the greatest indication of distance from foolishness and play.
As for your saying that wisdom is a purpose, and that if you say Allah did such-and-such for such-and-such, it follows that Allah needs it: it is said that the wisdom for which Allah legislates the laws does not return to Himself except in terms of perfection alone. As for benefit, who benefits from it? Creation. As for Allah, mighty and majestic, His wisdom returns to Him with nothing except the manifestation of the perfection of His attributes, mighty and majestic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that al-Qawiyy (the Strong) is one of Allah's names. Is it of the intransitive or transitive names? It is intransitive. Qadir (Capable) is from transitive verbs, but al-Qawiyy is from intransitive ones. Accordingly, it must be affirmed, along with the attribute it indicates, which is strength.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah is severe in punishment, but toward those who disobey Him.

Among its benefits is a warning against opposing Allah, for He is Mighty and severe in punishment. So woe to whoever opposes the command of his Lord. He will face severe punishment from One whose might is never touched by weakness: ﴿Indeed, He is Mighty, severe in punishment﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 23–24 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority, to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun﴾ [Ghafir 23, 24]. This sentence is emphasized by several emphatic particles. What are they?
* Student: Laqad (indeed).
* Shaykh: With (laqad)? That is not correct. With three emphatics?
* Student: With three emphatics.
* Shaykh: What are they?
* Student: The waw.
* Shaykh: The waw. Is the waw one of the emphatics?
* Student: The oath.
* Shaykh: You have shifted away from the waw as an emphatic?
* Student: The waw is the waw of the oath.
* Shaykh: Where is the waw of the oath? This waw is a conjunction particle!
* Student: The waw of the oath (...).
* Shaykh: And the lam.
* Student: And qad.
* Shaykh: And qad.
This construction occurs frequently in the Qur'an, ﴿laqad﴾, and it is said that this sentence is emphasized by three emphatics (...): the lam, which falls in its answer, and qad.
﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾. Moses is the son of 'Imran, the best, greatest and strongest of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and he is among the strongest and most powerful of the prophets. What shows this is what he did before prophethood and what he did after prophethood. Before prophethood, he passed by a man of his people who was quarrelling with a man of his enemies, and Moses struck him and killed him. This shows his strength and vigour. After prophethood, when he returned and saw that they had associated partners with Allah, he became exceedingly angry and threw down the tablets upon which Allah had written the Torah. He threw them, and some of them said: they broke. He threw the tablets and seized his brother Harun by the head, and Harun was a prophet, a partner of his in prophethood: ﴿He seized his brother by the head, dragging him towards himself﴾ [al-A'raf 150]. He said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard nor my head. I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."﴾ [Ta-Ha 94]. ﴿When the anger subsided from Moses, he took up the tablets﴾ [al-A'raf 154]. This shows his strength and vigour, upon him be prayers and peace. This is also from wisdom, for he was sent to the most rebellious people on earth, Pharaoh. For this reason he met him with strength. He said to him: ﴿You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidences, and I truly think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ [al-Isra' 102]. This is a strength that shows his strength, upon him be prayers and peace.
He, may Allah the Exalted, also sent him to a stubborn people, namely the Children of Israel. For this reason, as far as we know, there is no nation among the nations like the Children of Israel in stubbornness, aversion and arrogance, to the extent that when fighting was prescribed for them, they said to Moses: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight, while we will sit here﴾, and would that they had limited themselves to that. ﴿So fight, you and your Lord, for we are sitting here﴾, we will sit on the cushions and not move, and you and your Lord go and fight. ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here﴾ [al-Ma'idah 24]. Therefore it was from wisdom that this messenger be of this degree of severity, in keeping with those to whom he was sent, from Pharaoh and the Children of Israel.
As for His saying: ﴿with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ [Ghafir 23], ﴿Our signs﴾ is plural, indicating that he had multiple signs, and so it was: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them﴾ [al-Isra' 101], and so on. He was given signs, the greatest, strongest and clearest in sensory terms of which is the sign of the staff, for it is one of Allah's wondrous and remarkable sensory signs: a staff with which he drives his sheep and in which he has other uses, and on which he leans. When he threw it, it became a great serpent that swallowed whatever was before it, and when he took hold of it, it returned to being a staff, and when he struck the rock with it, water gushed forth. This staff is a sign of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Consider now, reflect on how many staves and ropes the sorcerers threw, their abundance and variety. Then he threw this staff, and it began to swallow all that they had falsified. I wonder where the belly is that can contain these things! But the signs of Allah dazzle the minds. Otherwise you would say: how can a serpent the size of a staff swallow what they falsified of ropes and staves, so where does it go? We say: do not ask where it goes; you believe and affirm this, and how it goes to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. There is no objection to these things, when you chew them, becoming a large thing a small thing.
Allah sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority. Authority (sultan): everything by which a person has power, that is, proof and strength, and it varies according to context. Thus, for a father over his children in discipline, authority is the authority of striking; the authority for those called to Allah is the authority of clarification; and the authority for one who is disputed with is the authority of proof. It varies according to places. The point is that whatever gives a person power over others is authority.
His saying: ﴿clear﴾ may be intransitive, and it may be transitive, for the quadriliteral (abana) is both intransitive and transitive. You say: "abantu lahu al-haqq" (I made the truth clear to him), and you say: "aban al-subh" (the morning became clear), that is, it became evident and manifest. So it is a quadriliteral verb suitable for both transitivity and intransitivity.
If someone says: how can one verb be suitable for both transitivity and intransitivity? We say: yes, it is possible; the Arabic language is broad. (raja'a) is a past-tense triliteral verb that is intransitive and transitive: ﴿They say: If we return to Medina﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. Is this intransitive or transitive? Intransitive. ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾ [al-Tawbah 83]. This is transitive. So there is no objection to a single verb being intransitive in one context and transitive in another context, and (aban) is of this kind. So is His saying, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿and a clear authority﴾ meaning "clear", or "making clear, manifesting the truth"?
Let us consider which is more eloquent: that which is clear in itself, or that which makes clear to others? The second, for that which makes clear to others must itself be clear. On this basis, the word (mubin) in the transitive sense is more comprehensive and broader in meaning, and what is more comprehensive and broader in meaning is adopted, and we do not say that the second is abandoned. If we adopt the more comprehensive and broader, we do not say that it has abandoned the second, why? Because the second is included in the first.
* In this noble verse there are benefits, among them: (...) the mission of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, with the three emphatics we mentioned just now: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs﴾ [Ghafir 23].
* And among the benefits of the verse: that Allah, glory be to Him, repeats the mention of the story of Moses, sometimes expanding it, sometimes condensing it, and varying it. It combines abundance with variety in terms of style, and variety in terms of expansion and brevity. Why? Because the Prophet ﷺ lived among polytheist people at the beginning of the message, and among Jewish people after the hijrah. For this reason the Meccan surahs mention the story of Moses sometimes at length and sometimes briefly, in order that the Prophet ﷺ be prepared to dispute with the Jews, among whom the hijrah would be to a land they inhabited. For this reason you will not find the story of any prophet (...) the story of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, neither in its variety, nor its repetition, nor its style.
* From the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of Moses, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through what Allah honoured him with, namely the message.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that Moses, upon him be peace, was given signs, and Allah the Exalted explained in other verses that they were nine signs.
* And among its benefits: that Moses was given authority, that is, power and strength in establishing proof and in other matters; as His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾ shows.
If you want to know something of the authority Allah gave him, look at his debate in Surah al-Shu'ara' with Pharaoh, where he silenced him and made him swallow a stone. At the end, he threatened him with force. Pharaoh says: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29]. This is a word of intimidation. ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ is more intimidating than if he had said: "I will imprison you." It is as if he is saying: I have many prisoners, and I am able to imprison them, and I will make you among them. This is more intimidating than if he had said: "I will imprison you."
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: what we pointed out in the previous verse, that no messenger was sent except that he was given clear signs proving his truthfulness, and this is from Allah's wisdom and Allah's mercy.
* Student: Was Harun, the prophet of Allah, sent with Moses as a messenger or a prophet?
* Shaykh: No, a messenger. Did they not say to Pharaoh: "We are two messengers of the Lord of the worlds"?
* Student: "There is no prophet whom Allah has sent except that he was given signs such that mankind believed upon their like." What is the meaning of "likeness"?
* Shaykh: That is: like the signs that the messengers brought.
* Student: In number, meaning?
* Shaykh: In number or in manner.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, "such that mankind believed upon their like"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Among the prophets there is none who has not been given signs such that mankind believed upon their like, and what I was given is revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]] according to those to whom they were sent. That is, the signs that the messengers bring are such that mankind believes upon their like; meaning they are convincing signs.
* Student: Some scholars of criticism and validation (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil), when speaking about a man, say: "This man is like the staff of Moses that swallows what they falsify." Some brothers joke with it, saying to another: "You are like the staff of Moses that swallows what they falsify." Is it permissible to joke with such a thing?
* Shaykh: I see that even the scholars of hadith who say this, may Allah pardon them, should not say it like this, because it is feared that it may be used mockingly, though the hadith scholars do not intend this at all. It is better to say: "This man is, for example, a sign; this man has wide knowledge; this man has vast learning," and the like.
* Student: Truly, O Shaykh, they also say: "So-and-so possesses the magic staff of Moses."
* Shaykh: This too is not permitted; this is worse, because saying "the magic staff of Moses" means that what he brought was sorcery, and this is dangerous.
* Student: What is the evidence that Allah will judge people in half a day?
* Shaykh: First: hadiths that have come concerning this. Second: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day will be better in resting place and finer in place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan 24], and the maqil (place of repose) is only at midday.
* Student: (...) We have benefited from this verse: ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear evidences﴾ [Ghafir 22], the linking of effects to causes (...)?
* Shaykh: The ba' is for causation.
* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, what is the difference between intransitive verbs that become transitive through a preposition and those that do not?
* Shaykh: They say: whatever is transitive by itself is transitive, and whatever is only transitive through a preposition is intransitive. That is, the verb that governs a direct object is the transitive one. Some of them also said there is a second sign; it has several signs, among them this one: that it is correct to form from it the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) when it is transitive, whereas that which is only transitive with a preposition does not correctly form the passive participle except with its complement.
* Student: What is intended by the authority with which Moses was sent?
* Shaykh: Did we not say: the authority is the strength of proof, varying by context?
* Student: May Allah bless you. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have crafted﴾ [Ta-Ha 69]. From this verse, when we read it, we learn that Moses, upon him be peace, threw the staff and it ate all the serpents, and you mentioned that the serpent, whenever the sorcerers threw (...). * Shaykh: No, in any case, if it enters its mouth it must dissolve quickly, but in the sight of people they see it swallowing and eating.

* Student: The saying of those who said: (...) like the saying of al-Qahtani:
Allah made me a staff of Moses for you, until it swallows your falsehood, my serpent.
* Shaykh: This is by way of resemblance, by way of comparison. There is a difference between this and what the brother mentioned. This one says: it is as if I am the staff of Moses that swallows your weak and false proofs.

What is the reason for not saying it?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed; because we say that the staff of Moses, upon him be peace, became a sign that swallowed all that they falsified, and this man, whatever he is, cannot possibly (...).

Then when he brought them the truth from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women; and the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error"﴾ [Ghafir 23–25].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾. What are the signs with which Moses was sent? How many signs?
* Student: Nine signs.
* Shaykh: Nine signs. Yes.
The ba' in His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾: what is its meaning?
* Student: For accompaniment.
* Shaykh: For accompaniment, or it explains what he was sent with, so it is for transitivity.
What is the wisdom in the signs that Allah gives to the messengers?
* Student: So that the truthfulness of these messengers is shown, so that mankind believes upon their like.
* Shaykh: As confirmation of the messengers, and as mercy toward those to whom they were sent.
His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿and a clear authority﴾? Does it mean that He sent him to be a king over Pharaoh, or what?
* Student: Authority is proof, and ﴿clear﴾ means manifest, or making manifest.
* Shaykh: Or both, and everything over which a person has power is called authority, whether it is proof, knowledge, weapons, or other things.
Enumerate for us the nine signs with which Moses was sent.
* Student: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate:
First: the staff.
Second: the hand; ﴿And insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white﴾ [al-Naml 12].
Third: the locusts.
* Shaykh: The flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and blood. How many is this?

* Another student: The splitting of the sea.

* Shaykh: The years and the loss of fruits. Good. Some of them said: striking the rock with the staff so that it gushes forth.
* Student: (...).

*Shaykh:* There is some ambiguity here. For the Children of Israel, the splitting of the sea and the water gushing from the rock would be included, but these two signs were not for the people of Pharaoh. For the people of Pharaoh: the years of drought and the shortage of crops, in addition to the seven previously mentioned.

He said: ﴿To Pharaoh﴾ is connected to ﴿We sent﴾. Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt who possessed it and dominated the Children of Israel, so he would slaughter their sons and spare their women. It is said that he did this because some soothsayers (kahin, pl. kuhhan) told him: "A man will arise among the Children of Israel through whose hand your kingdom will end." This is one view.

Another view is that he did this to humiliate and degrade them, because if the men are killed and the women are left, the nation is destroyed. This view is stronger, because the first view rests on reports from the Children of Israel, and it is known that reports from the Children of Israel are neither to be affirmed nor denied. The reasonable explanation for his slaughtering their sons and sparing their women is the humiliation of this people, who were few in number compared to the Qibt (Copts).

He said: ﴿To Pharaoh﴾ is connected to ﴿We sent﴾. Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt who possessed it and dominated the Children of Israel, so he would slaughter their sons and spare their women. It is said that he did this because some soothsayers told him: "A man will arise among the Children of Israel through whose hand your kingdom will end." This is one view.

Another view is that he did this to humiliate and degrade them, because if the men are killed and the women are left, the nation is destroyed. This view is stronger, because the first view rests on reports from the Children of Israel, and it is known that reports from the Children of Israel are neither to be affirmed nor denied. The reasonable explanation for his slaughtering their sons and sparing their women is the humiliation of this people, who were few in number compared to the Copts.

﴿To Pharaoh and Haman﴾. ﴿Haman﴾ was Pharaoh's minister. ﴿And Qarun﴾ was a merchant of Pharaoh's household, because Qarun was extremely wealthy. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾ [al-Qasas 28:76], meaning gold and silver, ﴿so that its keys would weigh heavily upon a band of strong men﴾ [al-Qasas 28:76]. "Tanu'u" means "to weigh down": the band, meaning the group of strong men, would be weighed down by them. These were his keys, so his treasuries were vast and great.

﴿And Qarun. Then they said﴾: the pronoun refers to the three: Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun. ﴿Then they said: "A sorcerer, a liar"﴾. ﴿A sorcerer﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, which the exegete supplied in his words: (he is a sorcerer, a liar). "Sahir" (sorcerer) is an active participle from "sihr" (magic), and it refers to one who bewitches people so that they see realities differently from what they are. He does not change realities, for only the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, changes realities. Rather, he shows people realities in a form other than their true nature, as the sorcerers of Pharaoh's household did when they cast their ropes and staffs, and people saw them as moving like snakes, though they were not. These people said: "Moses is a sorcerer. How can he throw the staff and it becomes a serpent? How can he put his hand in and it comes out white without harm?" This is nothing but magic.

﴿Liar﴾ means one who lies in what he claims of prophethood. He is a sorcerer in his signs and a liar in his claim. Then he said ﴿liar﴾, which is either an intensive form or an attributive form. The difference between the intensive form and the attributive form is that the attributive form is a constant description, while the intensive form is a repeated, recurring act. Do you understand? The word "najjar" (carpenter) here is an attributive form, though it may be an intensive form because of how much he works as a carpenter. But when it is said that someone is "akkal lil-ta'am" (a great eater), this may not be an attribute, but because he eats a lot, he is described as a great eater.

﴿So when he came to them with the truth﴾: Allah sent him with the signs. They said: "A sorcerer, a liar." ﴿So when he came to them with the truth﴾, with the truth, ﴿from Us﴾, from Allah the Exalted, which is the revelation. When Moses, peace be upon him, said to them: "Allah is your Lord, and Allah is One," and similar matters that were discussed between him and Pharaoh, as is mentioned in Surat al-Shu'ara' and Surat al-Isra' and elsewhere.

When he came to them with the truth, which they could not counter with a refuting argument, Pharaoh threatened Moses, saying: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among those imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:29]. This is a threat. Another point: ﴿They said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women"﴾ [Ghafir 40:25]. ﴿Spare﴾ means let them live, ﴿their women﴾. On this basis, the killing of the sons of the Children of Israel and the sparing of the women occurred twice: the first time before Moses was sent, and the second time after he was sent.

﴿They said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women."﴾ Their women, so that they would have no strength left and their awe would vanish, because if only the women remained, the women are weak. They cannot defend themselves or defend their rights, so Moses and his people would be left in the worst condition.

﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women﴾, and so on.

Now let us return to derive the benefits, so as not to stray:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾.

In this noble verse there is: the affirmation of Moses's prophethood, peace be upon him. From this benefit follows the establishment of proof against the Children of Israel who disbelieved and transgressed, even though Allah had sent this noble messenger to them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, does not send a messenger except with a clear sign that demonstrates his truthfulness. This is affirmed by the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah did not send any prophet except that He gave him of the signs that people could believe upon the like of." 

[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording is: "There was not among the prophets any prophet except that he was given of the signs what people believed in because of its like. But what I was given was a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]]

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the signs are an authority and proof upon those to whom the messengers were sent, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾. On this basis, the mention of "authority" after "signs" is the conjoining of a thing with itself, to show its benefit and fruit; the signs are the authority.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the signs must be clear and manifest the truth, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾.

Then He said: ﴿To Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun﴾, and so on.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: leaders stand in the place of followers, because the message was not to these three alone, but to all the people of Pharaoh. Rather, the chiefs stand in the place of the followers.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the stubborn opponents of the messengers have varied causes for their obstinacy and opposition to the messengers. It may be authority, it may be office, it may be wealth, it may be physical strength. In this verse there are three causes: kingship, the second is office (ministry), and the third is wealth. Among 'Ad, who had physical strength, they said: ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 41:15].

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obstinacy of those who deny the messengers, for they said to this noble messenger: he is a sorcerer and he is a liar.

Among its benefits: what they said in rejecting the call is mere assertion, because they did not establish any evidence for their claim. They merely said: "A sorcerer, a liar." This is what weak and incapable people resort to when they cannot counter argument with argument, so they turn to abuse, insults and similar things.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the signs brought by the prophets are beyond the ability of ordinary people, as shown by His saying: ﴿sorcerer﴾, and a sorcerer is one who brings about matters that overwhelm people. But the difference between the sorcerer and the prophet is that the prophet is supported by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not by his own action. That is, the sorcerer is one who works on a thing until he brings a miracle, whereas for the prophet, the signs come to him without any action of his own, but by the will of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. If someone says: "Then what is the difference between a karamah (a miraculous gift granted to a righteous servant) and a sign of a prophet?"

We say: the difference between them is that the karamah comes to a follower of the prophet, whereas the sign comes to the prophet himself. That is, one whom Allah grants a karamah from among the saints does not claim to be a messenger or a prophet, but Allah grants him the karamah as confirmation for him or as confirmation for Islam. In that there is also a sign for the prophet whom he follows.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 23–24 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority, to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun﴾ [Ghafir 23, 24]. This sentence is emphasized by several emphatic particles. What are they?
* Student: Laqad (indeed).
* Shaykh: With (laqad)? That is not correct. With three emphatics?
* Student: With three emphatics.
* Shaykh: What are they?
* Student: The waw.
* Shaykh: The waw. Is the waw one of the emphatics?
* Student: The oath.
* Shaykh: You have shifted away from the waw as an emphatic?
* Student: The waw is the waw of the oath.
* Shaykh: Where is the waw of the oath? This waw is a conjunction particle!
* Student: The waw of the oath (...).
* Shaykh: And the lam.
* Student: And qad.
* Shaykh: And qad.
This construction occurs frequently in the Qur'an, ﴿laqad﴾, and it is said that this sentence is emphasized by three emphatics (...): the lam, which falls in its answer, and qad.
﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾. Moses is the son of 'Imran, the best, greatest and strongest of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and he is among the strongest and most powerful of the prophets. What shows this is what he did before prophethood and what he did after prophethood. Before prophethood, he passed by a man of his people who was quarrelling with a man of his enemies, and Moses struck him and killed him. This shows his strength and vigour. After prophethood, when he returned and saw that they had associated partners with Allah, he became exceedingly angry and threw down the tablets upon which Allah had written the Torah. He threw them, and some of them said: they broke. He threw the tablets and seized his brother Harun by the head, and Harun was a prophet, a partner of his in prophethood: ﴿He seized his brother by the head, dragging him towards himself﴾ [al-A'raf 150]. He said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard nor my head. I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."﴾ [Ta-Ha 94]. ﴿When the anger subsided from Moses, he took up the tablets﴾ [al-A'raf 154]. This shows his strength and vigour, upon him be prayers and peace. This is also from wisdom, for he was sent to the most rebellious people on earth, Pharaoh. For this reason he met him with strength. He said to him: ﴿You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidences, and I truly think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ [al-Isra' 102]. This is a strength that shows his strength, upon him be prayers and peace.
He, may Allah the Exalted, also sent him to a stubborn people, namely the Children of Israel. For this reason, as far as we know, there is no nation among the nations like the Children of Israel in stubbornness, aversion and arrogance, to the extent that when fighting was prescribed for them, they said to Moses: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight, while we will sit here﴾, and would that they had limited themselves to that. ﴿So fight, you and your Lord, for we are sitting here﴾, we will sit on the cushions and not move, and you and your Lord go and fight. ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here﴾ [al-Ma'idah 24]. Therefore it was from wisdom that this messenger be of this degree of severity, in keeping with those to whom he was sent, from Pharaoh and the Children of Israel.
As for His saying: ﴿with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ [Ghafir 23], ﴿Our signs﴾ is plural, indicating that he had multiple signs, and so it was: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them﴾ [al-Isra' 101], and so on. He was given signs, the greatest, strongest and clearest in sensory terms of which is the sign of the staff, for it is one of Allah's wondrous and remarkable sensory signs: a staff with which he drives his sheep and in which he has other uses, and on which he leans. When he threw it, it became a great serpent that swallowed whatever was before it, and when he took hold of it, it returned to being a staff, and when he struck the rock with it, water gushed forth. This staff is a sign of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Consider now, reflect on how many staves and ropes the sorcerers threw, their abundance and variety. Then he threw this staff, and it began to swallow all that they had falsified. I wonder where the belly is that can contain these things! But the signs of Allah dazzle the minds. Otherwise you would say: how can a serpent the size of a staff swallow what they falsified of ropes and staves, so where does it go? We say: do not ask where it goes; you believe and affirm this, and how it goes to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. There is no objection to these things, when you chew them, becoming a large thing a small thing.
Allah sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority. Authority (sultan): everything by which a person has power, that is, proof and strength, and it varies according to context. Thus, for a father over his children in discipline, authority is the authority of striking; the authority for those called to Allah is the authority of clarification; and the authority for one who is disputed with is the authority of proof. It varies according to places. The point is that whatever gives a person power over others is authority.
His saying: ﴿clear﴾ may be intransitive, and it may be transitive, for the quadriliteral (abana) is both intransitive and transitive. You say: "abantu lahu al-haqq" (I made the truth clear to him), and you say: "aban al-subh" (the morning became clear), that is, it became evident and manifest. So it is a quadriliteral verb suitable for both transitivity and intransitivity.
If someone says: how can one verb be suitable for both transitivity and intransitivity? We say: yes, it is possible; the Arabic language is broad. (raja'a) is a past-tense triliteral verb that is intransitive and transitive: ﴿They say: If we return to Medina﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. Is this intransitive or transitive? Intransitive. ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾ [al-Tawbah 83]. This is transitive. So there is no objection to a single verb being intransitive in one context and transitive in another context, and (aban) is of this kind. So is His saying, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿and a clear authority﴾ meaning "clear", or "making clear, manifesting the truth"?
Let us consider which is more eloquent: that which is clear in itself, or that which makes clear to others? The second, for that which makes clear to others must itself be clear. On this basis, the word (mubin) in the transitive sense is more comprehensive and broader in meaning, and what is more comprehensive and broader in meaning is adopted, and we do not say that the second is abandoned. If we adopt the more comprehensive and broader, we do not say that it has abandoned the second, why? Because the second is included in the first.
* In this noble verse there are benefits, among them: (...) the mission of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, with the three emphatics we mentioned just now: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs﴾ [Ghafir 23].
* And among the benefits of the verse: that Allah, glory be to Him, repeats the mention of the story of Moses, sometimes expanding it, sometimes condensing it, and varying it. It combines abundance with variety in terms of style, and variety in terms of expansion and brevity. Why? Because the Prophet ﷺ lived among polytheist people at the beginning of the message, and among Jewish people after the hijrah. For this reason the Meccan surahs mention the story of Moses sometimes at length and sometimes briefly, in order that the Prophet ﷺ be prepared to dispute with the Jews, among whom the hijrah would be to a land they inhabited. For this reason you will not find the story of any prophet (...) the story of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, neither in its variety, nor its repetition, nor its style.
* From the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of Moses, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through what Allah honoured him with, namely the message.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that Moses, upon him be peace, was given signs, and Allah the Exalted explained in other verses that they were nine signs.
* And among its benefits: that Moses was given authority, that is, power and strength in establishing proof and in other matters; as His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾ shows.
If you want to know something of the authority Allah gave him, look at his debate in Surah al-Shu'ara' with Pharaoh, where he silenced him and made him swallow a stone. At the end, he threatened him with force. Pharaoh says: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29]. This is a word of intimidation. ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ is more intimidating than if he had said: "I will imprison you." It is as if he is saying: I have many prisoners, and I am able to imprison them, and I will make you among them. This is more intimidating than if he had said: "I will imprison you."
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: what we pointed out in the previous verse, that no messenger was sent except that he was given clear signs proving his truthfulness, and this is from Allah's wisdom and Allah's mercy.
* Student: Was Harun, the prophet of Allah, sent with Moses as a messenger or a prophet?
* Shaykh: No, a messenger. Did they not say to Pharaoh: "We are two messengers of the Lord of the worlds"?
* Student: "There is no prophet whom Allah has sent except that he was given signs such that mankind believed upon their like." What is the meaning of "likeness"?
* Shaykh: That is: like the signs that the messengers brought.
* Student: In number, meaning?
* Shaykh: In number or in manner.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, "such that mankind believed upon their like"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Among the prophets there is none who has not been given signs such that mankind believed upon their like, and what I was given is revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]] according to those to whom they were sent. That is, the signs that the messengers bring are such that mankind believes upon their like; meaning they are convincing signs.
* Student: Some scholars of criticism and validation (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil), when speaking about a man, say: "This man is like the staff of Moses that swallows what they falsify." Some brothers joke with it, saying to another: "You are like the staff of Moses that swallows what they falsify." Is it permissible to joke with such a thing?
* Shaykh: I see that even the scholars of hadith who say this, may Allah pardon them, should not say it like this, because it is feared that it may be used mockingly, though the hadith scholars do not intend this at all. It is better to say: "This man is, for example, a sign; this man has wide knowledge; this man has vast learning," and the like.
* Student: Truly, O Shaykh, they also say: "So-and-so possesses the magic staff of Moses."
* Shaykh: This too is not permitted; this is worse, because saying "the magic staff of Moses" means that what he brought was sorcery, and this is dangerous.
* Student: What is the evidence that Allah will judge people in half a day?
* Shaykh: First: hadiths that have come concerning this. Second: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day will be better in resting place and finer in place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan 24], and the maqil (place of repose) is only at midday.
* Student: (...) We have benefited from this verse: ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear evidences﴾ [Ghafir 22], the linking of effects to causes (...)?
* Shaykh: The ba' is for causation.
* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, what is the difference between intransitive verbs that become transitive through a preposition and those that do not?
* Shaykh: They say: whatever is transitive by itself is transitive, and whatever is only transitive through a preposition is intransitive. That is, the verb that governs a direct object is the transitive one. Some of them also said there is a second sign; it has several signs, among them this one: that it is correct to form from it the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) when it is transitive, whereas that which is only transitive with a preposition does not correctly form the passive participle except with its complement.
* Student: What is intended by the authority with which Moses was sent?
* Shaykh: Did we not say: the authority is the strength of proof, varying by context?
* Student: May Allah bless you. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have crafted﴾ [Ta-Ha 69]. From this verse, when we read it, we learn that Moses, upon him be peace, threw the staff and it ate all the serpents, and you mentioned that the serpent, whenever the sorcerers threw (...). Can we say that the things dissolved?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if the fly should steal anything from them﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. The scholars say: if it takes anything of food, no one can take it from it; that is, when the fly takes something it dissolves.
* Shaykh: No, in any case, if it enters its mouth it must dissolve quickly, but in the sight of people they see it swallowing and eating.
* Student: It eats, but it dissolves, it cannot..
* Shaykh: Perhaps; we do not know. We mentioned this; we said: perhaps.
* Student: The saying of those who said: (...) like the saying of al-Qahtani:
Allah made me a staff of Moses for you, until it swallows your falsehood, my serpent.
* Shaykh: This is by way of resemblance, by way of comparison. There is a difference between this and what the brother mentioned. This one says: it is as if I am the staff of Moses that swallows your weak and false proofs.
* Student: Some say that earlier miracles were sensory miracles beyond the usual, then when human reason developed and reached its height in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, the Qur'an came. What is your opinion?
* Shaykh: Perhaps we may say so, correct; but the Messenger ﷺ, Muhammad, brought sensory miracles and also spiritual miracles. He has great sensory miracles: the splitting of the moon is a miracle; water gushing from between his fingers is a miracle; the water welling up from the well whose water had dried up when a little of his saliva was spat into it, likewise sensory miracles. It is not far-fetched that the most complete in intellects are this Ummah, as the Messenger informed that Allah perfected morals through him.
* Student: The saying: "He is like the staff of Moses that swallows what they falsify." It is known that the scholars sometimes use expressions and intend a meaning by them; as if they are saying: he takes from liars and forgers. You objected, O Shaykh; you said: it should not be said. What is the reason for not saying it?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed; because we say that the staff of Moses, upon him be peace, became a sign that swallowed all that they falsified, and this man, whatever he is, cannot possibly (...).
* Student: O Shaykh, ﴿fa-yanzuru﴾: we have learned that the fa' of causation puts the verb in the subjunctive, and here it was not put in the subjunctive.
* Shaykh: Where is the one that was not put in the subjunctive?
* Student: ﴿fa-yanzuru﴾.
* Shaykh: It was not put in the subjunctive?!
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: How was it not put in the subjunctive?! By what are the five verbs put in the subjunctive?
* Student: By deleting the nun.
* Shaykh: By deleting the nun. And is ﴿fa-yanzuru﴾..?
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority (23), to Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun; but they said: "A sorcerer, a liar" (24). Then when he brought them the truth from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women; and the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error"﴾ [Ghafir 23–25].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾. What are the signs with which Moses was sent? How many signs?
* Student: Nine signs.
* Shaykh: Nine signs. Yes.
The ba' in His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾: what is its meaning?
* Student: For accompaniment.
* Shaykh: For accompaniment, or it explains what he was sent with, so it is for transitivity.
What is the wisdom in the signs that Allah gives to the messengers?
* Student: So that the truthfulness of these messengers is shown, so that mankind believes upon their like.
* Shaykh: As confirmation of the messengers, and as mercy toward those to whom they were sent.
His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿and a clear authority﴾? Does it mean that He sent him to be a king over Pharaoh, or what?
* Student: Authority is proof, and ﴿clear﴾ means manifest, or making manifest.
* Shaykh: Or both, and everything over which a person has power is called authority, whether it is proof, knowledge, weapons, or other things.
Enumerate for us the nine signs with which Moses was sent.
* Student: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate:
First: the staff.
Second: the hand; ﴿And insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white﴾ [al-Naml 12].
Third: the locusts.
* Shaykh: The flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and blood. How many is this?
* Student: This is seven.
* Another student: The splitting of the sea.
* Shaykh: Eight.
* Student: The loss of fruits.
* Shaykh: The years and the loss of fruits. Good. Some of them said: striking the rock with the staff so that it gushes forth.
* Student: (...).

*Shaykh:* There is some ambiguity here. For the Children of Israel, the splitting of the sea and the water gushing from the rock would be included, but these two signs were not for the people of Pharaoh. For the people of Pharaoh: the years of drought and the shortage of crops, in addition to the seven previously mentioned.

He said: ﴿To Pharaoh﴾ is connected to ﴿We sent﴾. Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt who possessed it and dominated the Children of Israel, so he would slaughter their sons and spare their women. It is said that he did this because some soothsayers (kahin, pl. kuhhan) told him: "A man will arise among the Children of Israel through whose hand your kingdom will end." This is one view.

Another view is that he did this to humiliate and degrade them, because if the men are killed and the women are left, the nation is destroyed. This view is stronger, because the first view rests on reports from the Children of Israel, and it is known that reports from the Children of Israel are neither to be affirmed nor denied. The reasonable explanation for his slaughtering their sons and sparing their women is the humiliation of this people, who were few in number compared to the Qibt (Copts).

He said: ﴿To Pharaoh﴾ is connected to ﴿We sent﴾. Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt who possessed it and dominated the Children of Israel, so he would slaughter their sons and spare their women. It is said that he did this because some soothsayers told him: "A man will arise among the Children of Israel through whose hand your kingdom will end." This is one view.

Another view is that he did this to humiliate and degrade them, because if the men are killed and the women are left, the nation is destroyed. This view is stronger, because the first view rests on reports from the Children of Israel, and it is known that reports from the Children of Israel are neither to be affirmed nor denied. The reasonable explanation for his slaughtering their sons and sparing their women is the humiliation of this people, who were few in number compared to the Copts.

﴿To Pharaoh and Haman﴾. ﴿Haman﴾ was Pharaoh's minister. ﴿And Qarun﴾ was a merchant of Pharaoh's household, because Qarun was extremely wealthy. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾ [al-Qasas 28:76], meaning gold and silver, ﴿so that its keys would weigh heavily upon a band of strong men﴾ [al-Qasas 28:76]. "Tanu'u" means "to weigh down": the band, meaning the group of strong men, would be weighed down by them. These were his keys, so his treasuries were vast and great.

﴿And Qarun. Then they said﴾: the pronoun refers to the three: Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun. ﴿Then they said: "A sorcerer, a liar"﴾. ﴿A sorcerer﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, which the exegete supplied in his words: (he is a sorcerer, a liar). "Sahir" (sorcerer) is an active participle from "sihr" (magic), and it refers to one who bewitches people so that they see realities differently from what they are. He does not change realities, for only the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, changes realities. Rather, he shows people realities in a form other than their true nature, as the sorcerers of Pharaoh's household did when they cast their ropes and staffs, and people saw them as moving like snakes, though they were not. These people said: "Moses is a sorcerer. How can he throw the staff and it becomes a serpent? How can he put his hand in and it comes out white without harm?" This is nothing but magic.

﴿Liar﴾ means one who lies in what he claims of prophethood. He is a sorcerer in his signs and a liar in his claim. Then he said ﴿liar﴾, which is either an intensive form or an attributive form. The difference between the intensive form and the attributive form is that the attributive form is a constant description, while the intensive form is a repeated, recurring act. Do you understand? The word "najjar" (carpenter) here is an attributive form, though it may be an intensive form because of how much he works as a carpenter. But when it is said that someone is "akkal lil-ta'am" (a great eater), this may not be an attribute, but because he eats a lot, he is described as a great eater.

﴿So when he came to them with the truth﴾: Allah sent him with the signs. They said: "A sorcerer, a liar." ﴿So when he came to them with the truth﴾, with the truth, ﴿from Us﴾, from Allah the Exalted, which is the revelation. When Moses, peace be upon him, said to them: "Allah is your Lord, and Allah is One," and similar matters that were discussed between him and Pharaoh, as is mentioned in Surat al-Shu'ara' and Surat al-Isra' and elsewhere.

When he came to them with the truth, which they could not counter with a refuting argument, Pharaoh threatened Moses, saying: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among those imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:29]. This is a threat. Another point: ﴿They said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women"﴾ [Ghafir 40:25]. ﴿Spare﴾ means let them live, ﴿their women﴾. On this basis, the killing of the sons of the Children of Israel and the sparing of the women occurred twice: the first time before Moses was sent, and the second time after he was sent.

﴿They said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women."﴾ Their women, so that they would have no strength left and their awe would vanish, because if only the women remained, the women are weak. They cannot defend themselves or defend their rights, so Moses and his people would be left in the worst condition.

﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women﴾, and so on.

Now let us return to derive the benefits, so as not to stray:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾.

In this noble verse there is: the affirmation of Moses's prophethood, peace be upon him. From this benefit follows the establishment of proof against the Children of Israel who disbelieved and transgressed, even though Allah had sent this noble messenger to them.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, does not send a messenger except with a clear sign that demonstrates his truthfulness. This is affirmed by the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah did not send any prophet except that He gave him of the signs that people could believe upon the like of." 

[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording is: "There was not among the prophets any prophet except that he was given of the signs what people believed in because of its like. But what I was given was a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]]

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the signs are an authority and proof upon those to whom the messengers were sent, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾. On this basis, the mention of "authority" after "signs" is the conjoining of a thing with itself, to show its benefit and fruit; the signs are the authority.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the signs must be clear and manifest the truth, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and a clear authority﴾.

Then He said: ﴿To Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun﴾, and so on.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: leaders stand in the place of followers, because the message was not to these three alone, but to all the people of Pharaoh. Rather, the chiefs stand in the place of the followers.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the stubborn opponents of the messengers have varied causes for their obstinacy and opposition to the messengers. It may be authority, it may be office, it may be wealth, it may be physical strength. In this verse there are three causes: kingship, the second is office (ministry), and the third is wealth. Among 'Ad, who had physical strength, they said: ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 41:15].

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obstinacy of those who deny the messengers, for they said to this noble messenger: he is a sorcerer and he is a liar.

Among its benefits: what they said in rejecting the call is mere assertion, because they did not establish any evidence for their claim. They merely said: "A sorcerer, a liar." This is what weak and incapable people resort to when they cannot counter argument with argument, so they turn to abuse, insults and similar things.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the signs brought by the prophets are beyond the ability of ordinary people, as shown by His saying: ﴿sorcerer﴾, and a sorcerer is one who brings about matters that overwhelm people. But the difference between the sorcerer and the prophet is that the prophet is supported by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not by his own action. That is, the sorcerer is one who works on a thing until he brings a miracle, whereas for the prophet, the signs come to him without any action of his own, but by the will of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. If someone says: "Then what is the difference between a karamah (a miraculous gift granted to a righteous servant) and a sign of a prophet?"

We say: the difference between them is that the karamah comes to a follower of the prophet, whereas the sign comes to the prophet himself. That is, one whom Allah grants a karamah from among the saints does not claim to be a messenger or a prophet, but Allah grants him the karamah as confirmation for him or as confirmation for Islam. In that there is also a sign for the prophet whom he follows.

Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: (﴿And the plotting of the disbelievers is nothing but in misguidance﴾ — destruction). (Mā) is negating. Is ﴿kayd﴾ the subject (mubtada') or do we make it its subject? ﴿Kayd﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and it is not valid for it to be its subject, because one of the conditions for (mā) to operate like (laysa) is that the negation not be nullified. Ibn Mālik said:

.............................. ∗∗∗ maʿa baqā l-nafyi wa-tartībin zukin

So when the negation is nullified, it does not operate like (mā). The Noble Qur'an contains much of this: ﴿This is nothing but a human like you﴾ [al-Mu'minun 24], and it did not say "mā hādhā illā basharan," because the negation was nullified.

So (mā) is negating, and ﴿kayd﴾ is the subject: ﴿the plotting of the disbelievers﴾. What is kayd? Kayd, makr (scheming), khadā' (deception) and what resembles them are all closely related words whose meaning is reaching the harming of the adversary from a place he does not perceive — that is, one reaches the harming of his opponent through hidden means that the opponent does not notice. This is because the one who plots, schemes or deceives does not bring about the thing openly in this manner, but through hidden means. So it is reaching the harming of the opponent from where he does not perceive, i.e., through hidden means.

So the disbelievers have a great plotting against Islam, and they plot against Islam rather than for it. There is a difference between plotting "against" something and plotting "for" something. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Thus did We devise for Yusuf﴾ [Yusuf 76], and He did not say "ʿalā" (against). But plotting against an enemy is called kayd against him. The disbelievers have plotting against the messengers; they plot a great plot and do every means by which they hope to refute the messengers' proof. But however much they work, Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿except in misguidance﴾ — their plotting is in misguidance, that is, in destruction and loss, just as the one who is astray is not guided to the path; likewise, the plotting of these disbelievers does not bring them to their goal.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Mūsā (peace be upon him) brought the truth to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn, and this shows that he proclaimed it openly before them.

* Among its benefits: these deniers were unable to refute the truth he brought, so they did not match the proof with its like.

* Among its benefits: these three resorted to killing and threats; they said: ﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him﴾.

* Among its benefits: that those who protect and defend the homeland are men, and that a woman is not the one who defends the city or repels the enemy; the evidence for this is that these said: ﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the complete partisanship of the disbelievers; meaning that they are partisan, for they say: ﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him﴾; that is, do not kill the non-believers among the Children of Israel; kill the sons of those who believe.

* Among its benefits: Allah, may He be exalted, may give His enemies power over the believers as a trial and test, and reality confirms this; and the more a person's faith grows strong, the more the enemies of Allah may harm him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the disbelievers plot against the believers, by His saying: ﴿And the plotting of the disbelievers is nothing but in misguidance﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the judgment that these three are disbelievers; for this reason it did not say "wa-mā kaydahum," but rather used the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, as a sign that these are disbelievers. We have previously mentioned that using the explicit in place of the pronoun yields two benefits:

The first benefit: the judgment upon those whose pronoun the explicit noun replaces, with this description.

The second: generality and comprehensiveness.

The third: indicating causation. ﴿And the plotting of the disbelievers is nothing but in misguidance﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: complete good tidings to the believers that however much the disbelievers plot, their plotting is lost and perishing; it will not benefit them, and they will gain nothing from it; and if they do gain, they gain only a temporary benefit, while the final outcome belongs to the righteous.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord."﴾ [Ghafir 26] I seek refuge in Allah! They had proposed that the sons of the Children of Israel be killed and their women spared, but Pharaoh said: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord.﴾ That is, "Leave me to kill Moses." He said this because Moses was the leader of the Children of Israel, and it is well known that killing a leader weakens and debilitates his followers.

In his saying ﴿Leave me to kill Moses﴾ ("leave me") there is evidence of Pharaoh's deception, and that he was a deceitful, scheming, wicked man.
