* Shaykh: He sees that he is being punished?
* Student: Sometimes a person sees (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is not derived from this, but it is used to refute the claim of the atheists, who said: "You say that the dead person is seated in his grave and punished, yet we dig the grave and find the dead person remains as he was?" So we respond to them: this sleeper sees that he is punished, that he is blessed, that he went and came back while on his bed without changing, even the blanket has not slipped off his back. So we say: measure the unseen by the seen. Then, if the punishment of the grave were perceived by observing it, it would not be faith in the unseen but faith in the witnessed, and faith in the witnessed does not benefit; that is, when a person witnesses a thing, his faith in it does not benefit...
Student: The punishment of the grave when a person sees it in his sleep.
* Shaykh: What does he see?
* Student: In dreams.
* Shaykh: He sees that he is punished?
* Student: A person sleeps and sees (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not derived from this, but it is used to refute the claim of the atheists who said: "You say that the dead person is seated in his grave and punished, yet we dig the grave and find the dead person remains as he was." So we respond to them that this sleeper sees that he is punished, blessed, that he went and came back while on his bed without change, even the blanket has not fallen from his back. We say: measure the unseen by the seen. Then, if the punishment of the grave were perceived by observing it, it would not be faith in the unseen but faith in the witnessed, and faith in the witnessed does not benefit. That is: when a person witnesses a thing, his faith in it does not benefit. You see disbelievers at the approach of death; they believe, but that does not benefit them. When Pharaoh was overtaken by drowning, he said: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims﴾ [Yunus 90]. See how far this goes: he acknowledged Allah's Oneness, then acknowledged that he was a follower of the Children of Israel, by His saying: ﴿in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, and he did not say "that there is no god but Allah," indicating that he became humbled until he became a follower of the Children of Israel after having been tyrannical over them.
* Student: Some Muslims console a disbeliever.
* Shaykh: That is, some Muslims console them?
* Student: Yes.
The scholars say: there is no harm, there is no harm in consoling a disbeliever. Some of them say it is not permissible, and some made a distinction, saying: if they do this to us, we do it, relying on Allah's saying: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it, or return it﴾ [An-Nisa 86]. This is closer to the truth: that if they do that to us, we do it.
But do we say: "may Allah magnify your reward, grant you good consolation, and forgive your deceased"? No, we do not say this. We say: "May Allah guide you to Islam and compensate you for your calamity," and that is all. And for the deceased we do not say "may Allah forgive him" or "he is among the people of the Fire."
* Student: Shaykh, the saying of one of the Companions to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I asked Allah the Exalted to let me see Umar in a dream," and he did not see Umar until a full year had passed (...). Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said (...). What is your view on this matter?
* Shaykh: Our statement is: this is more false than falsehood. How many widespread things are false! Umar ibn al-Khattab was killed as a martyr, and martyrdom expiates everything, everything except debt, and we do not know that he had debts.
* Student: In some Arab countries, Christians who are Arabs place a recording device inside the grave, saying: "We want to verify whether your claim, O Muslims, that the punishment of the grave and the bliss of the grave are established, is true. We want to verify this, and I do not want (...) the Qur'an or the Sunnah, but I want my intellect to judge whether this is correct or not. So what do we say to them?"
* Shaykh: So that he hears the screaming of the dead?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: We say: If Allah wished you to hear it through a recorder, He would have made you hear it with your own ears. Why a recorder? It has no need.
But when this act occurs, do we accept this act with them?
* Shaykh: We say: you are not believing me.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: If Allah wished us to hear it, we would have heard it without a recorder. Yes.
* Student: Can we consider His saying: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir 46] as an explanation of His saying: ﴿the evil of the punishment﴾?
* Shaykh: This is possible, and it is possible to say that the evil of the punishment is what we mentioned in the tafsir. As for ﴿the Fire﴾, it is a resumptive clause mentioned on its own.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said, in the rest of the speech of this believing man: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ [Ghafir 44]. (The particle *sa-* (*al-sin*) and *sawfa* both restrict the verb to the imperfect (*mudari'*). Among its signs is that any word that accepts *al-sin* or *sawfa* is an imperfect verb.) However, they differ. *Al-sin* indicates nearness, and *sawfa* indicates a delay. So His saying ﴿fa-satadhkurūn﴾ means "soon." Along with indicating nearness, it also indicates certainty, meaning that this is a matter that must occur. ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ when? When you witness the punishment. This is not far off, because the most that lies between them and it is that their appointed terms end, and everything that is coming is near. ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you.﴾ Will that benefit them at that time or not? It will not benefit them, just as when a counselor advises you to refrain from doing something, and you do not accept his advice, and then afterward you see its consequences are harmful, you will remember the counselor's words, remembering them with regret and sorrow.

He said: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ [Ghafir 44]. The *wāw* here is *istīnāf* (resumptive, beginning a new sentence), and it cannot be conjunctive (*'ātifah*), because if it were conjunctive the meaning would be "And I will entrust my affair to Allah," but that is not the meaning. Rather, the meaning is "And I entrust my affair to Allah." So the *wāw* here is resumptive: I entrust it to Allah, that is, I leave it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿amrī﴾ is a singular noun in the construct state (*mufrad mudāf*) that is general in meaning, and what is intended by it is the matter, that is, the whole affair ﴿to Allah﴾. This is the utmost degree of *tawakkul* (complete reliance upon Allah).

﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ [Ghafir 44]. This sentence is causal (*ta'līliyyah*) for the previous ruling, which is His saying "I entrust my affair to Allah." It is as if someone were to say: why did he entrust his affair to Allah? So the answer was that Allah, exalted is He, is Seeing of the servants.

﴿Seeing of the servants﴾ means: of their conditions, their present and their future, and all their affairs. He, glorified and exalted, knows what is before them and what is behind them. He knows all their conditions.

He said this when they threatened him with opposing his religion. That is, it is as if they threatened him, and he said: "I entrust my affair to Allah." However, the threat is not indicated in the verse, and the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that he did not say this when they threatened him, but rather he said it when he despaired that they would comply with his advice. So he said, like one bidding them farewell: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾. As for me, ﴿I entrust my affair to Allah﴾, because I have fulfilled what was incumbent upon me of advice, and this is the most that is obligatory upon me.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾ [Ghafir 45]. This also indicates a rejection of the author's statement, because if they had threatened him with killing, that would not have been a *makr* (scheming). Scheming is inflicting harm on someone from a direction he does not perceive. That is *makr*: that you harm your counterpart from a direction he does not perceive. But if they had threatened him with killing, this would not have been *makr*; rather, it would have been explicit and clear.

﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾ means: He saved him from their evil scheming. The word ﴿sayyi'āt﴾ here is an instance of the adjective being attached to its noun (*idāfat al-ṣifah ila mawṣūfihā*), meaning "the evil scheming." Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir 43].

His saying ﴿mā makarū﴾: *makr* (scheming), *khida'* (deception), *ghadr* (treachery), *mihāl* (cunning), and similar words are all close in meaning and revolve around one thing, which is to inflict harm on someone from a direction he does not perceive.

﴿mā makarū﴾: he said (by the author), "with it, of killing." In this he explained that the returning pronoun to the relative clause in His saying *mā* is omitted, and the estimate is: "what they schemed with."

He said: (﴿And there surrounded﴾ [means] "descended upon" ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning his people with him, ﴿the terrible punishment﴾, which is drowning.) *Ḥāqa* means "descended," but you sense that it is not synonymous with "descended" in every respect, and that explaining it as "descended" is an approximate explanation. The letter *qāf* in *ḥāqa* is close to *ṭā'*, so the meaning is as if it were *ḥāṭa bihim* (encompassed them), and this is stronger than "descended." So the apparent meaning of *ḥāqa* is "descended, encompassing them," and it is not merely "descended" without additional meaning.

His saying ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾: the author said "his people." Others said "his followers." The apparent meaning is that the two meanings are close, because those who followed him were only his people. As for the Children of Israel, they did not follow him; rather, he used to slaughter their sons and spare their women.

His saying (﴿with him﴾) he mentioned to prevent someone from supposing that the punishment descended upon the people of Pharaoh without him. But this is absolutely impossible, since if the people of Pharaoh were struck with punishment, it was because they disbelieved in Allah, and Pharaoh was more disbelieving in Allah than they were. Moreover, the apparent meaning is that when a person says "Honor the family of so-and-so," so-and-so is their leader and must be included among them, linguistically.

His saying ﴿terrible punishment﴾ is also an instance of the adjective attached to its noun, meaning "the evil punishment." The author explained it as drowning, and there is no doubt that this is among the evil punishments. But there were other punishments that the people of Pharaoh suffered: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years [of drought] and a shortage of fruits, that they might be reminded﴾ [Al-A'raf 130]. And He said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and blood﴾ [Al-A'raf 133]. All of this is among the evil punishments. The flood drowned what had been sown of their crops; the lice were to ruin what had sprouted; the frogs were to contaminate the water, because whenever they took a vessel to drink from, they found these frogs had filled it. As for blood, it is bleeding of the blood, either from the nose or from elsewhere. Thus they were punished in every respect: their crops drowned, what they had stored was infested with lice, the water was filled with frogs, and after the food reached the body and the body was nourished by it, it was expelled as blood flowing out. So they perished.

This involves an order and degrees. What did we say? The flood drowned the crops, the locusts consumed what had appeared, the flood and the locusts consume the crops; the flood drowns what was sown, and the locusts eat what had appeared, and the lice ruin what was stored, and the frogs contaminate the water, and blood, which is bleeding, dissipates what was gained from the food, by the food that one assumes has escaped these afflictions. This is among the evil punishments, and the final outcome was drowning, that Allah drowned the people of Pharaoh in the sea.

He said: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir 46]. This sentence is resumptive (*mustaʾnafah*), so ﴿al-nār﴾ (the Fire) is the subject (*mubtada'*), and ﴿yu'raḍūna﴾ (they are exposed) is the predicate sentence.

﴿They are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ does not mean that it burns them, because if Allah had intended that, He would have said "they will burn in it morning and evening." Rather, they are presented to it, so there comes to them from its scorching and punishment what they cannot bear, may Allah protect us. They are exposed to it in the morning (*ghudūwan*) and in the evening (*'ashiyyan*). The apparent meaning is that what is intended is continuity. It is possible that what is intended is only these two times. As for the first, it may be supported by the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening﴾ [Maryam 62], meaning throughout all time.

As for the second, it may be said that this is the apparent wording, meaning at the beginning of the day and at its end, and that they are exposed to the Fire at the beginning of the day, then when they are turned away from it, they hope that it will not return to them, and then it returns to them. This is worse than continuity, because a person's hoping that the punishment will be lifted from him and then its return is more severe than being constantly in it and despairing of its removal. For this reason Allah said to the people of the Fire: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it﴾ [As-Sajdah 20].

﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour is established﴾ [Ghafir 46]. It is said: ﴿Enter, O people of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment﴾. This is a reading, and "Enter" (*udkhulū*) is an imperative, and what is intended by it is humiliation and degradation. This is unlike His saying, exalted is He, to the people of Paradise: ﴿Enter it in peace, secure﴾ [Al-Hijr 46]; that is for honor. But this: ﴿Enter, O people of Pharaoh﴾ is for humiliation, may Allah protect us.

As for His saying ﴿Āl﴾ (people of), the author explained it by saying "O people of" (*yā āl*), indicating that it is in the accusative by the omitted vocative particle *yā*: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh." (And in one reading, with the *hamzah* opened and the *khā'* kasra, it is a command to the angels: ﴿Cause the people of Pharaoh to enter﴾.) That is, on the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the angels: cause the people of Pharaoh to enter ﴿the most severe punishment﴾, which is the punishment of Hell. We ask Allah for well-being.

Among the benefits in these verses:

First: that Allah, glorified and exalted, is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him, as He said: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you, and I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ [Ghafir 44].

* Among the benefits of these verses: First, a warning about those whom the believer advises, that they will remember his words and recognize that it is the truth, but when? At a time when this remembrance will not benefit them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strength of the believer's *tawakkul*, where he said: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾. Thus it is obligatory for every believer, when he wants his affairs to be resolved and made easy, to entrust his affair to Allah, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [At-Talaq 3], and He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers﴾ [Al-Anfal 64]. Whoever has Allah as his sufficiency is victorious and successful.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, glorified and exalted, of all His servants, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ [Ghafir 44]. This, as I told you, is an explanation that encompasses conditions and essences.

* Among the benefits of the following verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted, suffices whoever relies upon Him, and protects him from his enemy, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾ [Ghafir 45].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against the enemies of the Muslims, from His saying ﴿what they plotted﴾, and that the enemies of the Muslims may not confront them with hostility but may scheme against them. So the believer should beware of the scheming of Allah's enemies. This is abundant in the Qur'an. Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of the planners﴾ [Al-Anfal 30]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot. And I am plotting a plot. So give time to the disbelievers; give them time for a little﴾ [At-Tariq 15–17].

And among the scheming of Allah's enemies is that they do not confront the Muslims with hostility, but they invade them from directions they do not perceive, with deviant ideas and corrupt morals, as you now observe and hear what the enemies of the Muslims do to the Muslims. They drag into them base morals through visual, printed and audio media, and they send to them everything that opposes the religion of Islam in clothing and in other matters, and they lure them with enormous wealth to waste their time in vain and without benefit, such as the matter of sports and similar things. The point is that the enemies of the Muslims scheme against them with a tremendous scheme, and the Muslims either do not pay attention to this scheme or do not recognize it. But in any case, it is our duty to be cautious.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, exalted is He, rewards the doer of good for his good, and rewards the doer of evil for his evil, and the reward of the evildoer for his evil is in reality a reward for the doer of good, because the punishment of your enemies is in reality a victory for you, and you rejoice in it. This is derived from His saying: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and there surrounded the people of Pharaoh the evil punishment﴾ [Ghafir 45], where Allah explained the recompense for this and the recompense for those.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the punishment of the grave, from His saying: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir 46].

The punishment of the grave is established by the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus (*ijma'*). As for the Qur'an: in verses like this one: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾. Then He said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, [it will be said], "Enter"﴾ [Ghafir 46]. Because His saying "the day" (*yawm*) is a temporal adverb (*ẓarf zamān*) connected to what follows it, namely the verb ﴿udkhulū﴾ or ﴿udkhulū﴾, and this therefore can only be after the Day of Resurrection. Their being exposed to the Fire morning and evening occurs before the Day of Resurrection. So this indicates the affirmation of the punishment of the grave. I told you that it is established by the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus. As for the Qur'an, it is in verses like this.

And from it (i.e., from the evidences of the Qur'an) is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿If you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are extending their hands, [saying], "Discharge your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation"﴾ [Al-An'am 93]. ﴿Today⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ...﴾ when? "Today" here is *al* for the known presence (*al-'ahd al-ḥuḍūrī*), meaning this day, which is the day of your death. This indicates the establishment of the punishment of the grave.

As for the Sunnah, it is mutawatir (successively transmitted) concerning this, abundant in various forms, general and specific. Among the specific ones is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ when he passed by two graves being punished: "Indeed, they are being punished, and they are not being punished for a great matter." (Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6055) and Muslim (292/111), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.)

As for the consensus, all Muslims say in their prayers: "I seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of Hell and from the punishment of the grave." This is a matter with no difficulty in it, and it is part of our creed.

If someone says: is the punishment upon the body, or upon the soul, or upon both together?

We say: the apparent meaning of the Sunnah is that the punishment is upon the body during the questioning by the two angels. The Prophet ﷺ informed that the hypocrite and the doubter say: "I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it." Then he is struck with an iron mace, and he cries out with a cry that everything hears except the two jinn and humans; they do not hear it, and everything hears it. (Abu Dawud (4751) with his chain of narration from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ entered a palm grove of the Banu al-Najjar and heard a sound and was alarmed, and he said: "Who are the companions of these graves?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, people who died in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire and from the trial of the Dajjal." They said: "And why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Indeed, when the believer is placed in his grave, an angel comes to him and says: 'What did you worship?' If Allah has guided him, he says: 'I worshipped Allah.' It is said to him: 'What did you say about this man?' He says: 'He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger,' and he is not asked about anything other than that. Then he is taken to a house he had in the Fire, and it is said to him: 'This was your house in the Fire, but Allah protected you and had mercy on you, so He has replaced it for you with a house in Paradise.' He says: 'Let me go and give my family good news,' and it is said to him: 'Be still.' As for the disbeliever, when he is placed in his grave, an angel comes to him and rebukes him, and says: 'What did you worship?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, and you did not recite.' It is said to him: 'What did you say about this man?' He says: 'I said what the people said.' Then he is struck with an iron hammer between his ears, and he cries out a cry that everyone hears except the two jinn and humans.") What is meant by this is those close enough to hear it; as for those in the distant regions of the world, no. This indicates that what is punished during the questioning is the body, by His saying (the narration): "He is struck."

After that, the principle is that the punishment is upon the soul, although it may be connected to the body, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said. If we wish, we may say: this is a discussion of no benefit, and the Companions did not ask about it. So we affirm the punishment of the grave according to what came in the Book and the Sunnah, neither adding nor subtracting.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the existence of the Fire, from His saying: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir 46]. Its existence is established in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ saw the Fire when it was displayed to him while he was leading the people in the eclipse prayer, and he saw in it those who were being punished. So the Fire exists now.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the establishment of the Hour, from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established﴾ [Ghafir 46].

We believe in the Hour, that it will certainly come, and that people will be resurrected. From this we know that what some people say today when a man dies and is buried, such as "they took him to his final resting place," is a word of disbelief (kufr). If you say "to his final resting place," this means there is no resurrection after that and that this is the last stage for a human being, and the matter is not so. Therefore we say: whoever says this word, knowing its meaning and intending it, is a disbeliever, because he denies the resurrection. As for one who says it and means "in terms of the visible world," this is correct, but the apparent meaning of the expression is disbelief, so it is obligatory to avoid it. One may say, for example: "they took him to his grave, they took him to the place of his visiting."
Is it correct or incorrect?
* Student: If what is meant is (...).
* Shaykh: In reality the grave is a place of visiting. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾ [At-Takathur 1-2]. When a Bedouin heard a man reciting it, he said: "By Allah, the visitor is not one who settles down," meaning that there is something beyond this grave. He spoke the truth: the visitor is not one who settles; he visits and then walks away.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the humiliation of the disbelievers, both physical and in the heart. From where is this taken? From rebuking and humiliating them: ﴿Enter, O people of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir 46]. There is no doubt that their hearts are affected by this, and you will find regret and remorse, and we seek refuge in Allah.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the rebuke of the people of Pharaoh. It is as if He said: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh, and see whether it benefits you to be among his people or not." So there is in it a kind of reproach for them.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Fire is the most severe punishment, and that everything before it is lighter than it, from His saying: ﴿the most severe punishment﴾. There is no doubt that it is the most severe punishment. Likewise we say regarding bliss: what the believer finds of bliss in the grave is nothing compared to what he finds on the Day of Resurrection. The complete bliss is by entering Paradise, and what precedes it is like an introduction before it.
* Student: Can one derive from (...) that a person sees in his dream?
* Shaykh: What does he see? Does he see that he is being punished?
* Student: In dreams, he...
* Shaykh: He sees that he is being punished?
* Student: Sometimes a person sees (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is not derived from this, but it is used to refute the claim of the atheists, who said: "You say that the dead person is seated in his grave and punished, yet we dig the grave and find the dead person remains as he was?" So we respond to them: this sleeper sees that he is punished, that he is blessed, that he went and came back while on his bed without changing, even the blanket has not slipped off his back. So we say: measure the unseen by the seen. Then, if the punishment of the grave were perceived by observing it, it would not be faith in the unseen but faith in the witnessed, and faith in the witnessed does not benefit; that is, when a person witnesses a thing, his faith in it does not benefit...
Student: The punishment of the grave when a person sees it in his sleep.
* Shaykh: What does he see?
* Student: In dreams.
* Shaykh: He sees that he is punished?
* Student: A person sleeps and sees (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not derived from this, but it is used to refute the claim of the atheists who said: "You say that the dead person is seated in his grave and punished, yet we dig the grave and find the dead person remains as he was." So we respond to them that this sleeper sees that he is punished, blessed, that he went and came back while on his bed without change, even the blanket has not fallen from his back. We say: measure the unseen by the seen. Then, if the punishment of the grave were perceived by observing it, it would not be faith in the unseen but faith in the witnessed, and faith in the witnessed does not benefit. That is: when a person witnesses a thing, his faith in it does not benefit. You see disbelievers at the approach of death; they believe, but that does not benefit them. When Pharaoh was overtaken by drowning, he said: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims﴾ [Yunus 90]. See how far this goes: he acknowledged Allah's Oneness, then acknowledged that he was a follower of the Children of Israel, by His saying: ﴿in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, and he did not say "that there is no god but Allah," indicating that he became humbled until he became a follower of the Children of Israel after having been tyrannical over them.
* Student: Some Muslims console a disbeliever.
* Shaykh: That is, some Muslims console them?
* Student: Yes.
The scholars say: there is no harm, there is no harm in consoling a disbeliever. Some of them say it is not permissible, and some made a distinction, saying: if they do this to us, we do it, relying on Allah's saying: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it, or return it﴾ [An-Nisa 86]. This is closer to the truth: that if they do that to us, we do it.
But do we say: "may Allah magnify your reward, grant you good consolation, and forgive your deceased"? No, we do not say this. We say: "May Allah guide you to Islam and compensate you for your calamity," and that is all. And for the deceased we do not say "may Allah forgive him" or "he is among the people of the Fire."
* Student: Shaykh, the saying of one of the Companions to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I asked Allah the Exalted to let me see Umar in a dream," and he did not see Umar until a full year had passed (...). Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said (...). What is your view on this matter?
* Shaykh: Our statement is: this is more false than falsehood. How many widespread things are false! Umar ibn al-Khattab was killed as a martyr, and martyrdom expiates everything, everything except debt, and we do not know that he had debts.
* Student: In some Arab countries, Christians who are Arabs place a recording device inside the grave, saying: "We want to verify whether your claim, O Muslims, that the punishment of the grave and the bliss of the grave are established, is true. We want to verify this, and I do not want (...) the Qur'an or the Sunnah, but I want my intellect to judge whether this is correct or not. So what do we say to them?"
* Shaykh: So that he hears the screaming of the dead?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: We say: If Allah wished you to hear it through a recorder, He would have made you hear it with your own ears. Why a recorder? It has no need.
But when this act occurs, do we accept this act with them?
* Shaykh: We say: you are not believing me.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: If Allah wished us to hear it, we would have heard it without a recorder. Yes.
* Student: Can we consider His saying: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir 46] as an explanation of His saying: ﴿the evil of the punishment﴾?
* Shaykh: This is possible, and it is possible to say that the evil of the punishment is what we mentioned in the tafsir. As for ﴿the Fire﴾, it is a resumptive clause mentioned on its own.

**Student:** ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us any portion of the Fire?" (47) Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants." (48) And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment." (49) They will say, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidence?" They will say, "Yes." They will say, "Then call," but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error. (50) Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand. (51) The day when the excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil home.﴾ [Ghafir 47–52].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾. ﴿When they argue﴾ means: remember when they argue in the Fire, that is, each one of them presents his argument. The word (idh) (when) is an adverb whose governing verb is omitted, which the author (al-Mu'allif) estimated with his words: (remember ﴿when they argue﴾).

The *muhajja* (mutual dispute) is the contention and each one presenting his argument against the other. His words ﴿in the Fire﴾ indicate that these disputants are the people of the Fire, and the phrase is connected to ﴿they argue﴾. Then he explained this argument, saying: ﴿the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾. The weak may be weak in wealth, or in status and leadership, or in other respects that are considered weakness, and it is generally the case that the weak follows the strong.

His words ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ mean: those who showed pride, from *kibriya'* (greatness and pride), and the *sin* and *ta'* in it (*istakbaru*) are for emphasis.

﴿Indeed, we were﴾ means: in the worldly life, ﴿your followers﴾, the plural of *tabi'* (follower); that is, we were following you.

﴿So can you avail us any portion of the Fire?﴾ means: Will you repay us for our following you by bearing for us some of the Fire?

His words ﴿so can you avail﴾: the commentator said: (repelling) ﴿for us any portion﴾, a part, ﴿of the Fire﴾. Consider how these weak ones seek a means of intercession to those who were arrogant, how they plead with them by the following they had offered, so that they might bear for them a portion of the Fire. The answer of those who were arrogant was:

﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir 48]. If we are all in it, how can we avail you? How can we avail you any portion of the Fire? This is an argument to state the reality.

His words ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾ mean that He judged between them by His judgment of recompense, because the judgments of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are three: *qadari* (decreed), *shar'i* (legislated), and *jaza'i* (of recompense). The judgment of recompense is in reality part of the decreed judgment, but some scholars treat it separately because of its importance, since it is the ultimate purpose. His words ﴿judged between the servants﴾ mean: between people in general, between the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise. Here, "servitude" carries the general, all-encompassing meaning, since servitude is both general and specific.

* **So in this verse there are benefits:**

* Among them: the enmity of the disbelievers toward one another, and that the strong among them show no mercy to the weak; by His saying ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these disbelievers presented to their leaders a favor, that they had been their followers, in order to seek by it a means to have them bear for them a portion of the Fire. In this is evidence of a person seeking a means by a good deed he has done for another. But is this considered a reminder of favor (*minnah*)?

In reality, what shows whether it is a means (*tawassul*) or a reminder of favor (*minnah*) are the circumstances. It may be a reminder of favor, or it may be a means. If one says: "Just as I showed you mercy, gave you, and was good to you, so be good to me," this falls under the category of seeking a means.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the weak are always followers of the strong; by His saying ﴿so the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾. For this reason it becomes clear to us now that the imitation of the Muslims of the disbelievers signifies their weakness before them, because the weak always imitates the strong due to the weakness of his personality before him. And it is obligatory upon the Muslims to have a distinctive character of their own, and to have their own inherent strength, because strength is with them: they are the people of religion, the people of truth, those who know life, and in reality they are the people of life.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these followers wish that the leaders would take on some portion, even a little, of the punishment of the Fire on their behalf. The evidence that they want even a little is their saying: ﴿a portion﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the arrogant make the excuse that they have no power to do this, because all are in the Hellfire; so how could they take on a portion on their behalf? Yes, if they were not in the Hellfire and then were cast into the Fire for the purpose of relieving those a portion, it would be possible; but since all are in the Fire, the request for this to be realized is a request for something impossible.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the humiliation of these arrogant ones on the Day of Resurrection; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, all of us are in it﴾, meaning: now we have no superiority over you, and you have no superiority over us; all are in the Hellfire.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by these tormented ones in the Fire that Allah, glorified and exalted, has judged between the servants with a just judgment; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾.

* Among its benefits: that when the judgment of Allah is executed, it cannot be lifted or repelled; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged﴾. On this, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in Surah Qaf: ﴿Do not dispute before Me, for I had already sent to you the warning. The word is not changed before Me, and I am not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Qaf 28–29]. When the judgment of Allah is concluded, there is no repeal of His judgment.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by these tormented ones in the Hellfire that they are servants of Allah; but what is meant is the general servitude, which is the *kawni* (universal, existential) servitude. Servitude is of two kinds: the general, which is the universal servitude (*al-ubudiyya al-kawniyya*), and the specific, which is the legislated servitude (*al-ubudiyya al-shar'iyya*). Whoever submits to Allah in the legislated sense is a worshipper in the legislated sense, and likewise in the universal sense; whoever is arrogant toward worshipping Allah in the legislated sense is a worshipper in the universal sense and not a worshipper in the legislated sense.

The commentator said: (so He admitted the believers into Paradise and the disbelievers into the Fire). The meaning is more general than what he (may Allah have mercy on him) said. ﴿He judged between the servants﴾: between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and between the people of the Fire among themselves, and He judged with a general judgment.

**Student:** ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us any portion of the Fire?" (47) Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants." (48) And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment." (49) They will say, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidence?" They will say, "Yes." They will say, "Then call," but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error. (50) Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand. (51) The day when the excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil home.﴾ [Ghafir 47–52].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾. ﴿When they argue﴾ means: remember when they argue in the Fire, that is, each one of them presents his argument. The word (idh) (when) is an adverb whose governing verb is omitted, which the author (al-Mu'allif) estimated with his words: (remember ﴿when they argue﴾).

The *muhajja* (mutual dispute) is the contention and each one presenting his argument against the other. His words ﴿in the Fire﴾ indicate that these disputants are the people of the Fire, and the phrase is connected to ﴿they argue﴾. Then he explained this argument, saying: ﴿the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾. The weak may be weak in wealth, or in status and leadership, or in other respects that are considered weakness, and it is generally the case that the weak follows the strong.

His words ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ mean: those who showed pride, from *kibriya'* (greatness and pride), and the *sin* and *ta'* in it (*istakbaru*) are for emphasis.

﴿Indeed, we were﴾ means: in the worldly life, ﴿your followers﴾, the plural of *tabi'* (follower); that is, we were following you.

﴿So can you avail us any portion of the Fire?﴾ means: Will you repay us for our following you by bearing for us some of the Fire?

His words ﴿so can you avail﴾: the commentator said: (repelling) ﴿for us any portion﴾, a part, ﴿of the Fire﴾. Consider how these weak ones seek a means of intercession to those who were arrogant, how they plead with them by the following they had offered, so that they might bear for them a portion of the Fire. The answer of those who were arrogant was:

﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir 48]. If we are all in it, how can we avail you? How can we avail you any portion of the Fire? This is an argument to state the reality.

His words ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾ mean that He judged between them by His judgment of recompense, because the judgments of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are three: *qadari* (decreed), *shar'i* (legislated), and *jaza'i* (of recompense). The judgment of recompense is in reality part of the decreed judgment, but some scholars treat it separately because of its importance, since it is the ultimate purpose. His words ﴿judged between the servants﴾ mean: between people in general, between the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise. Here, "servitude" carries the general, all-encompassing meaning, since servitude is both general and specific.

* **So in this verse there are benefits:**

* Among them: the enmity of the disbelievers toward one another, and that the strong among them show no mercy to the weak; by His saying ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these disbelievers presented to their leaders a favor, that they had been their followers, in order to seek by it a means to have them bear for them a portion of the Fire. In this is evidence of a person seeking a means by a good deed he has done for another. But is this considered a reminder of favor (*minnah*)?

In reality, what shows whether it is a means (*tawassul*) or a reminder of favor (*minnah*) are the circumstances. It may be a reminder of favor, or it may be a means. If one says: "Just as I showed you mercy, gave you, and was good to you, so be good to me," this falls under the category of seeking a means.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the weak are always followers of the strong; by His saying ﴿so the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾. For this reason it becomes clear to us now that the imitation of the Muslims of the disbelievers signifies their weakness before them, because the weak always imitates the strong due to the weakness of his personality before him. And it is obligatory upon the Muslims to have a distinctive character of their own, and to have their own inherent strength, because strength is with them: they are the people of religion, the people of truth, those who know life, and in reality they are the people of life.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these followers wish that the leaders would take on some portion, even a little, of the punishment of the Fire on their behalf. The evidence that they want even a little is their saying: ﴿a portion﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the arrogant make the excuse that they have no power to do this, because all are in the Hellfire; so how could they take on a portion on their behalf? Yes, if they were not in the Hellfire and then were cast into the Fire for the purpose of relieving those a portion, it would be possible; but since all are in the Fire, the request for this to be realized is a request for something impossible.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the humiliation of these arrogant ones on the Day of Resurrection; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, all of us are in it﴾, meaning: now we have no superiority over you, and you have no superiority over us; all are in the Hellfire.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by these tormented ones in the Fire that Allah, glorified and exalted, has judged between the servants with a just judgment; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾.

* Among its benefits: that when the judgment of Allah is executed, it cannot be lifted or repelled; by their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged﴾. On this, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in Surah Qaf: ﴿Do not dispute before Me, for I had already sent to you the warning. The word is not changed before Me, and I am not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Qaf 28–29]. When the judgment of Allah is concluded, there is no repeal of His judgment.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by these tormented ones in the Hellfire that they are servants of Allah; but what is meant is the general servitude, which is the *kawni* (universal, existential) servitude. Servitude is of two kinds: the general, which is the universal servitude (*al-ubudiyya al-kawniyya*), and the specific, which is the legislated servitude (*al-ubudiyya al-shar'iyya*). Whoever submits to Allah in the legislated sense is a worshipper in the legislated sense, and likewise in the universal sense; whoever is arrogant toward worshipping Allah in the legislated sense is a worshipper in the universal sense and not a worshipper in the legislated sense.

The commentator said: (so He admitted the believers into Paradise and the disbelievers into the Fire). The meaning is more general than what he (may Allah have mercy on him) said. ﴿He judged between the servants﴾: between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and between the people of the Fire among themselves, and He judged with a general judgment.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verse 49–51 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, exalted is He, said: (﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ [Ghafir 49] i.e., the amount of a day, ﴿of the punishment﴾) Listen to this cry, which indicates misery and despair. ﴿Those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell﴾. Khazanah (keepers) is the plural of khazin, and they are those who are in charge of its storehouses, its protection and its safekeeping. For the Fire has keepers, and likewise Paradise has keepers, and every matter that is firmly established has its keepers. Hell will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein pulled by seventy thousand angels, and what can tell you what the angels are and what their strength is? So this Fire is firmly established, has keepers, and has leaders who will lead it on the Day of Resurrection.
﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell﴾. ﴿Jahannam﴾ is one of the names of the Fire. It has been said that it is Arabic, and it has been said that it is non-Arabic. According to the view that it is Arabic, it is derived from al-juhmah, which means darkness, because the Fire is black and dark; may Allah protect us and you from it.
According to the view that it is non-Arabic, it is said that its original form is kahnam, but it was Arabicized until it became Jahannam, and it is one of the names of the Fire.
He says: ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾. They say this—and Allah knows best—when they say to their Lord, mighty and majestic: ﴿"Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return [to disbelief], then indeed we are wrongdoers." He will say, "Remain in it, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [al-Mu'minun 107, 108]. At that point they seek intercession through others to speak to Allah. They say: "Call upon your Lord," and they did not say: "Call upon our Lord," because they have been broken in regard to their Lord; He said to them: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak to Me﴾. But after that they sought, by asking the angels, that they would call upon Allah on their behalf: ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾. ﴿Yukhaffif﴾ is in the jussive mood as a response to the imperative, which is His saying ﴿Call upon﴾. And I say: it is an imperative in its form, but in reality it is a supplication and a request.
﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾. What did they request? They requested lightening, not removal, and they requested a day, not permanence, because they are in despair. But they said: perhaps the request will benefit, even if it is only the lightening of a day of the punishment; we ask Allah for well-being. The implication of this is that they are in the greatest of punishments, and that they wished to rest, even for a single day.
﴿To lighten for us a day﴾. The author said: (i.e., the amount of a day). He said "the amount of a day" because in the Day of Resurrection there is no day or night; the sun and the moon will be folded up in the Fire of Hell, and everything pertaining to the affairs of this world has ended; there is nothing but the affair of the Hereafter. Glory be to Allah! So the author says: (the amount of a day ﴿of the punishment﴾).
The keepers say to them: (﴿They will say﴾, i.e., the keepers, mockingly). This is what the author said: mockingly. But it is possible that they said that to rebuke, reproach and cause regret, not mockingly, because the matter has already occurred; they make them acknowledge something that has taken place, to cause them regret so that their grief increases.
(﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?﴾ with manifest miracles). Would that he had said: with manifest signs, because the messengers came with signs, not with miracles; but signs are something that breaks the normal course of things, so it is a miracle. And we have explained, in the discussion of the karamat of the saints in Tawhid, that it is better to call what the messengers brought as evidence for their messengerhood "signs" (ayat).
(﴿With clear proofs.﴾ They said: "Yes." i.e., so they disbelieved in them. ﴿They said: "Then call."﴾) This is the mockery.
His saying: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?﴾. Such an expression occurs frequently in the Qur'an; that is, the hamzah (interrogative particle) comes first and is followed by a conjunction, such as ﴿Have they not traveled?﴾ [Ghafir 21], ﴿Have they not traveled?﴾ [Ghafir 82], ﴿Is it then, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it?﴾ [Yunus 51], and what is similar to that. So how do we analyze its grammatical structure (i'rab)? We say: regarding its i'rab there are two positions among the grammarians:
The first position: the sentence is conjoined to what precedes, and the waw (and) is placed before its proper position, and the estimate in ﴿Did there not [wa-lam takun]﴾ is: "and did there not [wa-lam takun]". This position involves nothing but the claim of anteposition and postposition, but it is easy; that is, it is easy to say: this is conjoined to what precedes.
Some of them said: the hamzah enters upon an omitted sentence, so the sentence is resumptive (mustaʼnafah), and its estimate depends on the context. In His saying ﴿Have they not traveled?﴾ the estimate is: "Have they been heedless and not traveled?" This is more sound in terms of the rules, but there are sometimes verses for which you cannot know what the estimated element is, so this is more sound and that is easier. Are you following the two positions?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Do you know what makes the minds atrophy? The calculator, the computer of inheritance shares, the recorders. Or not?
The calculator has atrophied the mind's activity in addition, subtraction and multiplication. The computer of inheritance shares: the mind is finished; it no longer searches the shares; you press the button and the problem and the division appear for you. The third said: "I don't need to follow the teacher, my recorder is here (...)." I listened to it.
* The Shaykh: What did we say about such constructions: ﴿Have they not traveled?﴾ ﴿Have they then not traveled?﴾ ﴿Is it then, when it has occurred?﴾
* The student: The first position: that there is anteposition and postposition.
* The Shaykh: The first position: that the sentence is conjoined to what precedes, and there is nothing in this except that we say: the waw is postponed from its place.
* The student: The second position: that after the hamzah there is an estimated sentence..
* The Shaykh: The second position: that the hamzah enters upon—?
* The student: Upon an omitted, estimated sentence, and it is estimated according to the context, each sentence according to its own situation, and this is more sound but has difficulty.
* The Shaykh: Difficulty in what?
* The student: Difficulty in the estimation.
* The Shaykh: In the estimation; because sometimes you barely know what suits the situation, and that other one is easier. This i'rab comes to you in every estimation on this position.
And His saying: ﴿Did there not [wa-lam takun] come to you﴾: the interrogative here is for confirmation (taqrir). It is said: whenever the interrogative enters upon a negation, it is for confirmation, as in His saying: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh 1], ﴿Was he not a drop of semen?﴾ [al-Qiyamah 37], ﴿Is not Allah Mighty, Able to Retaliate?﴾ [al-Zumar 37], and what is similar to that. They say: whenever the interrogative enters upon a negation, it is for confirmation.
Good, then we say: it is for confirmation. But does it leave the meaning of confirmation, or is another meaning added to the meaning of confirmation according to the context?
The answer: yes. In His saying ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ it is for confirmation, displaying Allah's favor upon him; ﴿Did there not [wa-lam takun] come to you your messengers?﴾ [Ghafir 50] is for confirmation with rebuke and reproach.
They said: ﴿Yes [bala]﴾. The answer to an interrogative accompanied by a negation, affirming, is with "bala"; the answer to an interrogative not accompanied by a negation, affirming, is with "na'am" (yes); the answer to an interrogative accompanied by a negation, in the case of negation, is "na'am"; and the answer to an interrogative accompanied by an affirmation, in the case of negation, is "la" (no). Know the difference.
It is said that Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said concerning the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿"Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes [bala]."﴾ [al-A'raf 172]: "He said: If they had said 'na'am' (yes), they would have disbelieved."[[Cited by al-Samin al-Halabi in his Tafsir (1/456) as a saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
The jurists said: if a man is asked, "Did you not divorce your wife?" and he says, "Na'am," he is not divorced. If he says, "Bala," he is divorced.
Ibn 'Abbas said: if they had said "na'am," they would have disbelieved. This is accepted when the person knows the Arabic language well. As for the common person, "na'am" and "bala" are the same to him; therefore, if the common person is asked, "Did you not divorce your wife?" and he says, "Na'am," what is the ruling? According to the sound view, she is divorced; what matters is the meanings. Moreover, the answer to this has come in the Arabic language with "na'am," and among it is the saying of the lover:

Did not the night gather Umm 'Amr with us, so that this is our closeness?

Umm 'Amr is his beloved.

Yes, and you see the crescent as I see it, and the day overtakes her as it overtakes me.

So he said "na'am" (yes). But this man is content; he is satisfied that the night brings him together with his beloved even if she is in the east and he is in the west, and likewise the day; and that she sees the crescent as he sees it. If she is in the east seeing the crescent and he is in the west seeing the crescent, that is sufficient; yes, it is a conjunction.

In any case, we have now understood the answer to an interrogative accompanied by a negation with affirmation, "bala," and with negation, "na'am"; and the interrogative accompanied by an affirmation with affirmation?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And with negation, "la" (no). May Allah bless you.
They said: ﴿Bala﴾, meaning: indeed, they had come to us, but they—may Allah protect us—disbelieved.
﴿They said: "Then call."﴾ This command is for mockery, because the angels know that it will not be accepted from them; so His saying ﴿Call﴾ is mockery of them, and mockery is what in our Arabic language is called "al-hakk" (mockery): "hakakt 'alayhi" means I played with his mind. Here they said ﴿Then call﴾ mocking them, because the angels know they will not be answered.
(﴿They said: "Then call"﴾ you yourselves, for we do not intercede for the disbelievers.) Because intercession for the disbelievers is a waste of time; the disbeliever is not benefited by intercession except for one disbeliever in whom intercession benefited by lightening his punishment. Who?
* Students: Abu Talib.
* The Shaykh: Abu Talib. The intercession of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, benefited only him. If Abu Bakr or 'Umar had come to intercede for Abu Talib, it would have been rejected. But the Prophet ﷺ had his intercession accepted for his uncle Abu Talib, so his punishment was lightened. Why? Because Abu Talib did much good for the Messenger ﷺ, and he gave him great support, to the extent that he said:

Indeed I know that the religion of Muhammad is among the best religions of mankind in religion.

He said this about the religion, and he said about the Messenger:

Indeed they know that our son is not a liar in our presence, nor is he concerned with false speech.

And he defended him, and was besieged with him in the valley (al-Shi'b). Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, accepted the intercession of the Messenger ﷺ for him, that his punishment be lightened. As for the Messenger's intercession for his mother, Allah prevented it. For his mother, who is closer than his uncle: when he asked Allah's permission to seek forgiveness for her, He said no; and when he asked His permission to visit her grave, He said yes, and he permitted him. So the Prophet ﷺ visited his mother's grave, stood by it and began to weep, but did not supplicate for her, and he made those with him weep.[[Muslim (976/108) narrated from Abu Hurayrah: The Prophet ﷺ visited the grave of his mother, wept and made those around him weep, and said: "I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but I was not permitted; and I asked Him for permission to visit her grave, and I was permitted. So visit the graves, for they remind of death."]]
Thus the disbelievers are not benefited by intercession, because intercession is a waste without benefit; moreover, it will not be permitted by Allah, and intercession is never possible without Allah's permission.
Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers﴾: ﴿mā﴾ is a negation of the Hijazi type, and ﴿supplication﴾ is its subject. Our Lord, "Open between us and our people"; is it Hijazi, brothers?
* A student: There is no "mā" in it.
* The Shaykh: There is "mā": ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers﴾.
* Students: "Our Lord, open between us..."
* The Shaykh: We are the ones who say: "Open now." You have made a mistake; I saw some of you writing. When you said that "mā" is Hijazi, some of you began writing that it is Hijazi. So I ask you now, and O Allah, open between us and our people in truth: is it Hijazi?
* A student: No, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* Students: It is negating.
* The Shaykh: It is negating, and the negating one is Hijazi.
* A student: What follows it is in the nominative.
* The Shaykh: What follows it is not in the nominative! ﴿In error﴾ is a prepositional phrase; you do not know whether it is nominative or accusative.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because the negation has been broken, and Ibn Malik says:
The working of "laysa" was applied to what is below "in," with the negation remaining and order retained.
The negation has now ceased to remain. He said: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾, it has become affirmative. Therefore "mā" here is not Hijazi, because the two dialects agree, the dialect of the Tamimites and of the Hijazis, that it does not operate in this case.
﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., their request, ﴿is only in error﴾, i.e., in loss; the author's saying "nonexistence" (in'idam) is open to question. Error is loss and failure to be guided, so the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error. The supplication of a disbeliever is never accepted except in two states:
The first state: when he is compelled, as in His saying: ﴿Or who responds to the compelled one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil?﴾ [al-Naml 62], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion; but when He delivers them to the land﴾ [Luqman 32]. The supplication of the compelled is answered only because of the sincerity of his turning to Allah, for the compelled one is sincere in turning to Allah.
The second state: when he is wronged, his supplication against his wrongdoer is accepted, due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Beware the supplication of the wronged, for there is no barrier between it and Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4347) and Muslim (19/29) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] Although this was addressed regarding a people who had embraced Islam, it is general. The supplication of a disbeliever is answered when he is wronged only as an establishment of justice, for Allah does not answer the disbeliever out of love for him, but to establish justice; because now there are two adversaries: a wronged party and a wrongdoer, so for the establishment of justice Allah, exalted is He, responds to the disbeliever's supplication.
* A student: May Allah honor you. In the verse you mentioned about Umm 'Amr, he said the answer is "na'am," not "bala." There is a negation in it (...).
* The Shaykh: What did we say, my brothers?
* A student: Evidence.
* The Shaykh: We said: this is evidence that it is answered with "na'am" in the sense of "bala," and we told you that when we say to the common person who was asked, "Did you not divorce your wife?" and he said "na'am," we say she is divorced; because this is colloquial language, and it also has a root in the Arabic language, and we brought these two verses.
* The student: Shaykh, there is a hadith that indicates what this verse of poetry brought, that "na'am" conveys (...).
* The Shaykh: Is a hadith demanded as evidence for establishing a linguistic matter?
* The student: Yes, Shaykh; the best one to speak in eloquent Arabic was the Prophet ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: But if it comes from the Arabs, no evidence is needed, because the speech of the Arabs is the evidence. Did you not know that some grammarians say: we do not cite hadith as evidence for the Arabic language? Why? Because narrators permit transmitting hadith by meaning, and it is known that among the narrators are those whose language changed. Imam Ahmad is ancient and one of the imams of hadith, and you have heard—it passed us in the rules of the Arabic language—what he says about anything? He says: "ayysh" (what?). Likewise narrators may have transmitted by meaning in their own language in which they spoke, so error occurred. As for the Qur'an, yes, because it is transmitted by mass transmission (mutawatir). But many grammarians say that the prophetic hadiths are cited as evidence for the Arabic language, because the original is non-change.
* A student: (...) ﴿They said: "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?"﴾ Can we take from this the excuse of ignorance (...)? They want to establish against them that the proof has been established upon them, so they are not excused by ignorance?
* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that it indicates that if the messengers had not come to them, they would have been excused. But it may be said that their intention by that is to establish the proof upon them, since it has already been established. As for the excuse of ignorance, there is no doubt that the excuse of ignorance is established, and we have no difficulty in this, neither in the matter of disbelief nor in what is below it, as long as the person says that he is a Muslim.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Correct. But if the Messenger tells us that Allah refused to forgive him, do we object to Allah? We do not know; the proof may have been established upon him, for there were remnants of the religion of Isma'il among the Arabs, and among them Waraqah ibn Nawfal who became a Christian.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verse 49–51 (part 2 of 2):

* Student: The saying of Allah Most High: (...) by the entry of the hamzah (interrogative particle) upon the conjunction (ʿataf), meaning: is it said that placing the conjunction before the hamzah (...) because the original principle is the absence of (...)?
* The Shaykh: The original principle is not to violate the sequence (tartib). Omitting what is known is common, and you have just heard it in His saying Most High: ﴿وَإِذْ يَتَحَاجُّونَ﴾ ("and when they argue"), and that the estimated (implied) wording is: (...). Omitting what is understood is common in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language. But inverting the order and shifting it (al-zahlaqah) is rare. However, I told you that departing from the sequence here is easier for a person, because at times verses come to you and you do not know what to estimate (as implied). Unless you say: if you know the estimate, follow the more firmly established (al-aqʿad) reading; and if you do not know it, follow the easier one, so that you are one who seeks the concessions. Is that acceptable? Yes, it is acceptable. That is: the concessions of the grammarians are not an obstacle. We have told you a very useful rule: when the grammarians differ on a matter, the correct view is the easier one.
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand. The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them will be the curse, and for them will be the evil home. And We had certainly given Moses guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture as guidance and reminder for those of understanding.﴾ [Ghafir 51–54].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Most High, said: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell﴾ [Ghafir 49] to the end of the verse.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the intensity of the regret of the people of the Fire; by His saying: ﴿Ask your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾.
* Among its benefits: that the people of the Fire argue among themselves, as was previously mentioned, and they also argue with others or ask others; by His saying: ﴿And those in the Fire said﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah's perfect wisdom in His creatures, just as He perfected His legislation; in that He appointed for the Fire keepers who guard it and attend to it.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the intensity of the shame of the people of the Fire before addressing Allah, Mighty and Majestic; by His saying?
* Student: They said to the keepers of the Fire: ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾.
* The Shaykh: That they sought intercession through the keepers' words, asking them to call upon their Lord, and they did not say: "Call upon our Lord." This indicates that this was after Allah had said to them: ﴿Remain in it and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Muminun 108].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the people of the Fire are in the greatest of punishment. From where is this derived? ﴿Lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾ indicates that they are under severe hardship, and that they wish for just one day.
Then He Most High said: ﴿They said: Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidences?﴾ [Ghafir 50] to the end.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the people of the Fire are punished with a physical punishment and a punishment of the heart. From where?
* Student: The rebuke and reproach directed at them.
* The Shaykh: The rebuke and reproach directed at them: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidences?﴾. This is harsher upon them than the punishment of the body; for this reason they say, as in Surah al-Mulk: ﴿Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk 10]. Allah Most High said: ﴿So they will acknowledge their sin﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that every nation of the people of the Fire had a messenger.
* Student: From the angels' saying to them: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidences? They said: Yes﴾ (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿Your messengers﴾: every nation had a messenger.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah Most High never sent a messenger except with signs that show he is truly a messenger of Allah.
* Student: From His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾, correct.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that attention to the attribute is greater than attention to the thing itself, because the attribute is what makes things clear. From where?
* Student: From His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾, and He did not say: "with the clear signs."
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾, where He mentioned the attribute and omitted the noun described, because what matters is the attribute.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the mockery of the messengers toward these people, i.e., the people of the Fire.
* Student: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidences? They said: Yes.﴾
* Another student: ﴿They said: Then call upon [them]﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿They said: Then call upon﴾ is from the category of mocking them, because the angels know that they will not be answered.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the supplication of the disbelievers is not accepted.
* Student: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾, good.
Does this include supplication of request (duʿaʾ al-masʾalah) and supplication of worship (duʿaʾ al-ʿibadah), or only supplication of request, or only supplication of worship?
* Student: Only supplication of worship; as for supplication of request.
* Another student: Both supplication of request and supplication of worship, except in a state of necessity.
* The Shaykh: It includes both supplication of request and supplication of worship. Good. What is excepted from supplication of request regarding the answering of a disbeliever?
* Student: The one in dire need (al-mudtarr) and the wronged (al-mazlum).
* The Shaykh: Yes, the one in dire need and the wronged. What is the evidence that the one in dire need is answered even if he is a disbeliever?
* Student: ﴿Or who responds to the one in distress when he calls upon Him?﴾ [al-Naml 62].
* The Shaykh: Good. Someone might say to you: this is about the Muslim.
* Student: ﴿Or who responds to the one in distress﴾ (...) generality.
* The Shaykh: Yes, if he claims that the disbeliever is excluded from it. We say: where is the evidence? Good, this is correct, but we want a clear text on answering the disbeliever in a state of necessity?
* Student: His saying Most High: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, His saying Most High: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut 65]. Good, correct.
What is the wisdom in answering the disbeliever in a state of necessity?
* Student: Because in this state he is more sincere in supplication.
* The Shaykh: Because in this state he is sincere toward Allah in supplication, manifesting his need for Him, so Allah answers him.
The wronged: what is the evidence that He answers the supplication of a wronged disbeliever?
* Student: The hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, when the Prophet ﷺ sent him to the people of Yemen; at the end of the hadith he said to him: "Beware of the supplication of the wronged, for there is no barrier between it and Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4347) and Muslim (19/29) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]
* The Shaykh: If someone said to you: is the wronged one from among the believers?
* Student: It is not specified in this hadith.
* The Shaykh: What is the wisdom in answering the supplication of a wronged disbeliever?
* Student: To establish justice.
* The Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you. So then: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ includes supplication of request and supplication of worship. What is the evidence that worship is not accepted from a disbeliever?
* Student: ﴿And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah 54].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾.
Then Allah, Blessed and Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ to the end. This sentence is emphasized by two emphatics: the first is (inna), and the second is the lam.
His saying ﴿Indeed, We will surely support﴾ uses the form of magnification, because the context requires it, since support must come from one who is strong. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not say "I will support," but said ﴿Indeed, We will surely support﴾, because the context calls for greatness, power and strength.
﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾: ﴿Our messengers﴾ is the plural of messenger, and it refers to all the messengers, because "messengers" is a plural with a pronoun suffix, and a plural with a suffix denotes generality.
His saying ﴿and those who believe﴾ is conjoined to ﴿Our messengers﴾, meaning: and We will support those who believe. Believe in what? They believe in what must be believed in. Faith is affirmation that necessarily entails acceptance and submission. Whoever denies is not a believer; whoever affirms but does not accept is not a believer; whoever affirms but does not submit is not a believer. Abu Talib, for example, affirmed the prophethood of the Messenger, peace be upon him, but he did not accept nor submit, so he is not a believer. Those who believe are those who affirm with their hearts, submit and surrender with their limbs, and accept what the messengers reported; these are the believers.
His saying ﴿in the life of this world﴾ is connected to ﴿We will support﴾, meaning: We will support them in the life of this world; ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾: ﴿and on the day﴾ is also conjoined to what preceded and is connected to ﴿We will support﴾, meaning: and We will support them on the day when the witnesses stand, and that is the Day of Resurrection.
﴿al-ashhad﴾ is the plural of shahid (witness). The author says: (They are the angels who testify for the messengers that they delivered the message and against the disbelievers that they denied). Thus the author, may Allah have mercy on him, restricted them to the angels, but the correct view is that it is more general than the angels: the angels bear witness, and this Ummah bears witness over those before it, as Allah Most High said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. The skins bear witness, and the limbs bear witness; so everything whose testimony is established is included in His saying ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾, and that is the Day of Resurrection.
* In this noble verse: emphasis on the support of Allah, glorified and exalted, for the messengers and those who believe; by His saying ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾.
* In this verse there is a doubt that a Christian uses as evidence, saying: God is the third of three. My proof is His saying ﴿Indeed, We﴾, and His saying ﴿Nous﴾ (we), ﴿Nurihim﴾ (We show them), and what resembles them of indications of plurality. So I say — the Christian says: God is the third of three, and I have an argument. How do we answer him?
We answer him by saying: You are among those whose hearts have deviation, because you followed the ambiguous (mutashabih), and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous﴾ [Al ʿImran 7], and you left the clear (muhkam) that affirms that Allah is One with no partner, such as His saying Most High: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 163], and such as His saying in denouncing these Christians: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say: Allah is the third of three; and there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 73]. So this Christian followed the ambiguous.
Likewise every falsifier who argues with a verse is one who follows the ambiguous. Allah, Mighty and Wise, has placed in His legislative verses and in His cosmic verses also what is ambiguous, as a trial and test for whom? For those who believe and for those in whose hearts is deviation.
