Al-'ashi is what comes after midday (zawal), and from it the hadith of Abu Hurayrah concerning the incident of Dhu al-Yadayn: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in one of the two evening prayers" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (482) and Muslim (573/97), from Abu Hurayrah]. So al-'ashi is what follows midday, and al-ibkar is what precedes midday. The author said: (the five prayers), because al-'ashi includes Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha, and al-ibkar is Fajr.

﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾. The correct view, as we said first, is that tasbih here means what is more general than the prayers.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them — there is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾ [Ghafir 56]. ﴿Indeed those who dispute﴾: this is (inna) and its noun, and its predicate is His words: ﴿there is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾, i.e., there is nothing in their breasts except pride.

His words: ﴿Indeed those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾. Al-mujadalah is contention (al-mukhasamah), and contention is called mujadalah because each disputant twists (yujdilu) the argument in order to defeat his opponent, like the twisting of a rope. Do you know the twisting of a rope? Its tightening. Each of the disputing parties twists the argument for himself in order to silence his opponent.

His words: ﴿yujadiluna﴾: the form mufa'alah usually occurs between two parties, though fa'ala may occur without a partner, such as safara, on the pattern fa'ala, and jadala on the pattern fa'ala, but it is not from two; yet generally the mufa'alah form arises between two.

﴿They dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾: who are the ones who dispute? They dispute with the people of truth and debate with them. You know the debate that took place between Ibrahim and his people, and between Ibrahim and the one who argued with him about his Lord, and many disputes in the Qur'an, in the Sunnah, and up to our day.

﴿Concerning the signs of Allah﴾: the author said (the Qur'an), and this interpretation is deficient, because the signs of Allah include the universal and the legislative; moreover, they include those who dispute within this Ummah and those who dispute about earlier peoples. Do those who dispute about earlier matters dispute about the Qur'an? No. So it is better to take the verse in its generality: they dispute concerning the signs of Allah, universal and legislative, if they are in this Ummah; the legislative ones are the Qur'an and also the Sunnah. If they are from before this Ummah, the dispute concerns the Torah, among the people of Musa.

So the author's interpretation is deficient. Why? Because it did not encompass the meaning but restricted it to part of it. But if someone claims that the author mentioned the Qur'an by way of example, we say: this is possible and plausible, but he erred in expression; the intended meaning should be stated as "its legislative signs, such as the Qur'an," so that the matter is clear.

﴿They dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾: disputing about the legislative signs includes following the ambiguous (mutashabih). For example, one comes to a verse of the Qur'an that contains ambiguity, which may bear a true meaning and a false meaning, while the true meaning is clearer, as is known; he wants to force it upon the false, weaker meaning. He brings verses of the Qur'an that appear contradictory: "The Qur'an is contradictory; how can it say this and then say that?" For example, he says that Allah said: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa' 42], they will not conceal a statement from Allah; and in another verse: ﴿Then their discourse will be only that they say: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am 23]. Did they conceal or not? They concealed, ﴿they said: by Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, while previously they had fully acknowledged it. So he comes and says: this Qur'an is contradictory; how does it affirm in one place that they do not conceal from Allah any statement, and in another that they deny? He disputes on the basis of such things.

If a person does not have a sword to cut through this argument, he remains perplexed. What is the sword that cuts such an argument? We say: the Day of Resurrection is not an hour of time; its duration is fifty thousand years. They acknowledged at first, and when they saw that the believers were saved, they said: "We will conceal, perhaps we ... ", or that they concealed at first, then when their limbs testified against them, they acknowledged and confessed.

In any case, I say: disputing about the signs in the Qur'an includes following the ambiguous; following the ambiguous is undoubtedly disputation. Likewise disputing about the universal signs: for example, one brings up creatures of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and says: "Why did Allah create this thing? Why did Allah create the scorpion? Why did Allah create the snake? Why did Allah create the lion?" and similar things; so, Allah intended only to harm and afflict creation!

Be attentive! When this question is put to an ordinary person, what does he say? He says: "Well, by Allah, I do not know; perhaps..." Then he is drawn into disputation, though we know that the creation of these creatures is for the benefit of the servants. We have mentioned in previous sessions that there are eight benefits in it that appear to the one who reflects. Thus we know that disputing about the signs occurs concerning both the universal and the legislative signs, and we have given two examples of this.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿without authority﴾. The commentator said: (proof, burhan). ﴿that has come to them﴾: this is an attribute of authority, and the author says authority (sultan) is proof (burhan).

We have mentioned previously that sultan is that by which authority is possessed, whether it be evidence, when a matter requires proof, or authority of administration, like the supreme sultan and the like, or strength and power, as in His words: ﴿You will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 33]. The point is that sultan is that by which a person has authority; interpret it in each place according to its context.

His words: ﴿without authority﴾: does this mean that a person could dispute falsely with authority? So this restriction is a description of reality, not a restrictive qualification; rather it is a qualification that describes the actual situation: whoever disputes about the signs of Allah is disputing without authority, and authority can never come to him for that.

His words: ﴿indeed, there is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾. ﴿In their breasts﴾: the commentator says (ma), meaning it is negating, because (in) has several meanings in the Arabic language, shared among several meanings; many words have multiple meanings, but who determines the meaning? The context and indications of the situation. Among these: whenever you find an affirmation after (in), it is negating, as in ﴿This is only a human like you﴾ and ﴿You are only fabricators﴾ [Hud 50], ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾ [Ghafir 56], and so on. So whenever you find an affirmation in the context of (in), know that it is negating. The rest of its meanings, God willing, will come later. But here He says: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾ [Ghafir 56]. He said: ﴿in their breasts﴾, and what is in the breasts is the heart. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but blind are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46]. When the heart becomes proud, may Allah protect us, the body becomes proud; and when the heart humbles itself to Allah, the body humbles itself. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there is in the body a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599/107), from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir]. The Messenger (peace be upon him) spoke the truth, and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, illustrated this with "a king who has soldiers, who commands the soldiers and they obey" [narrated by Ma'mar in al-Jami' (20375), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (108)].

Yet Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: the illustration of the Messenger ﷺ is more eloquent, because a king may be rebelled against by his soldiers, isn't that so? But can the heart be rebelled against by the limbs? Never, it is not possible. So He placed the arrogance in the chests, i.e., in the hearts, because the chests are its locus: ﴿They will never attain it﴾ [Ghafir 56] except the arrogance of pride and greed to rise above you.

﴿They will never attain it﴾ [Ghafir 56]: the sentence ﴿they will never attain it﴾ apparently is a new (independent) sentence and not a description of arrogance (﴿There is nothing in their chests but arrogance﴾). For this reason we say: when you recite, say: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them—there is nothing in their chests but arrogance﴾; this is the correct place to pause.

Do not stop at His saying: ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, because if you stop at ﴿without authority having come to them﴾ the meaning is not complete, and you would be stopping before the completion of the statement. Rather, say: ﴿there is nothing in their chests but arrogance﴾, then pause, and say: ﴿they will never attain it﴾. For if you join ﴿but arrogance they will never attain it﴾, the sentence ﴿they will never attain it﴾ would, by the recitation, become a description of arrogance, and the matter is not so; rather it is a new sentence from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: they will never attain what is in their chests of arrogance and rising above you.

As for His saying: ﴿they will never attain it﴾, its original form is (ببالغينه, bibalighīnahu), but where did the nun go? The nun was dropped due to the idafah (genitive construction), because the nun and the tanwin do not combine with the idafah. For this reason one of the people said, describing his distance from his companion:

"I am like tanwin, and you are idafah, so where do you see me that I may not take my place?"

The nun, like the tanwin, is dropped with the idafah (﴿They will never attain it, so seek refuge in Allah﴾ from their evil ﴿indeed He is the All-Hearing﴾ of their sayings ﴿the All-Seeing﴾ of their conditions).

﴿Seek refuge in Allah﴾: ﴿seek refuge﴾ means seek protection in Him and hold fast to Him, for He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the excellent Protector. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ entered upon a woman he had married, she said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you." He said: "You have sought refuge in the One who grants refuge; join your family." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (5255) from the hadith of Abu Usayd.] He left her, although he had married her desiring her, but to whom did she seek refuge? To One whose protection can never be violated. He said: "Join your family." Seek refuge in Allah from what? The commentator says: (from their evil). But the more appropriate view is that the matter is more general: seek refuge in Allah from every disliked thing, for a person has no refuge except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, no protection except in Him, and no shelter except in Him; He is the One to whom one flees.

﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ghafir 56]. He concluded the verse with hearing and sight, because what they harm the Prophet ﷺ with is either a statement, which is heard, or an action, which is seen. That is: if they harm you with speech, We hear; with action, We see. In this there is reassurance for the Messenger ﷺ, which will be known, God willing, when the benefits are mentioned. And Allah knows best.

* Student: The correct view is what some exegetes said regarding His saying: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath 2], that the earlier sin is what preceded the prophethood, and the later sin is abandoning the command (...).

* Shaykh: This is not correct, it is not sound. The Messenger ﷺ did things for which Allah rebuked him after the prophethood: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. When was it revealed? Was it before the prophethood or after? Brother, we do not declare the Messenger free of anything except what Allah has declared him free of. Then I told you a little while ago: a person after sin and repentance from it may be better than he was before it, and we gave you an example from whose story? From the story of Adam.

My brothers, leave the texts as they are, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, never wrongs anyone. For this reason I think—I am making sure of what I think—but I do not know whether you have heard this or not: when they said that the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. And when he covered her, she bore a light burden and carried it about. But when she became heavy, they both invoked Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous one, we will surely be among the grateful." (189) But when He gave them a righteous one, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them﴾ [al-A'raf 189–190]. "They said: this verse was revealed about Adam and Eve. She conceived, and Satan came to her and said: name your child 'Abd al-Harith. They refused to obey him, and the child was born dead. Then she conceived again, and he came to them and said: either you obey me or I will make for him two horns of a deer (a ayl, a kind of gazelle whose horn is strong like a spear), so that he comes out of your belly and splits it open. Then the love of the child overcame them, and they named him 'Abd al-Harith." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3077), Ahmad (20117), and al-Bazzar (4580) from the hadith of Samurah.] They made him a servant of other than Allah. Is it possible that this occurred from Adam? No, it is not possible. Then, even if it were supposed to have occurred, is it possible that Allah mentions the evil and does not mention the repentance from it? For we say: if it occurred, either he repented from it or he did not. If he did not repent, then he died upon shirk; and if he repented, it is not from the justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to mention the evil and not mention the deliverance from it.

So we say—may Allah bless you—some scholars—may Allah pardon us and them—resort to contrivance, or (strain) to be precise: the correct expression is they strain to exonerate the messengers from what Allah has described them with. But we believe that the Messenger differs from others in two matters. The first: it is impossible for him to do what undermines the message or his honour. The second: if he commits a sin, it is impossible that he does not repent from it; Allah does not confirm him upon a sin. We, now, are children of Adam: is it permissible for us that this happens and that? Is it permissible for the children of Adam to do what undermines honour, to commit indecency, to commit fornication? It is also permissible for them, if they do it, not to repent. The messengers differ from others in these two matters, brother.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, brother, you are not writing; I am looking to see what your opinion is. Comment, may Allah bless you, on those who attend with their bodies without their hearts.

* Student: It is not befitting (...).

* Shaykh: Enough. This comment, in any case, may Allah reward you with good. "Lā yanbaghī" may mean "impossible, unthinkable," as in His saying: ﴿It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 92].

In any case, my brothers, you—may Allah reward you with good—have left your families, your bedding and your homes and came to this place; so seize the opportunity. I have tested it: if a person neglects one letter of speech, he is finished; a single word may determine what follows it. So we hope that each of you will pay attention.

So the summary now: some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, strain in regard to the messengers, peace be upon them, and we say: we do not transgress the Qur'an and the Hadith at all. A prophet was stung by an ant; the ant is well known. It stung him, so he burned the whole ant colony, poured fire on it. Allah revealed to him: "Would not one ant only have stung you, and you destroyed a whole community for a single offence!" This indicates that a person must be careful.

Then, these ants cannot be disciplined. Do you think they would become disciplined if the other ant colonies heard this story and repented of stinging people? No. I say this to you lest you object to me that Allah, the Exalted, may destroy the obedient for the sin of the disobedient: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have wronged﴾ [al-Anfal 25]. Why? Because these obedient ones are charged with forbidding evil; and when they are destroyed, others are disciplined by them, unlike the matter of the ant colony.

* Student: (...) When the Children of Israel appear in the Qur'an, is it in the sense of honour or not in the sense of blame? And when the Jews appear, it is in the sense of reproach and blame. Is this consistent throughout the Qur'an?

* Shaykh: No, that is not correct. Allah mentions the Children of Israel by their sins and blames them: ﴿Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah 78]; He did not say "the Jews." ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah 47], and there are many verses.

* Student: If a wife says to her husband: "I seek refuge in Allah from you," as happened with the Messenger, is it (...) that he divorces her or not (...)?

* Shaykh: No. If she says, "I seek refuge in Allah from you," he says: "And I seek refuge in Allah that you say such words." Do you understand?

* Student: Shaykh (...)?

* Shaykh: Do not open the door on us, O Shaykh. Everyone goes home when he comes (...) she says, "I seek refuge in Allah from you." Make the tea: "I seek refuge in Allah from you." Cook lunch: "I seek refuge in Allah from you" (...).

In any case, if a person seeks refuge in Allah, the Messenger said: "Whoever seeks refuge in Allah, grant him refuge." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (1672), al-Nasa'i (2567), and Ahmad (5365) from the hadith of Ibn Umar.] But one considers whether Allah grants refuge to such a man or not. That is, does Allah grant refuge to this one who sought refuge in Allah? Suppose a man was commanded to do good and said to the one commanding him, "I seek refuge in Allah from you." Would Allah grant refuge to this man who sought refuge? He would not, because we do not grant refuge to one who seeks refuge in Allah unless Allah grants him refuge. As for the station of the Prophet ﷺ, it is a station higher than our stations.

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Ghafir 55]. Some hostile people say that persecution and trial in the religion of Allah are evidence that this religion is false. How do we respond to them?

* Shaykh: Who said it?

* Student: Some hostile people.

* Shaykh: Who are "some"? Are you giving me tales or hypotheticals? Where? How do they say it?!

* Student: They say: if this religion were true, people would not be harmed in detention centres and...

* Shaykh: No, this is different. The Messenger, had his religion not been true, would not have been harmed for it. If he had followed what his people were upon, they would not have harmed him. For this reason, it was part of Allah's wisdom that the paternal uncles of the Messenger, peace be upon him, were four in number—those who lived in his time were four, not ten uncles. Of those, two were disbelievers: one of them harmed him, and the other supported and sheltered him. Two embraced Islam: one of them embraced Islam early and has a station of truthfulness, and he was a martyr; the other embraced Islam late, but there is no doubt he has a station of truthfulness. Who disbelieved and harmed him? Abu Lahab. Who disbelieved and sheltered him? Abu Talib. Who has a station of truthfulness and precedence? Hamzah. And the fourth? al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Allah is Wise, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ [al-Rum 60].

* From the benefits of this verse: the command to patience, and it here is obligatory. Patience is of three kinds, as the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience upon the painful decrees of Allah. The first is the most perfect, then the second, then the third. Patience in obedience to Allah: that a person performs the act of obedience in the manner Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prescribed, without impatience and without aversion, rather fully submitting to it. This is patience in obedience to Allah. Patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah: that he restrains himself from engaging in sins, so he does not commit them, but endures even if it is difficult for him. The third: patience upon the decrees of Allah, meaning upon what Allah decrees for him of affliction in his body, mind, thought, family, wealth, or society. He endures and restrains himself from discontent with the limbs, the tongue, or the heart. Do you understand now?

Discontent of the heart is that there is some kind of objection to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in his heart: why did He decree this upon me, and not upon so-and-so? Why did Allah afflict me? Then perhaps he may disbelieve—we ask Allah for well-being—as He said, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good touches him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

Discontent of the tongue is to call for destruction and ruin, and similar pre-Islamic claims. Discontent of the limbs is striking the cheeks, tearing the collar, and the like. Thus patience upon the decrees of Allah includes restraining the heart, the tongue, and the limbs.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the consolation of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾.

* And among its benefits: a warning to his opponents, because Allah promised him victory and the humiliation of his enemies and opponents. So His saying "indeed the promise of Allah is true" is a consolation to him, and also a warning to his enemies.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that the promise of Allah, glorified and exalted, must come to pass, by His saying: ﴿true﴾, and truth is what is established and occurs. This is supported by His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah does not fail in the promise﴾ [al-Ra'd 31]; this is due to the completeness of His power and the truthfulness of His promise. Because failing a promise arises either from the promiser's lying or from his inability to fulfil it, and both are impossible regarding Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of seeking forgiveness, by His saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir 55].

* And among its benefits: the permissibility of sins upon the prophets, peace be upon them, by His saying: ﴿for your sin﴾ [Ghafir 55]. The address is to the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and if sin is permissible for the Messenger, the most noble of messengers, then for others it is all the more so.

If someone says: are not the prophets protected from sins?

The answer: this verse and similar ones indicate that the answer is negative, but they differ from others in this regard in two respects. The first: they are protected from lying, betrayal, and the like that affect the message. The second: they are protected from every sin that undermines honour. The third: they are protected from affirming sins; they must be alerted to them so that they are granted success in repenting from them. These are three distinctions between them and other people. As for other people, they are not protected from what undermines honour, nor from what undermines trustworthiness, nor from persisting in sins.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the command to glorify Allah with praise in the morning and evening, by His saying: ﴿And glorify with the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾ [Ghafir 55]. If by this is meant the five prayers, the command here is obligatory; if it is meant as the glorification which is the known remembrance, the command here is recommended.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾ [Ghafir 56]. His saying "without authority having come to them": is this a restrictive qualifier or to describe the reality?

* Student: To describe the reality.

* Shaykh: To describe the reality. What is the benefit of mentioning a qualifier that describes the reality?

* Student: To emphasise that this attribute is inherent to them.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Causation.

* Shaykh: Causation; that is, an indication that this is impossible. Where is the predicate of "indeed" (inna) in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute﴾?

* Student: ﴿There is in their chests﴾.

* Shaykh: The sentence: ﴿there is nothing in their chests but arrogance﴾ [Ghafir 56]. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿they will never attain it﴾ [Ghafir 56].

* Student: According to the author's view, that it is a description (...).

* Shaykh: But what is its meaning? What is the meaning of ﴿they will never attain it﴾?

* Student: They will never attain this arrogance which they have shown toward the Prophet ﷺ.

* Shaykh: That is, they will never attain their aim from arrogance.

Student: Yes, (...) arrogance toward the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and this arrogance they will never attain.

Shaykh: That is, they will never attain superiority over the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.

This verse contains several benefits. It describes the state of those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, and that they have no proof for what they dispute. Moreover, disputation concerning the signs of Allah is of two kinds. The first is disputation to establish the truth and refute falsehood; this is commanded, based on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And argue with them in the way that is best﴾ [an-Nahl 125]. The second is disputation in the opposite sense, to establish falsehood and refute the truth; this is the blameworthy kind, and such a verse as this noble one applies to it.

Among the benefits of this verse: affirmation of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which, as we said in the tafsir, are both legislative (shar'iyyah) and cosmic (kawniyyah).

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that what drives these disputants is arrogance and self-exaltation, based on His words: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾.

Among its benefits also: that these people will not reach their goal through what they dispute with, based on His words: ﴿They will never attain it﴾. Allah the Exalted has pointed to this in His words: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and thereupon it departs. And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya' 18]. So reflect on these powerful expressions: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood﴾ — al-qadhf (hurling) is throwing with force.
﴿and it crushes it﴾ — that is, it reaches its brain.
﴿and thereupon it departs﴾ — that is, it dies immediately; for "idha" here is "idha" of suddenness (fajā'iyyah), and the "idha" of suddenness indicates the sudden occurrence of a thing. This shows that the truth certainly prevails over falsehood, without doubt. If it is said: we sometimes find that disputation from the disbelievers is not followed, and sometimes it is not repelled, and a person is unable to repel it — we say: yes, this may happen, but the cause is not in the proof, rather it is in the one who argues. The cause is not in the argument; the argument stands and the truth prevails. But the cause lies in the arguer: he may have little knowledge, and so he does not know; he may have knowledge but lack understanding and not comprehend; he may have bad intention, desiring only victory for his own view and not victory for the truth, and such a person is forsaken; or he may be inarticulate (al-'iyy), meaning that he does not have the eloquence and clarity that lead to victory. Eloquence and clarity have a great effect in establishing the truth. Indeed, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: «Indeed, some eloquence is magic»[[Reported by al-Bukhari (5146) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. These four matters are what may cause falsehood to outwardly prevail over the truth, and these four are: either little knowledge —

Student: Or ignorance.

Shaykh: That is it; little knowledge is ignorance, or inarticulateness in expressing what is in one's mind.

Student: Or that he argues (...).

Shaykh: Yes, bad intention. The fourth?

Student: His lack of understanding.

Shaykh: Yes, deficiency of understanding. These four are what make falsehood a beacon that outwardly rises above the truth, whereas the truth itself can never, in any way, be overcome by falsehood.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that arrogance is the cause of every evil. For this reason: «He who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance will not enter Paradise»[[Reported by Muslim (91/147) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]. Is the type of arrogance found in these disputants rejection of the truth (batar al-haqq), or contempt for people (ghamt an-nas), or both?

Students: Both.

Shaykh: Both. This arrogance — may Allah protect us — combined both types of arrogance: rejecting the truth and refusing it. And the second?

Student: Looking down on people.

Another student: Disdain for people.

Shaykh: Looking down on people is ghamt an-nas; rejecting the truth is batar al-haqq.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the steadfastening of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, based on His words: ﴿They will never attain it﴾. Likewise, among its benefits: despairing these disputants, that they will never reach their aims.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that seeking refuge in Allah in the situation of disputation is legislated, based on His words: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾. This is because the disputant will bring up doubts that may be feared to affect him; if he seeks refuge in Allah and holds fast to Him, Allah will save him from them. For this reason He said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ [Ghafir 56]. In disputation He commands seeking refuge in Allah, and in judgment He commands seeking forgiveness: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous (105). And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 105]. This is because sins come between a person and the clear perception of the truth; whereas in the situation of disputation, a person needs someone to turn to and hold fast to; therefore He said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ [Ghafir 56].

Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirmation of hearing for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His words: ﴿Indeed, He is the Hearing﴾, and affirmation of sight, based on His words: ﴿the Seeing﴾. Scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have mentioned that hearing is of two kinds: first, perceiving what is heard; second, responding. As for perceiving what is heard, it occurs in several meanings:
First: showing the breadth of Allah's hearing, Mighty and Majestic. An example is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Certainly has Allah heard the speech of the one who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾ [al-Mujadila 1]. Hence 'A'isha said: «Praise be to Allah, who has encompassed all voices with His hearing»[[Reported by an-Nasa'i (3460), Ibn Majah (188), and Ahmad (24195) from the hadith of 'A'isha.]].
Second: warning, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [az-Zukhruf 80].
Third: support, as in the words of Allah to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46]. As for hearing in the sense of responding, it is as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], meaning the one who answers it; and as the worshipper says: "Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah" — meaning: Allah has answered the one who praised Him. As for al-Basir (the All-Seeing), it has two meanings:
The first meaning: the one who perceives everything with His sight, so it means seeing.
The second: knowledge, meaning that He is knowing of everything.
Also among the benefits of the noble verse: affirmation of hearing and seeing together, which is a stronger indication of perfection than the mention of only one of them; because the disputant may say and may do, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, warned him with this: ﴿Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ [Ghafir 56], since the one who seeks refuge in Allah seeks refuge either from words or from deeds.

The Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 57–58:

Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said after the verse from which the benefits have been drawn: ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. The lam here is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida') and it conveys emphasis; "khalq" (creation) is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿greater﴾ (akbar) is the predicate of the subject. ﴿The heavens﴾ are the seven layers, and ﴿the earth﴾ is the earth on which we live, and the Sunnah has come that it is seven, explicitly, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever takes a span of land unjustly, Allah will collar him with it on the Day of Resurrection, from seven earths" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2452) and Muslim (1610 / 137) from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd]. The Qur'an alluded to this in His saying: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq 12]; because the likeness here cannot be in attributes, since the difference between the heavens and the earth is evident, but it is a likeness in number.

﴿Greater﴾ is the predicate of the subject; that is, ﴿greater than the creation of mankind﴾; meaning, than bringing mankind into existence. Is it initial or repeated? Both initial and repeated: bringing the heavens and the earth into existence is greater than bringing mankind into existence, both initially and in repetition.

He says: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ [al-Mu'min 57]. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "It was revealed concerning the one who denies resurrection (﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ initially, ﴿is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ a second time)." So he restricted the creation of mankind in the second time, which is repetition, on the basis that the verse was revealed concerning the one who denies resurrection. The correct view is that the verse was revealed about something more general: it was revealed concerning the one who denies resurrection and in demonstrating the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Accordingly, we say: ﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ initially, ﴿is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ initially and in repetition.

﴿But most of mankind﴾: the author, the exegete, said: "(That is, the disbelievers of Makkah)." ﴿do not know﴾. In this explanation there is a deficiency, because "most of mankind" is more general than being from Makkah or elsewhere: most of mankind do not know. Why do they not know? Because they do not reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth; they are ignorant and do not know. ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer﴾ [al-Mu'min 58]. These are two examples which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explained. The first: are the blind and the seeing equal? No, they are not equal, and no one among people says that they are equal. Nor are ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ and ﴿the evildoer﴾; meaning, if it is established that the blind and the seeing are not equal, then likewise those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer are not equal; it is impossible for them to be equal.

The author said: "(So they — that is, those who are not guided — are like the blind, and one who knows is like the seeing)." The author brought this as a preface to explain the connection of the verse with what precedes it. But it may be said that in the new sentence Allah makes clear that these and those are not equal. (﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal﴾, nor ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning the good-doer, ﴿nor the evildoer﴾; there is an added "lā" for emphasis.)

It seems that, according to the author's statement, the estimation is: nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer. This meaning is clear. But his saying "meaning the good-doer" indicates that the one who believes and does righteous deeds is a good-doer (muhsin), based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ihsan is that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9 / 5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah].

As for His saying ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: ﴿believe﴾ is with the heart, and ﴿do righteous deeds﴾ is with the limbs, because when faith settles in the heart, deeds confirm it.

His saying ﴿righteous﴾ (al-salihat) is an adjective of a omitted noun, and the estimation is: "the righteous deeds." A righteous deed is that in which two matters are combined: first, sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; second, following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). With the loss of the first there is shirk, and with the loss of the second there is bid'ah (innovation). Allah, glorified and exalted, does not accept a deed in which He is associated with another, nor does He accept an innovation which anyone has introduced into His religion. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in the Hadith Qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partnership; whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his associate" [recorded by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not upon our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718 / 17) from the hadith of 'Aishah].

Therefore, there must be sincerity without shirk with it, and following without innovation with it, and by that the deed is righteous. ﴿Nor the evildoer﴾: meaning, the doer of evil deeds. Evil deeds are either deficiency or excess; either deficiency through shortcoming and lacking, or excess through addition, and both are wrongdoing.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Little do they remember﴾ (they are admonished, with ya' and ta'; meaning, their remembrance is very little).

His saying ﴿they remember﴾ means: they take admonition. There are two readings: ﴿yatadhakkarun﴾ and ﴿tatadhakkarun﴾, and both are correct, being from the seven canonical readings. Then the author pointed to the grammatical structure of this construction, which is frequent in the Qur'an, and said, may Allah have mercy on him: "(That is, their remembrance is very little)". On this basis, ﴿ma﴾ would be a verbal-source (masdariyyah) particle; that is, their remembrance is a little remembrance. But what appears is that ﴿qalilan﴾ is an adjective of an omitted noun, functioning as an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq); that is, they remember a little remembrance, and this ﴿ma﴾ is an extra ﴿ma﴾ for emphasis, emphasizing what? Emphasizing the paucity; that is, "little, little." On this basis the sentence is composed of a verb and subject, and of an absolute object which is ﴿qalilan﴾, since it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, and of the extra ﴿ma﴾ for emphasis.

Returning to drawing the benefits of the two verses, He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [al-Mu'min 57]. In this is the affirmation that the heavens and the earth are greater than humans, which is clear; indeed, humans are part of the earth, since they were created from clay.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: establishing the proof against those who deny resurrection; for if you acknowledge that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, it follows that you must acknowledge that He is able to create mankind, since whoever is capable of the greater is more capable of what is less.

Allah has also established many proofs for the affirmation of resurrection; among them this verse, which is reasoning from the greater to the lesser; and among them His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum 27]. The pronoun in ﴿and it﴾ refers to the repetition; ﴿easier for Him﴾ than the initiation, and this is something known by the senses and by reason.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming resurrection. What is the mode of inference?

* A student: ﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Mu'min 57] contains a refutation of mention of the higher, so it is...

* The Shaykh: No, my intention is the affirmation of resurrection, not the power of repetition.

* The student: ﴿is greater than the creation of mankind﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying ﴿is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, because the purpose of the verse is establishing resurrection.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that most people are in heedlessness and ignorance, by His saying: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ [al-Mu'min 57]. This resembles His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah; they follow only conjecture﴾ [al-An'am 116]. So be keen not to be among those who do not know.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that knowledge among people is scarce; for if most of them do not know, it follows that those who know are the minority.

If someone asks: Is the intended meaning the negation of knowledge, or the negation of its benefit and fruit?

It is said: both are intended. Most people are in ignorance, and most people, though they possess knowledge, do not benefit from their knowledge and do not profit from it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, for emphasis.

* Student: (...) What is the extra (...)?

* The Shaykh: No; its sign is that if you drop it, the sentence is complete without it.

So how is this comparison with the blind and the seeing, for one who has no will in this? * The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The purpose is not to blame the blind and the seeing so that it is said they have no will; the purpose is to explain their condition, that they are not equal by agreement.

* The Shaykh: No, one must repel it. This is not a patient person; rather it is obligatory upon him to repel it, and to know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is All-Wise, and that Allah may intend good for a person when He tests him.

* The Shaykh: Sign of what?

* The Shaykh: If he finds in himself discontent, discontent with Allah in his heart.

* Student: (...) or merely its occurrence?

* The Shaykh: No, he must repel it. If it has overwhelmed his heart, then it is obligatory to repel it. But I do not think a believer is discontent with his Lord. Yes, he dislikes what has happened; that is correct, every person dislikes the trial that befalls him. But that he believes Allah has wronged him, and that this is aggression from Allah against him, and the like, I do not think anyone does this.

* Student: Committing major sins by the prophets: can major sins occur from them?

* The Shaykh: It can occur, but they repent from them. Moses killed a soul without right, or was not permitted to do so.

* The Shaykh: Whether before prophethood or after it; and for this reason he apologized when asking for intercession because of that.

* The Shaykh: Difference? It is known, there is no doubt about it, but look, we have not yet reached this verse. Why do you ask about something we have not reached, nor have we taken its benefits or anything? Wait.

* The Shaykh: Houris are not a condition; the wives of Paradise will be better than (...) benefit.

* Student: We have learned.

* The Shaykh: We have learned now. The hadith has some weakness, but as we said: the women of this world are better without doubt. We ask Allah to make me and you among the people of Paradise.

* Student: ﴿Indeed the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe (59). And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled (60). It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight; indeed Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks (61). That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but He; so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Mu'min 59–62].

* From the benefits of this verse: first, coining of examples (darb al-amthal), which is attaching the intelligible to the perceptible. Its basis: that the negation of equality between the blind and the seeing is something known by the senses, and the negation of equality between those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer is something known by reason.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a teacher of people should link intelligibles to perceptibles, because that is closer to understanding and more conducive to acceptance; for what is perceptible is not denied, but the intelligible may be disputed and denied by one who disputes.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: negating equality between different matters, and this is one of the principles of the Sharia: that it does not equate between differing things nor joins things that are separate. Among it: some people boast and say that the Islamic religion is a religion of equality, and this is an error; the Islamic religion is a religion of justice, not of equality. Those who say it is a religion of equality want to move from this to equating man and woman, and the noble and the base; and this is an error, for Allah, the Exalted, has given each person what befits him in the Sharia and in destiny. For this reason not a single letter in the Qur'an says that people are equal at all; what is most found in the Qur'an is the negation of equivalence, that is, the negation of equality. But justice does come in the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed Allah commands justice and good-doing﴾ [al-Nahl 90]; ﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ [al-Nisa' 58]; ﴿Be just, that is nearer to piety﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8], and other verses. That is because justice means that we place each person in his proper station; so if two persons are equal in station we equalize them in judgment, and if they differ we distinguish between them. It is remarkable that many books of later scholars say this. And this matter may also lead to equating the believer and the disbeliever, since each of them is a human being; but if we say "justice," the disbeliever cannot be placed on the level of the Muslim, for that would be oppression against the Muslim and excess and exaggeration in regard to the disbeliever.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds, and the evil of evil deeds, by His saying: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, and not the evildoer﴾ [al-Mu'min 58].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that many people remember only a little; by His saying: ﴿Little do you remember﴾ [al-Mu'min 58].

* Among its benefits: that in this verse there is a witness to the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 116], and His saying: ﴿And most of mankind will not believe, though you should be eager﴾ [Yusuf 103].

* The Shaykh: Sign of what?

* Student: I mean the sign of a person (...) patience...

* The Shaykh: If he finds in himself discontent, discontent with Allah in his heart.

* Student: (...) or merely its occurrence?

* The Shaykh: No, he must repel it. If it has overwhelmed his heart, then it is obligatory to repel it. But I do not think a believer is discontent with his Lord. Yes, he dislikes what has happened; that is correct, every person dislikes the trial that befalls him. But that he believes Allah has wronged him, and that this is aggression from Allah against him, and the like, I do not think anyone does this.

* Student: Committing major sins by the prophets: can major sins occur from them?

* The Shaykh: It can occur, but they repent from them. Moses killed a soul without right, or was not permitted to do so.

* Student: (...) before prophethood.

* The Shaykh: Whether before prophethood or after it; and for this reason he apologized when asking for intercession because of that.

* Student: (...) ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Mu'min 58] (...) between faith and righteous deeds, since he mentioned faith and then said righteous deeds; is it permissible (...)?

* The Shaykh: Difference? It is known, there is no doubt about it, but look, we have not yet reached this verse. Why do you ask about something we have not reached, nor have we taken its benefits or anything? Wait.

* Student: (...)

* The Shaykh: Houris are not a condition; the wives of Paradise will be better than (...) benefit.

* Student: We have learned.

* The Shaykh: We have learned now. The hadith has some weakness, but as we said: the women of this world are better without doubt. We ask Allah to make me and you among the people of Paradise.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, Glory be to Allah! May Allah keep you safe, keep this.

* * *
* Student: ﴿Indeed the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe (59). And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled (60). It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight; indeed Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks (61). That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but He; so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Mu'min 59–62].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah said: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer﴾ [al-Mu'min 58].

* From the benefits of this verse: first, coining of examples (darb al-amthal), which is attaching the intelligible to the perceptible. Its basis: that the negation of equality between the blind and the seeing is something known by the senses, and the negation of equality between those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer is something known by reason.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a teacher of people should link intelligibles to perceptibles, because that is closer to understanding and more conducive to acceptance; for what is perceptible is not denied, but the intelligible may be disputed and denied by one who disputes.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: negating equality between different matters, and this is one of the principles of the Sharia: that it does not equate between differing things nor joins things that are separate. Among it: some people boast and say that the Islamic religion is a religion of equality, and this is an error; the Islamic religion is a religion of justice, not of equality. Those who say it is a religion of equality want to move from this to equating man and woman, and the noble and the base; and this is an error, for Allah, the Exalted, has given each person what befits him in the Sharia and in destiny. For this reason not a single letter in the Qur'an says that people are equal at all; what is most found in the Qur'an is the negation of equivalence, that is, the negation of equality. But justice does come in the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed Allah commands justice and good-doing﴾ [al-Nahl 90]; ﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ [al-Nisa' 58]; ﴿Be just, that is nearer to piety﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8], and other verses. That is because justice means that we place each person in his proper station; so if two persons are equal in station we equalize them in judgment, and if they differ we distinguish between them. It is remarkable that many books of later scholars say this. And this matter may also lead to equating the believer and the disbeliever, since each of them is a human being; but if we say "justice," the disbeliever cannot be placed on the level of the Muslim, for that would be oppression against the Muslim and excess and exaggeration in regard to the disbeliever.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds, and the evil of evil deeds, by His saying: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, and not the evildoer﴾ [al-Mu'min 58].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that many people remember only a little; by His saying: ﴿Little do you remember﴾ [al-Mu'min 58].

* Among its benefits: that in this verse there is a witness to the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 116], and His saying: ﴿And most of mankind will not believe, though you should be eager﴾ [Yusuf 103].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 59–60 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾ [Ghafir 59]. This sentence is emphasized with two emphatic particles, (inna) and (al-lam). Then this emphasis was reinforced by His saying "there is no doubt about it," which is a semantic emphasis, while the first is a verbal emphasis. ﴿There is no doubt about it﴾. ﴿Doubt﴾ (shakk). ﴿About it﴾ means: about its coming and its occurrence. The Hour here refers to the Day on which people will be resurrected. It was called "the Hour" because people use the word "hour" for a matter that strikes people with calamity and overwhelms them so that they do not perceive it. The author (al-Mu'allif) explained "doubt" (rayb) as "shakk," and this is a close explanation. But you will find a subtle, slight difference between them, that is, between rayb and shakk: rayb is doubt accompanied by agitation and hesitation.

So when someone says "irtāba" (he had doubt), it is not exactly the same as saying "shakka" (he doubted). Rather, irtiyāb carries unease and agitation, so it is more specific than shakk. Every rayb is a shakk, but not every shakk is a rayb. However, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, explain a thing by something close to it, as people explain a thing by what approximates it.

As for His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ [Ghafir 59]: do not believe in what? In the coming of the Hour. For this reason, its coming was emphasized to them. And since most people do not believe in it, most people are disbelievers, because belief in the Hour has a great effect on the realization of faith. Whoever does not believe in the Hour does not work for anything. How can someone who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning act? Whoever believes in the Day of Reckoning will be eager to be saved from the consequences of that Day.

﴿But most of the people do not believe (59). And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ [Ghafir 59, 60]. When He mentioned the Hour, He mentioned what protects from its consequences, which is calling upon Allah, so He said: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me"﴾. He expressed the sentence in the third-person form (ghayba) out of glorification of Him, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Your Lord said﴾, and He did not say "I say" or "We said" or anything similar, out of glorification of Allah.

﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾. ﴿Call upon Me﴾ is an imperative, and ﴿I will respond to you﴾ is its answer (jawab al-talab), the answer to a demand. Here, "calling" (du'a') includes both the supplication of request (du'a' al-mas'alah) and the supplication of worship (du'a' al-'ibadah). The supplication of request is for a person to say, "O my Lord, forgive me." The supplication of worship is for a person to worship Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, by what He has legislated. Worship is called supplication because it includes a person's seeking to be saved from the Fire and to enter Paradise. Isn't that so? If you asked every worshipper, "Why do you worship Allah?" he would say, "I want to be saved from the Fire and to enter the mercy of Allah." Thus worship includes supplication through the language of the state (bi-lisan al-hal).

As for His saying: ﴿I will respond to you﴾, we interpret it, in contrast to the supplication of request, as "I will give you what you ask," and we interpret it with regard to the supplication of worship as "acceptance," meaning: I will accept from you. So Allah's response to the supplication of request is that He gives the petitioner what he asked for, and His response to the supplication of worship is that He accepts from the worshipper. The commentator (al-mufassir) said: "(That is, worship Me, and I will reward you, by the indication of what follows it)." This interpretation, based on what you have heard, would you describe it as what? As deficient. It is considered a deficient interpretation. As for what follows, it is not an indication restricting it to this meaning. Rather, we say: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾ [Ghafir 60] shows that supplication is worship, because He said: ﴿Call upon Me﴾, and then said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾. There is no doubt that whoever is too proud to call upon Allah, and considers himself independent of Allah and not in need of Him, is undoubtedly deserving of this threat: that he will enter Hell in humiliation.

﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾. This is part of what was said. ﴿Will enter﴾ (sayadkhulūn), read with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (and vice versa). Reverse it to ﴿yudkhalūn﴾ (they will be made to enter). These are two authentic seven canonical recitations.

﴿Jahannam﴾ is the name of the Fire. It is a Arabized (mu'arrab) noun, and its origin, as it has been said, is (Kahannam). It has also been said that it is an Arabic word, and the nūn in it is additional, and its root is from (al-juhmah), meaning darkness. Whatever the case, it is the proper name for the Fire. May Allah protect us and you from it.

As for His saying ﴿humbled﴾ (dākhirīn), it means humiliated, abased. The dākhir is the one who is humiliated.

Let us return to the benefits of the two noble verses. The first: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾ [Ghafir 59].

* Among its benefits: the establishment of the Hour's occurrence with emphatic affirmation, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾.
* And among its benefits: a warning against neglecting this Hour and not preparing for it, by His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾.
* And among its benefits: the obligation to believe in the Resurrection.

And among its benefits: the obligation to believe in the Resurrection, because it is an emphatic report from Allah, and all of Allah's reports are true, and every promise of Allah is true.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the prohibition of doubting this Hour. Because His saying ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾ [al-Kahf 21] may be a plain report for emphasis, and it may be a report with the meaning of a prohibition, that is: do not doubt about it. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿This is the Book about which there is no doubt﴾ [al-Baqarah 2]. There are two interpretations of it: the first is that it is a pure report, and the second is that it is a report with the meaning of a prohibition, that is: do not doubt about it.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: most people do not believe in this Hour and deny it, saying: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 78], ﴿There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾ [al-Jathiyah 24].
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of a well-known expression, indeed the nullification of a well-known expression, which is that when a person dies, people say, "He has returned to his final abode." This statement is false, because the grave is not the final abode. The final abode is either Paradise or the Fire. As for the grave, it is a visit and a passage, just as the world is a passage; similarly, the grave is a passage. For this reason, a Bedouin heard a reciter recite Allah's saying: ﴿Competition in worldly gain distracts you until you visit the graves﴾ [al-Takathur 1, 2]. The Bedouin said: "By Allah, the visitor does not remain; there is something beyond the graves." How did he derive it from: ﴿You visit﴾? The visitor stays for a period, then departs.

So if we hear someone say, "He has been buried in his final abode," or something similar, we object to him and say: give up this expression, because its content, if the one who says it believed it, would make him a disbeliever.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me"﴾ [Ghafir 60], and so on to the end.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of speech to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is this speech an inner speech that is not manifested, or is it manifest speech? The second: it is manifest speech, because inner speech, when intended, is specified, as in His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8], and ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. So when speech is stated without qualification, what is meant is audible speech. This is the view of the early generations (al-salaf) and the leading scholars of later generations: that Allah speaks with an audible voice and with letters, because ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir 60] consists of words composed of letters, or not? Therefore, He speaks with letters and with a voice, the Mighty and Majestic.

As for the statement of the one who says that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in the self, and that what is heard is merely an expression of the speech of Allah, created by Allah for people to hear, and otherwise His speech is only what is within Himself, it is false. That is, this is a false statement, because if we interpret "speech" in this way, its meaning becomes knowledge, not speech.

Now we want to compare two statements. One says: "What is in the Mushaf is the speech of Allah, created." And another says: "What is in the Mushaf is an expression of the speech of Allah, created." Which of these is closer to the truth?

* Students: The first.
* The Shaykh: The first. The first is the statement of the Jahmiyyah (Jahmites) and the Mu'tazilah (Mu'tazilites), and the second is the statement of the Ash'ariyyah (Ash'arites). It has now become clear that the statement of the Mu'tazilah and the Jahmiyyah about the speech of Allah is better than the statement of the Ash'arites, even though the Ash'arites claim that they are among the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah). How can this be? So from this verse we establish that speech belongs to Allah, and speech cannot exist except with audible utterance and letters.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the Lord's greatness and magnificence, from His saying: ﴿And your Lord said﴾ [Ghafir 60], for this form indicates the greatness of the One who speaks, the Mighty and Majestic.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of lordship (rububiyyah) to Allah. It is divided into two types: general and specific.

The general is that which encompasses all creation, which is the nurturing of creation with blessings and sustaining them with blessings. The specific is the nurturing of the believing servants of Allah, whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has raised in what He loves.

Both types came together in His saying, concerning the magicians of the family of Pharaoh: ﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron"﴾ [al-A'raf 121, 122]. Which is the general? The first, "the Lord of the worlds." "The Lord of Moses and Aaron" is the specific.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: is calling upon Allah obligatory or recommended?
* Students: Calling upon Allah is obligatory.
* The Shaykh: From where do you derive it? From His saying: ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾, because it implies: do not call upon other than Me.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah has guaranteed and promised the one who calls upon Him that He will answer him, by His saying: ﴿I will respond to you﴾. If someone says: "We call upon Allah much but see no answer, and we work much but feel no acceptance; what is the answer?"

The answer is that we say: causes do not take effect unless they encounter a receptive locus. Have you seen that when you cut meat with a knife, it is cut, or not? It is cut. When you cut iron with it, it is not cut, even though it is sharp on meat and does nothing to iron. So the cause must have a receptive locus; otherwise it has no effect. In worship, a person worships his Lord and does not feel acceptance because there is something preventing it: either the loss of a condition, a pillar, or an obligation, or the occurrence of something that invalidates it. Isn't that so? Otherwise, if we established the acts of worship as we were commanded, we would find their effect. ﴿And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 45]. Which of us, when he prays, feels aversion to immorality and wrongdoing? Prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, so why do we not feel this? Because we are negligent.

In supplication, we always call upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and see no answer. So we say about it what we said at the beginning: the cause must have a receptive locus. If a person calls upon his Lord but has missed some of the obligatory or recommended etiquettes of supplication, or there is an obstacle preventing the acceptance of the supplication, then the flaw is not in the supplication, but in the one who supplicates and in the locus.

Let us give an example of a person who supplicates without feeling need for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and without feeling the urge to flee to Allah. His supplication is very deficient. If you say, for example, "My Lord, forgive me," you must feel that there are sins that need forgiveness, and that you are in the greatest necessity of the forgiveness of these sins, because if these sins are not forgiven, woe to you! One sin upon another becomes a major sin. For this reason, the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the belittling of sins and said: "Indeed, the likeness of these is like a people who camped in a land, and each one of them brought a stick, and they gathered a great quantity of firewood and kindled a great fire."[[Ahmad (2679) narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of belittled sins, for they gather upon a man until they destroy him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave an example of them: like a people who alighted in a barren land, and the food of the people was prepared; a man went and brought a stick, and another man brought a stick, until they gathered a heap, then they kindled a fire and cooked what they threw into it.]] Even though each one of them brought just one stick. So the point is that when you supplicate, you must feel that you are in the utmost need of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Second: among the etiquettes whose absence prevents the answer is that you have doubt about Allah's answering your supplication, such as considering what you ask for to be too great, saying: "This is not going to happen." This is an error, and it is among the things that prevent the answer. For this reason, "the Prophet ﷺ forbade the saying of one who says: 'O Allah, forgive me if You will,' and said: 'Let him resolve in his request and magnify his desire, for Allah is not overwhelmed by anything He gives.'"[[Muslim (3817) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you supplicates, let him not say, 'O Allah, forgive me if You will,' but let him resolve in his request and magnify his desire, for Allah is not overwhelmed by anything He gives."]]

Likewise, among the causes of the prevention of the answer is that a person supplicates for something sinful or for severing of kinship ties. He supplicates for sin, such as supplicating against a person who does not deserve to be cursed. This is sin, like supplicating against a ruler who has erred in some matter, saying: "O Allah, do not grant him success," and similar things. This is transgression in supplication. If you see a ruler, whether minor or major, who has erred, his remedy is not for you to say: "O Allah, do not grant him success." His remedy is for you to say: "O Allah, grant him success; let him reform, and let Allah reform through him." This is among the transgressions in supplication that are not accepted. Among the transgressions in supplication is severing of kinship ties: supplicating for the severing of kinship ties is also not accepted. Is the supplication of the oppressor against his victim accepted?
* Student: It is not accepted.
* The Shaykh: Why? Because it is sinful.

Fourth: among the obstacles to acceptance is eating what is forbidden. Eating what is forbidden is among the obstacles to acceptance, because "the Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man who travels far, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky, saying: 'O Lord, O Lord'" (all these four aspects are among the causes of the answering of supplication), "while his food is forbidden, his drink is forbidden, his clothing is forbidden, and he has been nourished with what is forbidden. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'How then could it be answered for him?'"[[Narrated by Muslim (1015) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] All these prevent, or come between, a person and the acceptance of his supplication and Allah's answering him.

If there are no obstacles, and the locus is suitable and receptive, then only the matter beyond that remains, which is the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. "Allah may ward off from a person evil greater than what he asked for; He may grant what he asked for; and He may store that for him as a reward on the Day of Resurrection," as came in the hadith.[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3604) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man supplicates to Allah with a supplication except that it is answered for him: either it is hastened for him in this world, or it is stored up for him in the Hereafter, or an expiation of his sins is made equal to what he supplicated, so long as he does not supplicate for sin, severing of kinship ties, or hastening." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does one hasten?" He said: "He says: 'I supplicated my Lord, but He did not answer me.'"]] Otherwise, we are most certainly confident of the truth of His saying: ﴿I will respond to you﴾, and that it must come to pass. I think we cannot complete the rest of the benefits, so let us limit ourselves to this. Yes.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. Is what occurs in the heart or in the self called speech, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: No, not unless it is qualified, such as when one says: "He said in himself," as in the hadith: "what its self whispers to it"[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (5269) and Muslim (127/201) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
* The Student: The statement of the Ash'arites: "what subsists in the self." Is their statement correct?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not correct. This is a false statement. For this reason, we have now weighed their statement against the statement of the Mu'tazilah, and the statement of the Mu'tazilah became closer to the truth than theirs, because they say: "This that is in the Mushaf is the speech of Allah, created; it is truly the speech of Allah, but it is created." And those (the Ash'arites) say: "It is created and an expression of the speech of Allah."
* Student: May Allah be good to you. The saying of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "I do not bear the concern of being answered, but I bear the concern of supplication." Does he mean (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. He means that a person may not have the conditions for acceptance. Now, each of you should take account of himself. When you are in prayer and say, "My Lord, forgive me and have mercy on me" between the two prostrations, do you feel that there are heavy sins from which you are asking God to deliver you? Or is it just a word you say to fulfill the obligation? In fact, when we take account of ourselves, we find great deficiency in us. When a person calls upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, his heart is illuminated simply by calling upon Allah, because supplication is an act of worship. But we ask Allah to help us and you to remember Him, thank Him, and worship Him well.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, this will come, God willing, with the benefits.
* Student: Why do we not say that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (...)?
* Shaykh: No, because there are controls, as you have heard: eating what is forbidden, if he supplicates for sin or severing of family ties, if the heart is heedless and distracted, if he doubts the matter. There are well-known controls from the Sharia.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Read what follows: ﴿So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, that they may be guided﴾ [al-Baqarah 186].
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. Has he responded to Allah in the etiquette of supplication and in other matters? You must all know that absolute statements in one place must be restricted by what indicates restriction in another place, because the Sharia is one; it came from one niche.
* Student: We said that a person should not undertake supplication until he understands the supplication. For example, a person who knows that this thing is difficult for him..
* Shaykh: Difficult for whom?
* Student: For him.
* Shaykh: For him?! If it were easy for him, he would not need to supplicate; he would just do it.
* Student: He supplicates for it?
* Shaykh: He supplicates, but transgression in supplication is not accepted. If he says: "O Allah, I ask You to make me among the noble messengers," what do we say?
* Students: Transgression.
* Shaykh: This is transgression in supplication. "O Allah, make me not commit a sin," is transgression in supplication. Or he says: "O Allah, I ask You to turn this mosque into gold and emerald; indeed You are over all things capable," (and it becomes) "Be, and it is." But this is contrary to custom, and in most cases there is no benefit in it either.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: This is possible; there is nothing wrong with it. May Allah make you like Sibawayh in grammar and like Ibn Taymiyyah in knowledge, amen. And we, God willing... they say that someone was heard circumambulating the Kaaba, and a person heard him saying: "O Allah, I ask You for grammar like the grammar of Ibn Hisham, and jurisprudence like the jurisprudence of Shaykh al-Islam; indeed You are over all things capable."
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you to rest in and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people do not give thanks. That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but Him, so how are you deluded? Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah. It is Allah who made the earth a place of settlement for you and the sky a canopy, and shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ghafir 64].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾ [Ghafir 60]. We have already discussed this verse, have we not? And we mentioned its benefits.
Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you.﴾ In this is Allah's promise, glory be to Him, to every supplicant that He will respond to him. But there must be conditions, which I think we have mentioned.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who are arrogant toward worshipping Allah will enter Hell in a state of humiliation and abasement, due to His saying: ﴿will enter Hell in humiliation﴾.
* Among its benefits: that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed; that is, the punishment corresponds to the offense, because when they were arrogant in this world, they were made to enter the Fire in abasement in the Hereafter: ﴿will enter Hell in humiliation﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Fire, due to His saying: ﴿Hell﴾.
* Among its benefits: that supplication is an act of worship, due to His saying: ﴿Call upon Me﴾, then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verses 59–60 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾ [Ghafir 59]. This sentence is emphasized with two emphatic particles, (inna) and (al-lam). Then this emphasis was reinforced by His saying "there is no doubt about it," which is a semantic emphasis, while the first is a verbal emphasis. ﴿There is no doubt about it﴾. ﴿Doubt﴾ (shakk). ﴿About it﴾ means: about its coming and its occurrence. The Hour here refers to the Day on which people will be resurrected. It was called "the Hour" because people use the word "hour" for a matter that strikes people with calamity and overwhelms them so that they do not perceive it. The author (al-Mu'allif) explained "doubt" (rayb) as "shakk," and this is a close explanation. But you will find a subtle, slight difference between them, that is, between rayb and shakk: rayb is doubt accompanied by agitation and hesitation.
