* Shaykh: This is its definition according to the scholars. As for *nahy* in the general sense, it means anything that indicates prohibition. Even the interrogative used for denial indicates prohibition. For instance, if you say to someone who has done something undesirable, "Do you do this?", you are asking a question, but it implies a prohibition. Its technical definition is what we have given, and we are not discussing what merely conveys prohibition.
﴿So avoid the filth﴾. If you said that this is a prohibition, we would say you are mistaken. Rather, we say this is a command to avoid.
* Student: (*nuhītu*)?
* Shaykh: No. ﴿So avoid the filth﴾. *Nuhītu* ("I was forbidden") is a past-tense verb form, but it is not a prohibitive form. It is a report that he was forbidden. So what is the prohibitive form? "Do not worship those who call upon other than Allah." That is its meaning.
Now the brother has confused prohibition in meaning with prohibition in form. Prohibition in form, as the technical term is used, is a demand to refrain, issued from a position of superiority, in the present tense preceded by the prohibitive *lā*. That is *nahy*. As for what indicates prohibition by means other than this form, it is not called *nahy* in the technical sense, even though it is prohibition in meaning and not in technical terminology.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you out as a child, then [He lets you grow] that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become elders—and among you is one who is taken in death before that—and that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will use reason. (67) He is the One who gives life and causes death; and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is. (68) Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah—how are they turned away? (69) Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers; they will soon know. (70) When the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged (71) into the boiling water, then in the Fire they will be burned. (72) Then it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to associate (73)?﴾ [Ghafir 67–73].
* Shaykh: No, is this a verse? Do you have this as a verse?
* Student: Yes.
* Another student: But he did not complete the verse.
* Shaykh: No, is ﴿you associate﴾ the last verse?
* Student: Yes, I have the end of the verse.
* Shaykh: Fine, that is enough. The verse-endings (*ru'ūs al-āy*) may be paused upon even if what follows is connected to them. For example, you may say ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾ [al-Ma'un 4] and pause, then say ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'un 5].
﴿Where is that which you used to associate﴾ [Ghafir 73] is connected to what follows, ﴿other than Allah﴾ [Ghafir 74]. But if it is the end of a verse, then pausing there is prescribed (*tawqīfī*), meaning it is to be followed as transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ), so one pauses there.
* Student: ﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to associate (73) other than Allah?" They will say, "They have strayed from us; rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers﴾ [Ghafir 73–74].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen...﴾ to the end.

﴿Khalaqakum﴾ means: He began your creation. Khalq (creation) means bringing into existence with measuring and determining. The poet said:

"You indeed measure what you create, and some people create but do not measure."

So it is bringing into existence with determination.

﴿Min turab﴾ (from dust). He said: (by the creation of your father Adam from it). The origin, then, is that we are from dust, from this earth: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once more﴾ [Ta-Ha 55]. So the earth is the first and the last with respect to the children of Adam until the Day of Resurrection.

(﴿Then from a drop of semen﴾ — maniyy.) This is considered with regard to the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Then from a clinging clot﴾ — this is the third stage, and the second is considered with regard to the offspring of Adam. The 'alaqah, he said, is (thick blood) like a thread. ﴿Then He brings you forth as a child﴾, and Allah, exalted is He, omitted mention of the lump of flesh and the creation of the other form, going straight to His words ﴿then He brings you forth as a child﴾, in the sense of (children). He said "in the sense of children" because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) from the kāf in ﴿yukhrijukum﴾, and it is plural, whereas ṭifl is singular. On this basis, ṭifl must be taken to mean ṭifl-an in the sense of children. It has also been said that ﴿ṭiflan﴾ is in the singular sense, and that the meaning is: then He brings forth each one of you as a child, so that ﴿yukhrijukum﴾ is plural with regard to the group, i.e., each one of us comes forth as a child. On this view, there is no need to interpret ṭifl as meaning children.

﴿Then that you may reach your full strength (ashudd)﴾. He said: (﴿Then﴾ He keeps you alive ﴿that you may reach﴾). He estimated this because the lam requires a complement, so its complement is omitted, and the estimate is: then He keeps you alive. (﴿That you may reach your full strength﴾: your strength is completed from thirty years to forty.) This is the attainment of ashudd: a person is at his strongest from thirty to forty years old, then he begins to decline gradually. However, there may be factors that cause his strength to remain for a longer period, and there may be factors that cause his strength to collapse before he completes forty. But in principle, when a person completes forty years, he begins to weaken. ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength﴾, i.e., the completion of your strength.

(﴿Then that you may become elders﴾, with the dammah and kasrah on the shin.) That is: ﴿shuyūkhan﴾ and ﴿shīkhan﴾ (shuyūkh/shuyūkhan), and both readings are among the seven canonical readings. This is the author's method: when he mentions both readings together, it means that both readings are among the seven. ﴿Then that you may become elders﴾, meaning old, reaching the age of old age.

He said: (﴿And among you is one who is taken in death before﴾, i.e., before the full strength and old age.) He said: (He did that with you so that you may live, ﴿and that you may reach an appointed term﴾). The exegete estimates this because of the presence of the conjunctive particle, which is His words ﴿and that you may reach an appointed term﴾. (﴿An appointed term﴾: a limited time.) Musamma means specified, and it means limited.

﴿And that you may perhaps understand﴾, i.e., that you may be among those possessing intellects and comprehend Allah's wisdom, mighty and majestic, in His decree and legislation. You now see that in the measuring, the measured thing grows little by little until it becomes large; likewise the Law, in which the laws develop little by little until they are complete. This is among Allah's universal sunnah and His legislative sunnah: that matters do not come all at once, but develop until they reach perfection. This is from perfect wisdom.

His words ﴿la'allakum ta'qilun﴾ (that you may perhaps understand) do not mean the intellect of perception, but the intellect of management and right guidance, because intellect is of two kinds:

An intellect of perception, upon which the legal obligations depend. For this reason it is said: among the conditions for the validity of prayer is intellect, meaning the intellect of perception.

And an intellect of management and right guidance, which is good conduct. For this reason we say: the disbelievers do not understand, although with respect to the intellect of perception they are strong, vigorous, and clever; but they are devoid of the intellect of management and conduct.

﴿And that you may reach an appointed term and that you may perhaps understand﴾. In these verses, Allah, glorified and exalted, has explained the origin of the children of Adam and the end of the children of Adam.

* Among the benefits in it:

* First: the clarification that Allah, glorified and exalted, is He who created us alone, and that there is no creator except Allah. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in Surat al-Tur: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur 35]. What is the answer?

Our answer: they were not created from nothing, and they are not the creators; therefore they have a creator.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification that the origin of the children of Adam is dust, as in His words ﴿from dust﴾. Dust, as is known, varies, and therefore the natures of the children of Adam differ, their colours differ, and their tongues differ, just as their origin differs. Dust, as you know, includes sand, clay, salt-flats, and other things.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the transition of this origin to another origin, which is water: the sperm, the semen. ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the loins and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq 5-7]. In another verse: ﴿from a despised fluid﴾ [al-Mursalat 20]; meaning: thick, not gushing forth and not flowing, because it is not liquid like flowing water; rather it is a despised fluid, i.e., weak and not moving.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the development of human creation in the mother's womb. Here Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned only the drop and the clot, because the drop is the origin and the clot is the origin of the material of life, since life is only by blood, which is the origin of the material. For this reason, if a person's blood were drained, he would perish.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification of Allah's power, that after this state in the mother's womb he comes forth as a complete child.

* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah divided people, after their emergence as children, into categories:

The first category: that a person reaches his full strength and then dies.

The second: that he reaches old age.

The third: that he dies before that, i.e., before reaching full strength and before old age.

On what basis is this? We say: this is purely the will of Allah, mighty and majestic; it has no known basis, but is purely His will. Yet even though it is purely His will, Allah may decree universal causes and legislative causes by which life is prolonged and health remains, and He may decree causes to the contrary.

Among the legislative causes is what the Prophet, peace be upon him, mentioned in his saying: «Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded for him and that his life be prolonged, let him maintain his kinship ties»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5986) and Muslim (2557/21) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: "Whoever loves that his provision be expanded for him and his life be prolonged, let him maintain his ties of kinship."]]. This is evidence that maintaining family ties is among the causes of abundant provision and long life. Allah makes it easy for this servant to maintain his ties, so his life is prolonged. This is something written, but we have no knowledge of it; the Prophet ﷺ urged us to do it in this manner.

As for the universal causes, they are avoiding harmful causes to health. This is endless and is well known; most of those who know it are physicians. Allah makes available to a person, from the causes of health, medicine, food, and air, that by which long life is attained.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that however long a person's term may be, it has a limited end. Although a person in himself harbours a very distant hope, thinking he will remain for hundreds of years, in reality, however long he lives, the term is decreed, and whatever is limited and counted has an end. For every day that passes diminishes life. A poet said:

"A man rejoices in the days he passes through, and every day that passes brings him nearer to his term."

Is this correct? Yes: a man rejoices in the days he passes, saying, "Thank God, my life is long, and I have enjoyed much," but every day that passes brings him nearer to the term. So it lengthens in one respect and shortens in another. Then at the end of the term: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at 46].
Measure what lies ahead by what has passed. Some of us have reached sixty years, or fifty, or twenty, or something similar. Those days that have passed seem as if they were an hour: today you are as yesterday, and yesterday as the day before, as though it were an hour, as though it were dreams. This is why He said: ﴿and that you may reach an appointed term﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification of Allah's blessing upon us through knowledge and clear explanation, because that is the means of reaching the goal of intellect; this is shown by His words ﴿and that you may perhaps understand﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation that Allah's rulings have reasons; i.e., Allah's rulings are grounded in wisdom.

Is this restricted to the legislative rulings, or does it include both the legislative and the universal rulings?

The answer: the latter. All of Allah's universal and legislative rulings have reasons; that is, all are for a wisdom. But this wisdom may be known to us, and people differ greatly in this: some of them Allah makes aware of the secrets of His creation and the secrets of His law, some He does not make aware, and some are in between.

Likewise, all of Allah's legislative rulings are for a wisdom, all have reasons.

As for what the jurists say, that a given ruling is ta'abbudi (devotional, whose reason is not known), they do not mean by this that it has no reason, but that its reason is unknown to us, so for us there is only mere devotion. For this reason, when a woman asked Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: "What is the matter with a menstruating woman who makes up fasts but does not make up prayers?" She said: "That used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasts and not commanded to make up the prayers."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321) and Muslim, and the wording is his (335/69), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] This is the wisdom: the legislation of Allah is wisdom, and all of Allah's law is wisdom. But if a person seeks to find a reasonable wisdom for it, there is no harm in him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of the people of intellect, i.e., the intelligent, because Allah made it a goal when He said: ﴿and that you may perhaps understand﴾.

We have now mentioned that Allah's universal and legislative rulings have wisdom. If someone says: How do you answer the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23]?

The answer: there is no contradiction, because Allah did not say "there is no wisdom in what He does," but said ﴿He is not questioned about what He does﴾, because everything He does is wisdom and is not questioned about; we know that He did not do it except for a wisdom, so He is not questioned.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verse 68 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He it is who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ This, like the first, is a resumed (isti'nafiyyah) sentence that shows the perfection of Allah's power, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿He it is who gives life and causes death﴾ means: He places life in the dead and death in the living. ﴿He it is who gives life and causes death﴾ — alone, or together with another? Alone. No one gives life and causes death. For this reason Abraham said to the one who argued with him about his Lord, ﴿Abraham said, "My Lord is He who gives life and causes death." He said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:258]. So no one can give life to a dead person, nor cause a living person to die.

If it is said: Does not 'Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam give life to the dead? We say: Yes, but by the permission of Allah, by the same verse, ﴿and [I will] bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:49].

If it is said: Does not a man kill another, who was alive, so that he dies? We say: Yes, but what he did is the cause of death, and it is not the act of causing death itself. Often a person's jugular veins are cut and his belly is split open, yet he remains alive and recovers. So the conclusion, O people, is that giving life and causing death are in the hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

(﴿And when He decrees a matter﴾ means He intends to bring something into existence. ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾.) Here ﴿amran﴾ (a matter) means "a affair" (sha'nan); that is, it is the singular of "al-umur" (affairs), not the singular of "al-awamir" (commands). That is: when He decrees an affair of the affairs and determines it, nothing prevents Him from bringing it into existence. With what does He bring it into existence? With the word: "Be," and it is. ﴿Indeed, the likeness of 'Isa with Allah is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:59]. For this reason 'Isa is described as "a word of Allah"; that is, he came into being by His word. The conclusion is that when He decrees a matter and determines it, He says to it, "Be," and it is.

Does the phrase refer to existing things, non-existent things, or both? Both. Even if He wills the annihilation of something, He says to it, "Be," and it ceases to exist. So the author's statement "the bringing of something into existence" would have been better if he had added "or its annihilation," because when He decrees a matter, whether bringing into existence or annihilation, He says to it, "Be," and it is.

Other than Allah, if you wanted to demolish a house, you would spend days demolishing it. But when Allah wills to demolish this house, or the whole village in its entirety, what does He do? He says, "Be," and it is; it collapses and becomes scattered dust.

So we say: when He decrees a matter, whether bringing something into existence or annihilating it, He only says to it, "Be," and it is. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything in measure﴾ [al-Qamar 54:49]. Everything is in measure, the small and the great, what relates to His actions and the actions of His servants. Everything He created is in measure. ﴿And Our command is but one [word], like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar 54:50]. Is the thing commanded delayed?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: What is it? ﴿Like a glance of the eye﴾. The glance of the eye: nothing is faster than it. One time, without repetition. ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾ The fa' (then) indicates immediate sequence.

Allah said concerning the resurrection of people: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:13–14]. Glory be to Allah, how great is the power of Allah! With one word all things come to be as Allah wills. Pay attention to the final point: they come to be as Allah wills, even if the one commanded is not aware of it. But it must be as Allah wills. When the pen said, "My Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]. And what did it do? It wrote what will exist until the Day of Resurrection, even though it did not know it, but it was commanded, so it must comply.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly, in obedience"﴾ [Fussilat 41:11]. There is no compulsion here; it is willing obedience.

So we say: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾, that is, to bring something into existence or annihilate something, ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-innama﴾ connects to the answer of (idha, "when"), and it indicates sequence.

And His saying ﴿"Be," and it is﴾ — without delay?
* Students: Without delay.
* The Shaykh: Without delay, because this fa' indicates sequence.

He said: (with the nun vowelled with a damma and with a fatha, on the presumption of "an") — so there are two readings: ﴿kun fa-yakunu﴾ and ﴿kun fa-yakuna﴾. On the first reading the fa' is for resumption (isti'naf); on the second the fa' is the fa' of causation (sababiyyah) after which the verb is put in the subjunctive, which is well known in the science of grammar.

He said: (on the presumption of "an"; that is, it comes into being immediately after the will, which is the meaning of the saying mentioned). May Allah pardon this author. He says: (immediately after the will, which has the meaning of the saying mentioned). By this he intends to negate the speech; that is, His saying ﴿Indeed He only says to it "Be"﴾ means only that He intends to say. For he, may Allah pardon him, wants to negate the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since his school is that of the Ash'aris, who say that speech is the meaning subsisting in the self, and not something heard, nor a directed address sent to the one addressed. Yet the verse is explicit: ﴿He only says to it﴾ is an explicit, directed speech, ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾

The meaning of ﴿He says to it﴾, according to his words, would be: He wills that it be, and it was. There is no doubt that this is distortion of words from their places. We ask Allah, exalted is He, to pardon whoever distorts it with good intention. We do not believe of this author, Allah willing, anything but good, but he erred in this. The correct view is that He says a speech that is heard by the one addressed, so he complies with the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* From this noble verse: the statement that Allah, exalted is He, is the One who gives life and causes death, and this is part of the completeness of His lordship.
* Among its benefits: giving life and causing death are not difficult for Him; this is shown by ﴿And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾
* Among its benefits: a refutation of those who deny resurrection, who said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:78]. What is its basis? When He decrees resurrection, what does He say? "Be," and it is. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has not man seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation. [He] who has made for you from the green tree, fire﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:77–80], up to His saying: ﴿His command is only when He wills a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:82].

Let us now set out the proofs in these verses showing Allah's power to revive the dead. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned eight aspects of His power to revive the dead:

The first aspect: His saying ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ What is the indication of this?
* Student: Because the One who gave them life the first time is the One who can give them life again.
* The Shaykh: Well done. Because the One who was able to originate them the first time is able to restore them, since restoration is easier: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum 30:27].

The second proof: ﴿And He is Knowing of all creation.﴾ What is the indication?
* Student: It entails power; that is, He is able to give life.
* Another student: The One who creates creatures knows what He has created.
* The Shaykh: How does He create them? That is, creation is not hidden from Him. If creation is not hidden from Him, what could incapacitate Him? He is over all things capable.

﴿He who has made for you from the green tree, fire.﴾ What is the indication of this verse for Allah's power to revive the dead?
* Student: Allah is the One who created us, so it is not beyond Him to make fire from the green tree.
* The Shaykh: No. The One who made fire from the green tree is able to restore us. What is the indication?
* Student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created the tree originally green; when He transformed it from greenness into fire...
* The Shaykh: It becomes firewood that is kindled.
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No, that is wrong.
* Student: When the tree was first created it was alive; when the tree died He gave it life again by making use of it.
* The Shaykh: That is his statement.
* Student: Since the Glorified and Exalted made the green tree, which is the opposite of fire (that is, it does not ignite), He is able to give life.
* The Shaykh: Yes. There is a well-known tree in the Hijaz: when you strike it with a flint like this, it ignites into fire. So fire comes out of its opposite. The One who brings the opposite out of its opposite is able to give life to the dead. The green tree contains moisture and coolness, while fire contains dryness and heat. He brings out this hot, dry substance from a moist, cool substance, and this is part of complete power.

His saying ﴿then you kindle from it﴾ is for emphasis: emphasis that it came out and you kindled it.

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:81]. What is the indication?
* Student: That the One who created the heavens and the earth is able to restore the life...
* The Shaykh: Is He able to restore life, or to give life to the dead?
* Student: To give life to the dead.
* The Shaykh: Good, and what is the indication?
* Student: Likewise, since He created the heavens and the earth in their greatness, creating man is easier, or restoring him.
* The Shaykh: Well done. Because the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people, and whoever is able to do the greater is able to do what is less.

﴿And He is the Creator, the Knowing﴾.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Good. If He is the Creator, the Knowing, then He is able to create everything, including the restoration of the dead. This is a fifth proof.

﴿His command is only when He wills a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:82]. What is the indication?
* Student: That ﴿shay'an﴾ (a thing) is indefinite in a conditional context, so it encompasses everything.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it encompasses everything, even the giving of life to the dead.

﴿that He says to it "Be," and it is﴾ needs no helpers and no hesitation.

﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:83]. What is the indication from this sentence?
* Student: ﴿Kull shay'in﴾ is indefinite in a negative context, so His hand holds the dominion.
* The Shaykh: It is not a negation.
* Student: From the generality of (kull), since if He owns everything, resurrection falls within the generality.
* Another student: Another aspect: ﴿Exalted is He﴾ is the declaration of Allah's transcendence above deficiencies, among them incapacity to give life.
* The Shaykh: Good, these are two aspects.
* Student: A third aspect: since Allah, exalted is He, owns everything, He is the Creator of everything, and the creator of a thing owns it.
* The Shaykh: The generality.

﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾. This is the eighth.
* Student: The indication in it is that they claim that they die and perish, as they see (...). Allah, the Glorified, affirmed that they will return to Him, and they do not return except by restoration, which is giving life.
* The Shaykh: We want something clearer than this.
* Student: Because it is not possible to return unless (...).
* The Shaykh: Good, and besides this, the wording differs.
* Student: He will return them, the One who created them.
* The Shaykh: How does the One who created them return them?
* Student: The One able to return them is able to give them life.
* The Shaykh: "The One able to return them," this is not correct, it does not hold. We say: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾. Were it not for this return, creation would be purposeless. Since our existence necessarily ends with our return to Allah, there must be giving of life; otherwise all life would be purposeless.

Observe Allah's affirmation of giving life after death, because action is built upon it. If anyone did not believe in the Day of Reckoning, he would not act. For what would he act? As long as there is only this worldly life, we die and live, so for what do we act? Hence a person works for this world: he plunders, steals, commits adultery, drinks wine, and does everything, because there is nothing beyond this world. It is impossible for us to be upright except by faith in the Last Day. For this reason you find Allah, exalted is He, pairing faith in the Last Day with faith in Him in many places, perhaps more often than faith in Him and His messengers, because faith in the Last Day is the foundation on which action rests. Had we not believed that our deeds lie before us on the Day of Resurrection, we would not strive for righteous action, because otherwise it would go to waste. Therefore faith in the Last Day is among the greatest motivations for uprightness. As for one who does not believe in Allah, may Allah protect us, nor in resurrection, his whole deed will be scattered dust.

Good. We have reached His saying: ﴿Have you not considered those who dispute﴾.
* Student: Does Allah, exalted is He, say to a thing "Be" — is this word (...)?
* The Shaykh: Is this among the unseen matters or the perceptible matters?
* Student: Unseen.
* The Shaykh: Good, is it among the matters known by revelation (sam'iyyah) or by reason ('aqliyyah)?
* Student: By revelation.
* The Shaykh: Then we stop at what revelation has brought: ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾ Allah knows best.
* Student: Shaykh, some of those who hold beliefs about the shaykhs, and so on, say that the shaykh benefits and harms, but by the permission of Allah. We want a decisive refutation of them, because this matter has become confused. They say: they benefit and harm, but by the permission of Allah and by the will of Allah?
* The Shaykh: We say: where is the evidence that Allah has permitted them?
* Student: They say: the evidence is the senses.
* The Shaykh: What is the sense?
* Student: The frequent occurrence of this thing.
* The Shaykh: Good. The frequent occurrence of this thing: either it is something every person perceives, in which case the shaykhs have no distinction, as with supplication: one supplicates and Allah responds. Or it is something a person does not perceive, in which case it is from the devils. The devils serve these shaykhs, because they lead people astray from the path of Allah, and the devil wants of us only that he sow enmity and hatred among us and bar us from the remembrance of Allah. So we say this. Otherwise, there is no doubt that they deceive the common people. They say: "Come, I will turn your donkey into a horse," then they supplicate Allah openly, while the devil changes this donkey into a horse by illusion. Otherwise, in reality, whoever goes a little way will find the horse has become a donkey again. It is a kind of sorcery and a kind of deception, and they consume people's wealth falsely.

I heard from some quarters in Africa that the shaykhs say: "The obligation has been lifted from us; there is no need to fast, pray, or pay zakat, and all the prohibitions have been lifted from us." For this reason one of them is like a billy goat, marrying fifty women or more by a marriage contract of what?
* Student: Invalid.
* The Shaykh: No, it is valid in his view. He is a saint from whom the obligations have been lifted, and he says: these obligations are only means to reach the goal; once one reaches the goal, the obligations are void. It is like a man preparing for a journey who rides a car, or takes the stick of a camel, and when he arrives in the town throws it away. We ask Allah for well-being. And the devils serve him.

Shaykh al-Islam even mentioned that some people say: "I saw you at 'Arafat, you, O Ibn Taymiyyah," while he was in Syria and had not performed the Hajj. He said: "That was a devil taking my form, claiming to be Ibn Taymiyyah, and saying to whoever wants: this is lawful, and this is unlawful." Yes indeed.
* Student: "Al-Khallaq" is one of the names of Allah.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: And "al-Khaliq"?
* The Shaykh: And "al-Khaliq" is one of the names of Allah, like "al-Ghafur," "Ghafir al-dhanb," and "al-Ghaffar."
* Student: (...) Those who say: "Glory be to Him who commanded between the kaf and the nun"?
* The Shaykh: This is not correct. "From whose command after the kaf and the nun," that is, "Kun." Does it come after the kaf and the nun, or between them? After the kaf and the nun. That is, "amr" here means "ma'mur" (the thing commanded). If the command is His act, that is, His command, it is before the kaf and the nun; and if the command is the thing commanded, it is after the kaf and the nun.
* Student: Permissible?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not permissible. Permissible, and yet it is not correct?
* Student: After?
* The Shaykh: Yes, after. Or you say: "As for His command with the kaf and the nun," or do not say all these...
* * *

*Student:* I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, how they are turned away? Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers, they will soon know. When the shackles and chains are around their necks, they will be dragged through scalding water, and then they will be burned in the Fire. Then it will be said to them, "Where is what you used to associate with Allah?" They will say, "They have abandoned us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray. That is because you used to exult in the land without right and because you used to be insolent. Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant. So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.﹀ [Ghafir 69–77].

*Shaykh:* I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. We begin our study in the summer sessions of this year 1416 AH, on this day, Saturday, the tenth of the month of Safar of this year. We ask Allah, may He be exalted, to grant us and you success in beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

I say to you: knowledge requires hardship, perseverance, and diligence. Whenever a person trains himself in this, it becomes habitual and becomes an easy matter for him. But if he inclines to laziness, ease, and inactivity, it becomes extremely difficult for him to be diligent, because the soul becomes accustomed to what it has been trained in. A person seeking knowledge is like the one striving in the way of Allah (jihad) in preparing his equipment, because Allah, may He be exalted, made striving in the way of Allah and knowledge equal, when He said: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together.﴾ That is, it is not possible for them all to go out to fight. ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may be cautious?﴾ That is, a group remains behind. ﴿That they may gain understanding of the religion﴾: the subject of "they may gain understanding" is the remaining group. ﴿That they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may be cautious﴾ [al-Tawbah 122].

Indeed, some scholars said that seeking knowledge is more emphatic than striving in the way of Allah, because striving is built upon knowledge, while knowledge is not built upon striving. Rather, the striver cannot strive in the correct manner except by seeking knowledge. Therefore it is more emphatic.

So a person's continued study, review, repetition, and memorization of Islamic knowledge is exactly like the striver in the way of Allah, equal in every respect.

If we were asked: which is better, striving in the way of Allah or seeking knowledge? We would say: we cannot prefer one over the other absolutely. Some people, we tell them: seeking knowledge is better for you. And some people, we tell them: striving is better for you. This is why you find that the answers of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, regarding the ranking of deeds, show that he addressed each person according to his condition.

By this, the difficulty that comes to mind is resolved, since the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, says in some hadiths: "The best deeds are such-and-such," and in others: "The best deeds are such-and-such." It is said that this difference is according to the condition of the one being addressed.

We say: for some people, seeking knowledge is better in their case, and for some people, striving is better in their case. Whoever is a vessel of knowledge, a memorizer, understanding, and diligent in knowledge, then seeking knowledge is better for him, because it produces more.

In the ranking of deeds, each person is addressed according to what his condition requires. By this, the difficulty that arises in the mind is resolved, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says in some hadiths: "The best deeds are such-and-such," and in others: "The best deeds are such-and-such." It is said that this difference is according to the condition of the one addressed.

We say: for some people, seeking knowledge is better in their case, and for some people, striving is better in their case. Whoever is a vessel of knowledge, a great memorizer, understanding, and diligent in knowledge, then seeking knowledge is better for him, because it produces more and benefits the Muslims more.

As for whoever is in other than this condition, with little memorization and little understanding, but who is courageous, strong, and brave, then striving is better for him. "And for each there are degrees according to what they have done."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verse 69–72:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir 69].

﴿Have you not considered﴾: this interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), because when the interrogative hamza enters a negation, it becomes an affirmation of it. So the meaning of ﴿Have you not considered﴾ is: have you seen. The address is either to the Messenger (ﷺ) or to everyone who is suitable to be addressed, and this kind of address occurs frequently in the Qur'an.

We have already explained that the address directed to the Messenger (ﷺ), or that which apparently is directed to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), is divided into three categories:

The first category: that which is definitely specific to him.

The second category: that which is definitely general to him and to the Ummah.

The third category: that in which neither of these is clear.

As for the first, which is definitely specific to the Messenger, it is specific to him, and there is no difficulty in this, such as the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden﴾ [al-Sharh 1, 2], and ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And He found you lost and guided you﴾ [al-Duha 6, 7], and what is similar to them. To whom is the address here? It is to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) specifically, and it does not include the Ummah.

As for that which is definitely for him and for others, such as the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them﴾ [al-Talaq 1]. He did not say, "When you divorce women," so this indicates that the address specific to him is for him and for the Ummah; because He addressed him first with the vocative, then directed the address to the Ummah in general, saying: ﴿when you (plural) divorce﴾. This indicates that the address specific to him with the vocative is not specific to him but is for him and for the Ummah.

That which is not like this, meaning: that which is neither this nor that, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have differed concerning it: is it an address specific to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) that does not include the Ummah except by way of ruling through emulation of him, or is it general to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and others, with the address being to whoever is suitable to be addressed?

The difference regarding such a matter is almost verbal, because all agree that this ruling is established for the Messenger and for others. But if we say it is specific to him, then with respect to others it becomes general by way of emulation and exemplary following. However, the ruling does not actually differ, because if it does not include the Ummah verbally, it includes them in ruling, due to the command to emulate him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

So here, ﴿Have you not considered those who dispute﴾ [Ghafir 69]: which of the three categories is it? This is something that admits of possibility: that it is specific to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), or general to everyone to whom the address is directed.

﴿Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾. The author said: (the Qur'an). This explanation is considered deficient, because the signs of Allah are greater than being cosmic or legislative, and greater than being in the Qur'an or the Torah or the Gospel or other books sent down to the messengers.

So the correct statement is: in the cosmic and legislative signs of Allah, and the most fitting of what is included in them is the Qur'an.

Disputation (mujadalah) is contending with an opponent in order to turn him away from what he is upon of opposition, derived from jadl, which is twisting a rope until it becomes firm and strong. Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah: whom do they dispute? They dispute the messengers and their followers. The disputation between the messengers and their followers has existed since the messengers were sent until our present day. Do not be surprised that there exist those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in this time, because this is the way (sunnah) of Allah the Mighty and Majestic since He sent the messengers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾ [al-Furqan 31]. Every prophet has an enemy from among the criminals, and if he has an enemy from among the criminals, this enemy must dispute, and consequently must fight with swords.

Disputation concerning the cosmic signs of Allah: that one denies that Allah is the Creator. This has indeed occurred; there are those who attribute what happens in the universe to natural matters without there being a manager for them, and say: this is a nature that interacts and from which what is observed results.

There are also those who dispute concerning the cosmic signs of Allah with matters beneath that; such as affirming a cause that Allah did not make a cause, as happens among the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) with pessimism regarding birds, places, and times, and what is similar to that. For example, they are pessimistic about times, such as the month of Safar; they say: this month is a month of evil, which they regard as an omen.

They are also pessimistic about birds: about the type of bird, or the manner of its flying, or its direction, or what is similar to that.

They are also pessimistic about persons: a person sees a man and, the first time he sees him, is pessimistic about him. This appears to have existed even until our era: some people in a certain region of the Kingdom, when one of them comes to open his shop and then meets a person of ugly appearance, for example, he says: that's it, today is ill-omened, there will be no sale or purchase. This is pessimism regarding persons, and this too is among the disputation concerning the cosmic signs of Allah.

As for disputation concerning the legislative signs of Allah, speak of it without restraint: they deny the legislative signs of Allah, reject them, dispute some matters in them, saying: there is contradiction in them, and such and such, and the kinds of disputation are many.

He says: (﴿How﴾ in what way ﴿are they turned away﴾ from faith). That is, this is as if it were an interrogative of wonder and denunciation: how are they turned away from faith when it is clear and manifest, yet they are turned away from it and dispute concerning it?!

Then He said: ﴿Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir 70]. This is a substitute for His saying: ﴿those who dispute﴾, or an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan). The difference between them: the explicative apposition resembles a qualifier in clarifying the substituted noun, whereas a substitute may be a mere substitute devoid of qualification. For example, if you say: "Zayd came, your brother," "your brother" here is a substitute, and we have not gained much from it. But when an explicative apposition comes, as in this verse: ﴿those who denied the Book﴾, we have gained a meaning that is closer to a qualifier than to substitution, and therefore they call it explicative apposition.

﴿Those who denied the Book﴾: that is, they said it is a lie. And "the Book" here is preceded by the article (al), as you know. Is it for a specific known (ʿahd), for totality (istighraq), or for the genus (jins)? The closest thing is that it is for the genus, and the author made it for the specific known, so he said: (the Qur'an). There is no doubt that it is not permissible to deviate from the genus or the clarification of reality, except with evidence, so pay attention.

So what is the original usage of (al): is it for clarifying the reality, or for clarifying the genus, or for the specific known? Yes, for clarifying the genus, because clarifying the genus means totality, and this is the original. If you make it for the specific known, you have shifted its general meaning to a particular meaning, and likewise if you make it for the reality. We will give three examples so the matter becomes clear:

If you say: "The man is better than the woman," is it for generality? No, because among women there are some better than men. So this is for clarifying the reality.

If someone raises against you: ﴿Man was created weak﴾ [al-Nisa 28]: for what is this? For the genus, meaning totality: meaning every human being was created weak. If someone raises against you the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger (15). But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil 15, 16]: this is for the mentioned specific known (ʿahd dhikri).

﴿O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord﴾ [al-Nisa 170]: this too is for the mental specific known (ʿahd dhihni).

Here the author, may Allah have mercy on him, took His saying: ﴿the Book﴾ to be the mental specific known, and said it is the Qur'an. The correct view is that it is general, and that what is meant is the genus of the Book; because the Torah was denied by some people, the Gospel was denied by some people, and likewise the Psalms, and the rest of the books, the last of which is the Qur'an.

(﴿And that with which We sent Our messengers﴾ of monotheism and resurrection, and they are the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿but they will come to know﴾).

﴿And that with which We sent Our messengers﴾: its coordination with His saying ﴿the Book﴾ is by repeating the governing element (ʿamil), because coordination (ʿatf) may occur with repetition of the governing element and without it. You say: "I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr" — this is coordination without repetition of the governing element. "I passed by Zayd and by ʿAmr" — this is coordination with repetition of the governing element. Repetition of the governing element indicates that the coordinated item is independent of what it is coordinated with, because it is not a follower of it in every respect, as evidenced by repeating the governing element. So His saying: ﴿and that with which We sent Our messengers﴾ indicates that what the messengers were sent with is as if independent of the Book; for this reason the Sunnah is in the position of the Book in indicating and the obligation of acting upon it.

﴿And that with which We sent Our messengers﴾: the author said: (of monotheism and resurrection, and they are the disbelievers of Makkah). Monotheism means the oneness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in what He deserves of names and attributes, worship, and lordship. As for resurrection, it is the bringing forth of people from their graves on the Day of Resurrection.

The closest thing is that it is for the genus, and the author made it for the specific known, so he said: (the Qur'an). If you make it for the specific known, you have shifted its general meaning to a particular meaning, and likewise if you make it for the reality. If someone raises against you the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger (15). As for resurrection, it is the bringing forth of people from their graves on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: (﴿in the boiling water﴾, meaning Jahannam), and it is described as such because it is extremely hot.

(﴿Then in the Fire they will be burned﴾, kindled), because the fuel of the Fire is people and stones.

The third category: that in which neither of these is clear.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 40, verse 73–76 (part 1 of 3):

(“Then it will be said to them” [Ghafir 73] as a rebuke, “Where are those you used to associate” (73) “besides Allah” with Him, namely the idols.) The interrogative here is, without doubt, for reproach, censure and reducing them to helplessness; all of these are contained in this question. And this is a pain in the heart, because a person feels the utmost regret when the idols he used to worship, which he claimed would bring him closer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, now have gone astray from him and are nowhere to be found. It is like if you were to seize a slave, for example, and torture him, and say: "Where is your master whom you claim will protect you?" Would this not be more painful regret for him? Yes. So these people are made to feel this regret, and it is said: “Where are those you used to associate” (73) “besides Allah”, that is, with Allah, the idols. At that point they will grieve with a grief beyond which there is no grief.

For this reason they say, in an acknowledgment forced upon them in reality: (“They say: They have gone astray from us”, that is, they have vanished, “so we do not see them”.)

So they know that these will not benefit them, and that they have vanished from them at the time they most need them. Rather, they say: “Nay, we used not to call upon anything before.” Glory be to Allah! That is, they deny that they ever associated partners, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: “Then their trial will be only that they will say, ‘By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.’ Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to invent has gone astray from them.” [al-An'am 23, 24]. The upshot is that they feel this great regret, and then they deny it.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: “Nay, we used not to call upon anything before.” “Call upon” (nadʿū) means worship (naʿbud), because supplication (duʿa') is divided into two kinds: supplication of request (duʿa' al-masʾalah) and supplication of worship (duʿa' al-ʿibadah), and both are inseparable. Supplication of request is worship, as in the hadith: “Supplication is worship”[[Abu Dawud (1479) narrated it with his chain from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Supplication is worship…” the hadith.]], and supplication of worship is also supplication of request, because if you asked the worshipper: “Why do you worship Allah?” he would say: “Hoping for His reward and fearing His punishment.” So he is calling upon Him by the tongue of his state. That is why supplication came to mean worship and worship came to mean supplication. Observe this in His saying: “And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated.” [Ghafir 60]. But supplication of request is explicit supplication in asking, as the one who says: “My Lord, forgive me and have mercy on me,” and so on. Supplication of worship is supplication by implication, because a person worships Allah only out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward.

Is supplication of request explicit worship or implicit worship? It is implicit worship, because the one who asks is humbled before the one he asks, so he is worshipping him.

He said: (“Nay, we used not to call upon anything before” — they denied their worship of them. Then they were brought forward, and Allah the Exalted said: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell” [al-Anbiya' 98], that is, its firewood.) The complete verse is: “You will be entering it. Had these been gods, they would not have entered it, and all of them will abide therein.” [al-Anbiya' 98, 99]. So these denied, they lied against themselves, thinking that this would benefit them, just as a criminal in this world who denies his crime may be helped by it; but in the Hereafter it does not benefit. Indeed, when they deny, a seal is placed upon their mouths, and the hands, feet, skins and tongues speak of what they did, and at that point they have no device and find no way.

* Among the benefits of this verse: these who denied the Book and what Allah sent with His messengers are punished with a physical punishment, with chains, shackles and dragging in the Fire, and they are punished with a punishment of the heart through rebuke, reproach and censure, so it is said: “Where are those you used to associate” (73) “besides Allah” [Ghafir 73, 74].

* Among the benefits of this verse: affirming that speech belongs to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Can this be taken from the verse?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The verse does not indicate this, because the speaker is not specified in “It will be said to them”; but in other verses it is shown that Allah says it to them: “And on the Day He calls to them, He will say: Where are My partners whom you used to claim?” [al-Qasas 62].

Who is calling them? Allah, because He said: “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?” It may be said that they are called by Allah and also called by the angels whom Allah has assigned, or it may be said that the angels call them, but their calling is attributed to Allah because He is the one who commands it, just as Allah attributed the taking of souls to Himself, although the one who directly takes souls is the messengers. But we say: these possibilities we do not raise when the apparent meaning is present, because speech is to be taken as what? As its apparent meaning, until there is evidence that diverts it from the apparent. So when Allah says: “On the Day He calls to them, He will say: Where are My partners whom you used to claim?” [al-Qasas 62], it is explicit that the caller is Allah, so it stays as it is, and what is in the passive form is understood as the caller being Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* A student: “And the chains, they will be dragged” [Ghafir 71] — there is no returning pronoun, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: There is no returning pronoun? We have mentioned the returning pronoun; we said it is omitted, and the estimate is: “they will be dragged with them.” Omitting the returning pronoun is permitted; whatever is known may be omitted.

* A student: You explained the interrogative as an interrogative of affirmation.

* The Shaykh: Which one?

* The student: “Have you not seen” [alam tara].

* The Shaykh: “Have you not seen”, yes.

* The student: Then you said among its benefits is amazement?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed; because of His saying: “How are they turned away?” [anna yusrafun].

* The student: Amazement does not contain an interrogative.

* The Shaykh: No, from “how are they turned away” there is an interrogative.

* * *

* The student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. “Then it will be said to them: Where are those you used to associate (73) besides Allah? They will say: They have gone astray from us; rather, we did not used to call upon anything before. Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers (74). That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent (75). Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein; and wretched is the abode of the arrogant.” [Ghafir 73–76].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: “Then it will be said to them: Where are those you used to associate (73) besides Allah?” Who is the speaker?

* A student: The speaker is Allah.

* The Shaykh: The speaker is Allah. What is the evidence from the Qur'an? “Then He will say: Where are My partners whom you used to claim?” [al-Qasas 62].

Is there another meaning in which the speaker is other than Allah as well?

* A student: Yes, in the same verse there is a possibility, because the subject is omitted; but the other verse establishes it and leaves no possibility.

* The Shaykh: It may also be the angels, meaning the object is omitted..

* A student: It may also be that the speakers are the angels, and it is attributed to Allah the Exalted because He is the one who commands it, just as..

* The Shaykh: The verse the brother mentioned is explicit, but is there not a verse in the Qur'an showing that the angels also rebuke them? If there is, there is no objection; this verse is formed in the passive for this reason. Good.

What is meant by this saying? What is the purpose of it?

* A student: Rebuke.

* The Shaykh: Rebuke and censure, good. So they are punished in two ways together?

* A student: The heart and the senses.

* The Shaykh: The heart and the body, because their censure and blame undoubtedly affect them.

Allah the Exalted says: “Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers” [Ghafir 74]. “Thus” (kadhalika): the kaf is a particle, but in reality it is a noun; it is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), and the sense of the sentence is: "Like that misguidance, Allah leads the disbelievers astray." It is a particle in form, but a noun in meaning; its place in grammatical analysis is an absolute object of the verb that follows it.

As you know, this kind of expression occurs often in the Qur'an, and its analysis, as you have heard, is that the kaf is a particle meaning "like," and its analysis is an absolute object of the verb after it, and the estimate is according to each context. But in our verse: "Like that misguidance, Allah leads the disbelievers astray."

His saying: “Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray” [Ghafir 74] means: He places them in misguidance.

The commentator says: (“Thus” means: like the misguidance of these deniers, “Allah leads the disbelievers astray”.)

He said: (It is also said to them: “That” — the punishment — “is because you used to exult in the land without right”.) “That” (dhalikum): the indicated thing is the punishment, and the addressees are those disbelievers; for this reason the kaf came with the plural pronoun, and the demonstrative came in the singular masculine, because the punishment is singular masculine.

Know that the demonstrative and the second-person kaf sometimes agree and sometimes differ: the demonstrative follows the thing indicated, and the second-person kaf follows the addressee. If you are told: point to a feminine singular thing while addressing a group of women, how do you say it?

* A student: “Then that is the one about whom you blamed me.” [Yusuf 32].

* The Shaykh: “Then that is the one about whom you blamed me” [Yusuf 32]. Point to a dual masculine while addressing a dual feminine.

* A student: Dhanikuma.

* The Shaykh: Dhanikuma, good. Point to a feminine singular while addressing a group of males?

* A student: Tankum.

* The Shaykh: In the Qur'an: “And that is the Garden which you have been given as inheritance” [al-Zukhruf 72]; the indicated thing is feminine singular, and the addressees are a group of males. The important thing is this rule: the demonstrative follows the thing indicated, and the second-person kaf follows the addressee; they may agree or differ.

His saying: “That is because” — the ba is causal, and "ma" is verbal (masdariyya); the sign of the verbal "ma" is that what follows it can be converted into a verbal noun. For example, in His saying "That is because you used to…", if we convert what follows into a verbal noun, the estimate becomes: "That is by your being those who exult in the land without right."

His saying "because you used to" — it is known that kuntum here is past tense; that is, before death.

"You exult in the land without right": that is, you exult in falsehood, because they exult in shirk and disbelief, and in everyone who shared their sin, they rejoice in him.

His saying "without right" — the commentator said: (from associating partners and denying resurrection). In reality this is deficient unless he intended it as an example; otherwise "without right" is more general than shirk and denial of resurrection. They exult in the land without right: in shirk, denial of resurrection, aggression, making lawful what is forbidden and forbidding what is lawful, such as the sa'iba, the wasila, the ham, and the like.

The point is that the author's saying "from associating partners and denying resurrection" is deficient unless he did not intend it as an example; if he intended an example, then an example does not restrict.

(“And that you used to be insolent” — you used to extend yourselves in exultation.) The waw is a conjunction, the ba is causal, and this clause is coordinated with what precedes it by repeating the governing particle. What is the governing particle? The ba. Coordination by repeating the governing particle means that the second is independent of the first; so they are punished for both matters together: a punishment specific to exultation and a punishment specific to insolence, with the ba indicating causation. ("And that you used to be insolent" — you used to extend yourselves in exultation.)

“Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein” [Ghafir 76]. “Enter” is an imperative verb, and the one commanding is the angels; the command is meant as humiliation, not honor, but a humiliating and binding command, because they must enter.

His saying "gates of Hell" is plural. How many gates are there? The gates of Hell are seven, as Allah the Exalted said: “It has seven gates; for each gate is a portion assigned” [al-Hijr 44]. Jahannam is a name of the Fire, and it was so named because it is of deep gloom (juhma). If we say that jahannam is an Arabic name with a nun added, then there is no need to say it is derived from juhma, which means darkness and depth; and whichever it is, it is a name of the Fire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

“Abiding therein” — “abiding” (khalidin) is a circumstantial state of the subject in His saying "enter". Is this abiding a long stay or eternity? We say: in the Arabic language, khulud is used to mean a long stay, and it is used to mean eternity, and what is meant here is the second; that is, they abide therein forever. The evidence is that Allah explicitly stated in the Noble Qur'an that the people of the Fire abide therein forever in three places:

The first: the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: “Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged — Allah will not forgive them, nor guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever; and that is ever easy for Allah.” [al-Nisa' 168, 169].

The second verse: His saying, exalted: “Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing fire, abiding therein forever.” [al-Ahzab 64, 65].

The third verse: the saying of Allah, exalted: “And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.” [al-Jinn 23].

By these three verses it becomes clear that the view of those who say the Fire is not everlasting and will perish is weak, indeed false, for this view is rejected because it contradicts the explicit Qur'an; and no one who contradicts the explicit Qur'an can do so merely on the basis of rationalizations, such as saying: Allah's mercy preceded His wrath, and that these people will eventually perish, they and the Fire.

It is said: Yes, Allah's mercy preceded His wrath; but Allah's promise is true, is it not? And if Allah's promise is true, then they will be made to abide therein forever.

If someone says: how can eternal abiding in this painful punishment be the recompense for a person who lived in this world only a hundred or a thousand years?

It is said: here the punishment exceeds the time of the deed, because no one remains in this world forever; this implies an injustice, since the recompense has become far more than the deed, and is not proportionate. As I told you, let us suppose that someone lived a thousand years or ten thousand years, but he lived for a term, and then we say: his punishment is everlasting; would this be injustice?

It is said: this person spent his entire worldly life in opposing Allah and His messengers, so he spends his entire other life in punishment, and this is justice. Moreover, this one who is punished forever was told in this world and it was made clear to him that his recompense would be everlasting punishment; so why would he proceed toward something he knows is his recompense? At that point there is no injustice and no excuse for the disbelievers. So the point is that His saying "abiding therein" [Ghafir 76] means everlasting eternity. "Wretched is the abode of the arrogant" [Ghafir 76]: this sentence is an expressive sentence meant to express censure, and its counterpart in praise is "How excellent is the abode of the righteous." "Wretched" (fa-bi'sa) here is an expressive verb meant to express censure, and the meaning is that this abode is entirely censure, entirely calamity; for this reason it is described as "the abode of the arrogant."

* A student: A hadith: “The intention of the disbeliever…”[[We have not found it with this wording. It is narrated with the wording “The intention of the wicked is worse than his deed,” recorded by al-Qada'i in his Musnad (148) from the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, may Allah be pleased with him, and by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (2/256) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.]]..

* The Shaykh: First: this is not an authentic hadith from the Messenger.

Secondly: the meaning of its speaker is that a person can attain by intention what he cannot attain by action. This is the sense. A sick person who wishes he were well and does what Allah has obligated upon him has attained by intention what he did not attain by action. Likewise, if a person intends evil while he is unable to carry it out, he is punished as the doer is punished, but for his intention. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the poor man who had no wealth, and another man who said: "If I had the wealth of so-and-so, I would act with it as so-and-so acts." The Prophet ﷺ said: «He is by his intention, and the two of them are equal in the burden [of sin]»[[Al-Tirmidhi (2325) and Ibn Majah (4228), with the wording being Ibn Majah's, both by their chains from Abu Kabshah al-Anmari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The likeness of this Ummah is like the likeness of four men. A man whom Allah gave wealth and knowledge; he acts by his knowledge in his wealth, spending it in its right. And a man whom Allah gave knowledge but not wealth, so he says: 'If I had like this, I would do what he does.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Those two are equal in reward. And a man whom Allah gave wealth but not knowledge, so he wallows in his wealth, spending it in other than its right. And a man whom Allah gave neither knowledge nor wealth, so he says: "If I had like this, I would do what he does." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Those two are equal in burden."»]].

* The student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We have restricted the gates of Hellfire to seven based on this verse, yet it has passed with us regarding the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: «Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names»; and likewise regarding the eight gates of Paradise, we said that it does not indicate restriction. What is the basis for restriction in this verse?
* The Shaykh: This one asks, saying: You stated that the number has no implication (mafhum) in the Prophet's ﷺ saying: «Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise»[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (2736) and Muslim (2677/5), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. You said that this number does not indicate restriction, and that Allah has other names. So why do we say there is restriction, or that the number indicates restriction, in the gates of Hellfire and the gates of Paradise?
The answer: We say, as for the first, which is His saying: «Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names», we only said that it is not restrictive, based on evidence. What is the evidence? The hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, the hadith of distress, in which he said: «I ask You by every name that is Yours, by which You named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You»[[Narrated by Ahmad (4318) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. And if Allah has kept the knowledge of the unseen to Himself, then it is impossible for a person to comprehend it, because Allah has kept it to Himself. Therefore we said: the number has no implication in His saying «Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names», and that the meaning is: Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
* The student: We said that the claim that the Fire is not eternal contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an. If this speaker says: This is a threat (wa'id), and breaking a threat is permissible?
* The Shaykh: We say: This is not possible, because we do not say that breaking a threat is permissible except in a matter of necessity that cannot be avoided, such as: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah will be angry with him﴾ [An-Nisa' 93]. These are some of the answers given to this verse: that this is a threat, and breaking a threat is generosity and is praise for the one who breaks it. But this answer, in reality, is a shaky answer, not a firm one. Because we say: Allah does not break His promise, that is, what He promised of punishment or honor. As for the verse ﴿abiding therein﴾ in the verse of killing, the word "abiding" is taken in the second meaning, which is a long stay, and with this there is no contradiction.
* The student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And whether We show you part of that which We promise them or cause you to die, then to Us they will be returned. (77) And We have already sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth, and the falsifiers will lose at that time. (78) It is Allah who made for you the grazing livestock that you may ride some of them and eat from them. (79) And for you therein are [other] benefits, and that you may reach by them a need within your breasts; and upon them and upon the ship you are carried. (80) And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ [Ghafir 77–81].
* The Shaykh: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.
The saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, regarding the people of the Fire, who will be told: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell﴾ [Ghafir 76]. What is the intended meaning of this command?
* A student: It means the command to enter the Fire, that is, Allah's command to it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what is meant by it?
* The student: It means the Day of Resurrection, and humiliation.
* The Shaykh: Humiliation?! And His saying, exalted is He, regarding the people of Paradise: ﴿Enter it in peace, secure﴾ [Al-Hijr 46]. What is the intended meaning of the command there?
* The student: (...).
Honor, good. From this we derive that words differ in meaning according to context, and this is a great benefit for the student of knowledge: that words differ in meaning according to context. How many a word has one meaning in one context and another meaning in a different context.
Do the people of the Fire abide in it forever?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, forever. Do you have evidence for this?
* The student: It is mentioned in three verses that indicate permanence.
* The Shaykh: Well done. Recite one of them to us.
* A student: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever; they will not find any protector or helper﴾ [Al-Ahzab 64–65].
* The Shaykh: Well done, this is in Surat al-Ahzab.
* The student: The second: ﴿except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾.
* The Shaykh: And the second is ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah would not forgive them nor guide them to any path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [An-Nisa' 168–169]. In which surah is this?
* The student: This is in Surat an-Nisa'.
* The student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [Al-Jinn 23].
* The Shaykh: In which surah is this?
* The student: Al-Jinn.
* The Shaykh: In Surat al-Jinn, well done.
Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Ghafir 77]. (Be patient): the address here is to the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family.
The saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray the disbelievers﴾ [Ghafir 74].
* From it is derived: that Allah, exalted is He, leads the disbeliever astray because of his disbelief. The proof of this is that when a ruling is linked to an attribute, that attribute is its cause. Here, what is linked to disbelief is being led astray. Therefore, disbelief is a cause of being led astray. This is confirmed by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [As-Saff 5].
From this it follows that the one who is led astray, when he goes astray, is himself the cause of his going astray, because if Allah, exalted is He, had known any good in him, He would have made him hear. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [Al-An'am 124]. This verse means that Allah knows best where the message will be in a particular person, and likewise where the effect of the message will be in a particular person, and the effect of the message is guidance.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the Qadariyyah: ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray the disbelievers﴾. What is the basis of this?
* A student: Because this one who is led astray is the cause of his own misguidance, so he has a will that establishes this for him.
* The Shaykh: They say this, the Qadariyyah affirm that man has an independent will.
* A student: The Qadariyyah say that the actions of the servants are not created by Allah, glorified and exalted is He.
* The Shaykh: And Allah has no connection with them.
* The student: But the verse indicates that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the one who leads them astray.
* The Shaykh: Yes, so this is a refutation of the Qadariyyah.
It is fitting on this occasion, although this lesson is not a lesson in creed, to say: People have divided on this matter into two extremes and a middle, regarding the actions of servants:
Some of them say: the actions of servants are created by Allah, and the servant is compelled (majbur) to them, and he has no will, because Allah is the Creator of everything, and if Allah is the Creator, then man has no management.
Others said the opposite: man is the doer by his own choice, and Allah has no connection to it. These are two extremes.
And some said: man is the doer by his own choice, but his action is linked to the will of Allah. This is the middle position.
Know that the causes of error in such matters is that some people look at the texts from one angle only; that is, they take one text and leave another. The Jabriyyah (Determinists) saw the generality of Allah's will and the generality of Allah's creation, and that man is needy of Allah, and similar things, so they said: Then man has no will and no choice, and his act is by compulsion.
And the Qadariyyah saw that man acts and does not feel that anyone compels him, and Allah attributed the act to him, saying: ﴿They establish prayer and give zakah﴾ [Al-Hajj 41]. So he is independent in his deed, and Allah has no connection to it. They took from one side and left another side. And likewise with all scholarly disagreements: when you see scholars disagreeing into two extremes and a middle, know that each of the two extremes took one side of the evidence and left another side.
Then He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿That is because you used to exult in the earth without right﴾ [Ghafir 75], to the end.
* In this noble verse: the affirmation of causes is derived from His saying: ﴿That is because you used to exult﴾, since the "ba'" here indicates causation.
Know also that people have differed regarding causes in three positions: two extremes and a middle.
One group of people affirmed causes and that they act by themselves; meaning that when the cause exists, the effect necessarily exists.
Another group denied the influence of causes and said: causes do not have influence, because if you made this dependent on a cause, you would have affirmed a partner with Allah in creating, and this is shirk. So here there are two extremes:
One extreme affirms causes, and that they are influential in themselves, meaning that whenever the cause exists, the effect necessarily exists; the cause is influential in its essence.
And another group says: causes have no influence, because if you gave causes influence, you would have associated with Allah by making a creator besides Allah, mighty and majestic.
